33: ### Shared-file and prerequisite notes
34: 
35: - `src/lib.rs` registers the eleven new modules and root re-exports. No Cargo feature or dependency was added.
36: - Existing M01–M05 types are reused unchanged: `Point`/`Vector` (`Add/Sub/Mul`, dot/cross/length), `Rect` (`bounds_or_empty`, `center_x`, `center_y`), `IRect`, `Matrix` (`set_sin_cos`, `pre_scale`, `post_concat`, `map_points_in_place`, `map_homogeneous_points`, `has_perspective`), `Point3`, `PointPriv`, and the `floating_point`/`scalar` helper families. No earlier behavior was modified.
37: - Two path-owned declarations are introduced early because M06 public signatures consume them: `SkPathDirection` (`Cw`/`Ccw`, in `src/sk_geometry.rs`) and `SkPathVerb` (in `src/sk_edge_clipper.rs`). M07 adopts both unchanged; `SkPathVerb` already uses the reference discriminants.
38: - `skvx::float2`/`float4` arithmetic is replaced by scalar `Point`/`[Scalar; 4]` operations. Every site keeps the reference expression order, including the two-lane cubic chop and the four-lane midtangent coefficient accumulation; `skvx::fma` maps to `f32::mul_add`, `std::fma` to `f64::mul_add`.
39: - The `SkConic` public fields remain `pts: [Point; 3]` and `w: Scalar` with the `set_w` guard (`w > 0 && finite`, else 1), so caller-visible layout/order matches the reference value semantics.
40: - `SkAutoConicToQuads` owns a `Vec<Point>` instead of `AutoSTMalloc`; `compute_quads` returns a borrowed slice into that storage and `count_quads` reports the quad count.

33:     return (static_cast<int>(ft) & 2) != 0;

20:     kConvex_Degenerate,  // known to not have a determinable direction, but convex

22:     kConcave,

32: static inline bool SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(SkPathConvexity cv) {
33:     return cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW
34:         || cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW
35:         || cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate;
36: }
37: 
38: static inline SkPathConvexity SkPathConvexity_OppositeConvexDirection(SkPathConvexity cv) {
39:     SkASSERT(SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(cv));
40:     switch (cv) {
41:         case SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW:  cv = SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW; break;
42:         case SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW: cv = SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW;  break;
43:         default: break;
44:     }
45:     return cv;
46: }

50:     kCCW,        // == SkPathDirection::kCCW

57:         case SkPathDirection::kCCW: return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW;

65:         case SkPathFirstDirection::kCCW:     return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW;
66:         case SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown: return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate;

66:  *  Path's can also identify as a "rect" -- but we don't store any special tag for this.
67:  *
68:  *  Here are the special "types" we have APIs for (e.g. isRRect()) and what we store:
69:  *
70:  *      kGeneral  : no identifying shape, no extra data
71:  *      (Rect)    : no tag, but isRect() will examing the points/verbs, and try to
72:  *                  deduce that it represents a rect.
73:  *      kOval     : the path bounds is also the oval's bounds -- we store the direction
74:  *                  and start_index (important for dashing). see SkPathMakers.h
75:  *      kRRect    : same as kOval for implicit bounds, direction and start_index.
76:  *                  Note: we don't store its radii -- we deduce those when isRRect() is
77:  *                        called, by examining the points/verbs.
78:  */
79: enum class SkPathIsAType : uint8_t {
80:     kGeneral,
81:     kOval,
82:     kRRect,
83: };
84: 
85: struct SkPathIsAData {
86:     uint8_t         fStartIndex;
87:     SkPathDirection fDirection;
88: };

10: /*
11:  *  Close is funny -- it has no explicit point data, but we return 2 points,
12:  *  the logical 2 points that would make up the line connecting the end of
13:  *  the contour, and its beginning.
14:  *
15:  *  To do this, we have local storage (fClosePointStorage)
16:  */
17: std::optional<SkPathIter::Rec> SkPathIter::next() {
18:     if (vIndex >= fVerbs.size()) {
19:         return {};
20:     }
21: 
22:     size_t n = 0;
23: 
24:     float w = -1;
25:     SkPathVerb v;
26:     switch (v = fVerbs[vIndex++]) {
27:         case SkPathVerb::kMove:
28:             fClosePointStorage[1] = fPoints[pIndex++]; // remember for close
29:             return Rec{{&fClosePointStorage[1], 1}, w, v};
30:         case SkPathVerb::kLine:  n = 1; break;
31:         case SkPathVerb::kQuad:  n = 2; break;
32:         case SkPathVerb::kConic: n = 2; w = fConics[cIndex++]; break;
33:         case SkPathVerb::kCubic: n = 3; break;
34:         case SkPathVerb::kClose:
35:             SkASSERT(pIndex > 0);
36:             fClosePointStorage[0] = fPoints[pIndex-1];   // the last point we saw
37:             return Rec{fClosePointStorage, w, v};
38:     }
39: 
40:     SkASSERT(pIndex > 0);
41:     auto start = pIndex - 1;
42:     SkASSERT(n >= 1 && n <= 3);
43:     pIndex += n;
44:     return Rec{{&fPoints[start], n+1}, w, v};
45: 
46: }
47:

50: std::optional<SkPathContourIter::Rec> SkPathContourIter::next() {
51:     if (fVerbs.empty()) {
52:         return {};
53:     }
54: 
55:     SkASSERT(fVerbs[0] == SkPathVerb::kMove);
56:     size_t npts = 1, nvbs = 1, nws = 0;
57: 
58:     for (size_t i = 1; i < fVerbs.size(); ++i) {
59:         switch (fVerbs[i]) {
60:             case SkPathVerb::kMove: goto DONE;
61:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:  npts += 1; break;
62:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:  npts += 2; break;
63:             case SkPathVerb::kConic: npts += 2; nws += 1; break;
64:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic: npts += 3; break;
65:             case SkPathVerb::kClose: nvbs += 1; goto DONE;
66:         }
67:         nvbs += 1;
68:     }
69: DONE:
70:     Rec rec = {
71:         fPoints.subspan(0, npts),
72:         fVerbs.subspan(0, nvbs),
73:         fConics.subspan(0, nws),
74:     };
75:     fPoints = fPoints.last(fPoints.size() - npts);
76:     fVerbs  = fVerbs.last( fVerbs.size()  - nvbs);
77:     fConics = fConics.last(fConics.size() - nws);
78:     return rec;
79: }

119: static void check_iter(skiatest::Reporter* reporter, const SkPathRaw& raw,
120:                        SkSpan<SkPoint> pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs, SkSpan<const float> cns) {
121:     size_t pIndex = 0, vIndex = 0, cIndex = 0;
122:     size_t moveToIndex = 0; // track the start of each contour
123: 
124:     auto iter = raw.iter();
125:     while (auto r = iter.next()) {
126:         REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, vIndex < vbs.size());
127:         REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, vbs[vIndex++] == r->fVerb);
128:         switch (r->fVerb) {
129:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:
130:                 moveToIndex = pIndex;
131:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pIndex < pts.size());
132:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[0]);
133:                 break;
134:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:
135:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pIndex < pts.size());
136:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex-1] == r->fPoints[0]);
137:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[1]);
138:                 break;
139:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
140:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pIndex+1 < pts.size());
141:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex-1] == r->fPoints[0]);
142:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[1]);
143:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[2]);
144:                 break;
145:             case SkPathVerb::kConic:
146:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pIndex+1 < pts.size());
147:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex-1] == r->fPoints[0]);
148:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[1]);
149:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[2]);
150:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, cIndex < cns.size());
151:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, cns[cIndex++] == r->fConicWeight);
152:                 break;
153:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
154:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pIndex+2 < pts.size());
155:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex-1] == r->fPoints[0]);
156:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[1]);
157:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[2]);
158:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex++] == r->fPoints[3]);
159:                 break;
160:             case SkPathVerb::kClose:
161:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[pIndex-1]    == r->fPoints[0]);   // last  pt
162:                 REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, pts[moveToIndex] == r->fPoints[1]);   // first pt
163:                 break;
164:         }
165:     }
166: 
167:     // make sure the iter is really done
168:     REPORTER_ASSERT(reporter, !iter.next());
169: }

34: static uint64_t next_pathdata_unique_id() {

37:             std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max() >> kHighBitsToMakeRoomForFillType;
38:     static std::atomic<uint64_t> nextID{1};

40:     SkASSERT_RELEASE(id <= kMaxID);

44: class SkSafeAccumulator {
45: public:
46:     SkSafeAccumulator(size_t n = 0) : fTotal(n) {}
47: 
48:     bool ok() const { return fSafe.ok(); }
49:     explicit operator bool() const { return fSafe.ok(); }
50: 
51:     SkSafeAccumulator& add(size_t n) {
52:         fTotal = fSafe.add(fTotal, n);
53:         return *this;
54:     }
55: 
56:     SkSafeAccumulator& addMul(size_t a, size_t b) {
57:         fTotal = fSafe.add(fTotal, fSafe.mul(a, b));
58:         return *this;
59:     }
60: 
61:     std::optional<size_t> total() const {
62:         if (fSafe.ok()) {
63:             return fTotal;
64:         }

66:     }

72: static constexpr auto gPtsPerVerb = std::to_array<uint8_t>({
73:     1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 0,  // move, line, quad, conic, cubic, close
74: });
75: 
76: static inline bool valid_conic_weight(float w) {
77:     return w >= 0 && SkIsFinite(w);
78: }
79: 
80: static bool valid_path_data(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts,
81:                             SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
82:                             SkSpan<const float> conics) {
83:     if (vbs.empty()) {
84:         return pts.empty() && conics.empty();
85:     }
86: 
87:     // We must begin with a Move (unless we're empty)
88:     if (vbs.front() != SkPathVerb::kMove) {
89:         return false;
90:     }
91:     SkPathVerb prev = SkPathVerb::kMove;
92:     size_t point_count = 1,
93:            conic_count = 0;
94: 
95:     // Check that we have a valid sequence.
96:     for (size_t i = 1; i < vbs.size(); ++i) {
97:         SkPathVerb curr = vbs[i];
98: 
99:         if (static_cast<unsigned>(curr) > static_cast<unsigned>(SkPathVerb::kLast_Verb)) {
100:             return false;
101:         }
102: 
103:         // Previous verb             Valid next verb
104:         // -----------------------------------------
105:         // Move                  --> not Move
106:         // Line/Quad/Conic/Cubic --> *
107:         // Close                 --> Move
108:         //
109:         if (prev == SkPathVerb::kMove && curr == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
110:             return false;
111:         }
112:         if (prev == SkPathVerb::kClose && curr != SkPathVerb::kMove) {
113:             return false;
114:         }
115: 
116:         point_count += gPtsPerVerb[SkToSizeT(curr)];
117:         conic_count += (curr == SkPathVerb::kConic);
118: 
119:         prev = curr;
120:     }
121: 
122:     if (pts.size() != point_count || conics.size() != conic_count){
123:         return false;
124:     }
125: 
126:     for (auto w : conics) {
127:         if (!valid_conic_weight(w)) {
128:             return false;
129:         }
130:     }
131: 
132:     return true;
133: }

201: // NOTE: This only allocates and initializes the span pointers (points, verbs),
202: //       it does NOT set the other fields
203: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Alloc(size_t npts, size_t nvbs, size_t ncns) {
204:     SkSafeAccumulator accum(sizeof(SkPathData));
205: 
206:     accum.addMul(npts, sizeof(SkPoint))
207:          .addMul(ncns, sizeof(float))
208:          .addMul(nvbs, sizeof(SkPathVerb));
209: 
210:     if (auto size = accum.total()) {
211:         // This trick allows us to just make one allocation, for us and our buffer
212:         // rather than allocating us and also allocating the buffer (via malloc or new[])
213:         // We have the corresponding operator delete() specified as well.
214:         void* storage = ::operator new (*size);
215:         sk_sp<SkPathData> path(new (storage) SkPathData(npts, nvbs, ncns));
216: 
217:         return path;
218:     }
219:     return nullptr;
220: }

222: bool SkPathData::finishInit(std::optional<SkRect> bounds, std::optional<uint8_t> segmentMask) {
223:     SkASSERT(valid_path_data(fPoints, fVerbs, fConics));
224: 
225:     if (fPoints.empty()) {
226:         fBounds = SkRect::MakeEmpty();
227:         fSegmentMask = 0;
228:         return true;
229:     }
230: 
231:     if (segmentMask.has_value()) {
232:         fSegmentMask = segmentMask.value();
233:     } else {
234:         fSegmentMask = SkPathPriv::ComputeSegmentMask(fVerbs);
235:     }
236: 
237:     if (bounds.has_value()) {
238:         fBounds = bounds.value().makeSorted();
239:         SkASSERT(SkIsFinite(&fPoints.data()->fX, fPoints.size() * 2));
240:     } else {
241:         if (auto r = SkPathPriv::TrimmedBounds(fPoints, fVerbs)) {
242:             fBounds = r.value();
243:         } else {
244:             report_pathdata_make_failure("non-finite bounds");
245:             return false;
246:         }
247:     }
248: 
249:     SkASSERT(fBounds.isSorted());
250:     return true;
251: }

253: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::MakeTransform(const SkPathRaw& src, const SkMatrix& mx) {
254:     if (src.empty()) {
255:         return SkPathData::Empty();
256:     }
257: 
258:     if (mx.hasPerspective()) {
259:         return SkPathBuilder()
260:             .addRaw(src, SkPathBuilder::Reserve::kExact)
261:             .transform(mx)
262:             .detachData();
263:     }
264: 
265:     // Allocate our result, so we can map the new points directly into it
266:     auto result = Alloc(src.points().size(), src.verbs().size(), src.conics().size());
267:     mx.mapPoints(result->fPoints, src.points());
268:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(result->fConics, src.conics());
269:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(result->fVerbs,  src.verbs());
270: 
271:     std::optional<SkRect> transformedBounds;
272:     if (mx.rectStaysRect()) {
273:         // safe us from having to compute our transformed bounds in finishInit()
274:         transformedBounds = mx.mapRect(src.bounds());
275:         if (!transformedBounds.value().isFinite()) {
276:             report_pathdata_make_failure("transform created non-finite bounds");
277:             return nullptr;
278:         }
279:     }
280: 
281:     if (!result->finishInit(transformedBounds, src.fSegmentMask)) {
282:         return nullptr;
283:     }
284: 
285:     result->setConvexity(SkPathPriv::TransformConvexity(mx, src.fPoints, src.fConvexity));
286: 
287:     return result;
288: }
289: 
290: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::makeTransform(const SkMatrix& mx) const {
291:     if (mx.isIdentity()) {
292:         return sk_ref_sp(this);
293:     }
294: 
295:     // not important for transform, just need a value
296:     const SkPathFillType ft = SkPathFillType::kDefault;
297: 
298:     auto result = MakeTransform(this->raw(ft, SkResolveConvexity::kNo), mx);
299: 
300:     if (!result) {
301:         return nullptr;
302:     }
303: 
304:     if (fType == SkPathIsAType::kGeneral) {
305:         return result;
306:     }
307: 
308:     // See if we can maintain our IsA status ...
309:     bool canMaintainIsA =
310:             mx.rectStaysRect() && SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(fPoints) && !result->bounds().isEmpty();
311:     if (!canMaintainIsA) {
312:         return result;
313:     }
314: 
315:     auto [dir, start] = SkPathPriv::TransformDirAndStart(
316:             mx, fType == SkPathIsAType::kRRect, fIsA.fDirection, fIsA.fStartIndex);
317:     result->setupIsA(fType, dir, start);
318:     return result;
319: }
320: 
321: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::makeOffset(SkVector v) const {
322:     return this->makeTransform(SkMatrix::Translate(v));
323: }
324: 
325: bool operator==(const SkPathData& a, const SkPathData& b) {
326:     if (&a == &b) {
327:         return true;
328:     }
329: 
330:     return  SkSpanPriv::EQ(a.fPoints, b.fPoints) &&
331:             SkSpanPriv::EQ(a.fConics, b.fConics) &&
332:             SkSpanPriv::EQ(a.fVerbs,  b.fVerbs);
333: }
334: 
335: /////////////////////////////////////
336: 
337: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::MakeNoCheck(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts,
338:                                           SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
339:                                           SkSpan<const float> conics,
340:                                           std::optional<SkRect> bounds,
341:                                           std::optional<unsigned> segmentMask) {
342:     SkASSERT(valid_path_data(pts, vbs, conics));
343: 
344:     auto path = Alloc(pts.size(), vbs.size(), conics.size());
345: 
346:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(path->fPoints, pts);
347:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(path->fConics, conics);
348:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(path->fVerbs,  vbs);
349: 
350:     return path->finishInit(bounds, segmentMask) ? path : nullptr;
351: }
352: 
353: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::MakeNoCheck(const SkPathRaw& raw) {
354:     return MakeNoCheck(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics(), raw.fBounds, raw.fSegmentMask);
355: }
356: 
357: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Empty() {
358:     return sk_ref_sp(PeekEmptySingleton());
359: }
360: 
361: void SkPathData::setupIsA(SkPathIsAType type, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
362:     this->setConvexity(SkPathDirection_ToConvexity(dir));
363: 
364:     SkASSERT(type == SkPathIsAType::kOval || type == SkPathIsAType::kRRect);
365:     fType = type;
366: 
367:     SkASSERT((type == SkPathIsAType::kOval && index < 4) ||
368:              (type == SkPathIsAType::kRRect && index < 8));
369: 
370:     fIsA.fDirection  = dir;
371:     fIsA.fStartIndex = SkTo<uint8_t>(index);
372: }
373: 
374: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Rect(const SkRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
375:     if (!r.isFinite()) {
376:         return nullptr;
377:     }
378:     SkPathRawShapes::Rect raw(r, dir, index);
379:     return MakeNoCheck(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics(), raw.fBounds, raw.fSegmentMask);
380: }
381: 
382: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Oval(const SkRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
383:     if (!r.isFinite()) {
384:         return nullptr;
385:     }
386:     SkPathRawShapes::Oval raw(r, dir, index);
387:     auto path = MakeNoCheck(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics(), raw.fBounds, raw.fSegmentMask);
388: 
389:     path->setupIsA(SkPathIsAType::kOval, dir, index);
390:     return path;
391: }
392: 
393: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::RRect(const SkRRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
394:     if (!r.isValid()) {
395:         return nullptr;
396:     }
397:     SkPathRawShapes::RRect raw(r, dir, index);
398:     // we use Make, not MakeNoCheck, to confirm all points an conics are finite
399:     if (auto path = Make(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics())) {
400:         path->setupIsA(SkPathIsAType::kRRect, dir, index);
401:         return path;
402:     }
403:     return nullptr;
404: }
405: 
406: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Polygon(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, bool isClosed) {
407:     if (pts.size() == 0 || (pts.size() == 1 && !isClosed)) {
408:         return Empty();
409:     }
410: 
411:     const size_t nverbs = pts.size() + isClosed;    // +1 for the kClose verb
412:     const size_t nconics = 0;
413:     auto path = Alloc(pts.size(), nverbs, nconics);
414: 
415:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(path->fPoints, pts);
416: 
417:     path->fVerbs[0] = SkPathVerb::kMove;
418:     for (size_t i = 1; i < pts.size(); ++i) {
419:         path->fVerbs[i] = SkPathVerb::kLine;
420:     }
421:     if (isClosed) {
422:         path->fVerbs.back() = SkPathVerb::kClose;
423:     }
424: 
425:     return path->finishInit({}, kLine_SkPathSegmentMask) ? path : nullptr;
426: }

430: SkPathConvexity SkPathData::getConvexityOrUnknown() const {
431:     return static_cast<SkPathConvexity>(fConvexity.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
432: }
433: 
434: SkPathConvexity SkPathData::getResolvedConvexity() const {
435:     auto convexity = this->getConvexityOrUnknown();
436:     if (convexity == SkPathConvexity::kUnknown) {
437:         convexity = SkPathPriv::ComputeConvexity(fPoints, fVerbs, fConics);
438:         this->setConvexity(convexity);
439:     }
440:     return convexity;
441: }

443: void SkPathData::setConvexity(SkPathConvexity convexity) const {
444:     fConvexity.store((uint8_t)convexity, std::memory_order_relaxed);

448:     return SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(this->getResolvedConvexity());

460:         fBounds,
461:         ft,
462:         rc == SkResolveConvexity::kYes ? this->getResolvedConvexity()
463:                                        : this->getConvexityOrUnknown(),
464:         fSegmentMask,
465:     };
466: }

468: std::optional<std::array<SkPoint, 2>> SkPathData::asLine() const {
469:     if (fPoints.size() == 2 && fVerbs.size() == 2 && fConics.size() == 0 &&
470:         fVerbs[1] == SkPathVerb::kLine)
471:     {
472:         SkASSERT(fVerbs[0] == SkPathVerb::kMove);
473:         return {{ fPoints[0], fPoints[1] }};

475:     return {};

478: std::optional<SkPathRectInfo> SkPathData::asRect() const {
479:     if (auto rc = SkPathPriv::IsRectContour(fPoints, fVerbs, fSegmentMask, false)) {
480:         SkASSERT(rc->fRect == fBounds);
481:         return {{
482:             fBounds,
483:             rc->fDirection,
484:             0, // start index???
485:         }};

487:     return {};
488: }

493:             fBounds,
494:             fIsA.fDirection,
495:             fIsA.fStartIndex,

505:             fIsA.fDirection,
506:             fIsA.fStartIndex,
507:         }};

509:     return {};

516:                     fNextIsNewContour = true;
517:                 } break;
518:                 case SkPathVerb::kClose:
519:                     if (fNeedsCloseLine) return closeline();
520:                     break;
521:                 default: {
522:                     unsigned v = static_cast<unsigned>(verb);
523:                     // Actual edge.

532:                     SkDEBUGCODE(fIsConic = (verb == SkPathVerb::kConic);)
533:                     SkASSERT(fIsConic == (cws_count > 0));
534: 
535:                     bool isNewContour = fNextIsNewContour;
536:                     fNextIsNewContour = false;
537:                     return { &fPts[-(pts_count + 1)], Edge(v), isNewContour };

546:     /** Approximates conic with quad array. Conic is constructed from start SkPoint p0,
547:         control SkPoint p1, end SkPoint p2, and weight w.
548:         Quad array is stored in pts; this storage is supplied by caller.
549:         Maximum quad count is 2 to the pow2.
550:         Every third point in array shares last SkPoint of previous quad and first SkPoint of
551:         next quad. Maximum pts storage size is given by:
552:         (1 + 2 * (1 << pow2)) * sizeof(SkPoint).
553: 
554:         Returns quad count used the approximation, which may be smaller
555:         than the number requested.
556: 
557:         conic weight determines the amount of influence conic control point has on the curve.
558:         w less than one represents an elliptical section. w greater than one represents
559:         a hyperbolic section. w equal to one represents a parabolic section.
560: 
561:         Two quad curves are sufficient to approximate an elliptical conic with a sweep
562:         of up to 90 degrees; in this case, set pow2 to one.
563: 
564:         @param p0    conic start SkPoint
565:         @param p1    conic control SkPoint
566:         @param p2    conic end SkPoint
567:         @param w     conic weight
568:         @param pts   storage for quad array
569:         @param pow2  quad count, as power of two, normally 0 to 5 (1 to 32 quad curves)
570:         @return      number of quad curves written to pts
571:     */
572:     static int ConvertConicToQuads(const SkPoint& p0, const SkPoint& p1, const SkPoint& p2,
573:                                    SkScalar w, SkPoint pts[], int pow2);

688:     /** Specifies whether SkPath is volatile; whether it will be altered or discarded
689:         by the caller after it is drawn. SkPath by default have volatile set false, allowing
690:         Skia to attach a cache of data which speeds repeated drawing.
691: 
692:         Mark temporary paths, discarded or modified after use, as volatile
693:         to inform Skia that the path need not be cached.
694: 
695:         Mark animating SkPath volatile to improve performance.
696:         Mark unchanging SkPath non-volatile to improve repeated rendering.
697: 
698:         raster surface SkPath draws are affected by volatile for some shadows.
699:         GPU surface SkPath draws are affected by volatile for some shadows and concave geometries.
700: 
701:         @param isVolatile  true if caller will alter SkPath after drawing
702:         @return            reference to SkPath

760:     /** \class SkPath::Iter
761:         Iterates through verb array, and associated SkPoint array and conic weight.
762:         Provides options to treat open contours as closed, and to ignore
763:         degenerate data.

765:     class SK_API Iter {
766:     public:
767: 
768:         /** Initializes SkPath::Iter with an empty SkPath. next() on SkPath::Iter returns
769:             kDone_Verb.

773: 
774:         example: https://fiddle.skia.org/c/@Path_Iter_Iter
775:         */
776:         Iter();
777: 
778:         /** Sets SkPath::Iter to return elements of verb array, SkPoint array, and conic weight in
779:             path. If forceClose is true, SkPath::Iter will add kLine_Verb and kClose_Verb after each
780:             open contour. path is not altered.
781: 
782:             @param path        SkPath to iterate
783:             @param forceClose  true if open contours generate kClose_Verb
784:             @return            SkPath::Iter of path
785: 
786:         example: https://fiddle.skia.org/c/@Path_Iter_const_SkPath
787:         */
788:         Iter(const SkPath& path, bool forceClose);
789: 
790:         /** Sets SkPath::Iter to return elements of verb array, SkPoint array, and conic weight in
791:             path. If forceClose is true, SkPath::Iter will add kLine_Verb and kClose_Verb after each
792:             open contour. path is not altered.
793: 
794:             @param path        SkPath to iterate
795:             @param forceClose  true if open contours generate kClose_Verb
796: 
797:         example: https://fiddle.skia.org/c/@Path_Iter_setPath
798:         */
799:         void setPath(const SkPath& path, bool forceClose);
800: 
801:         /** Returns next SkPath::Verb in verb array, and advances SkPath::Iter.
802:             When verb array is exhausted, returns kDone_Verb.
803: 
804:             Zero to four SkPoint are stored in pts, depending on the returned SkPath::Verb.
805: 
806:             @param pts  storage for SkPoint data describing returned SkPath::Verb
807:             @return     next SkPath::Verb from verb array
808: 
809:         example: https://fiddle.skia.org/c/@Path_RawIter_next
810:         */
811:         Verb next(SkPoint pts[4]);
812: 
813:         std::optional<IterRec> next();
814: 
815:         /** Returns conic weight if next() returned kConic_Verb.
816: 
817:             If next() has not been called, or next() did not return kConic_Verb,
818:             result is undefined.
819: 
820:             @return  conic weight for conic SkPoint returned by next()
821:         */
822:         SkScalar conicWeight() const { return *fConicWeights; }
823: 
824:         /** Returns true if last kLine_Verb returned by next() was generated
825:             by kClose_Verb. When true, the end point returned by next() is
826:             also the start point of contour.
827: 
828:             If next() has not been called, or next() did not return kLine_Verb,
829:             result is undefined.
830: 
831:             @return  true if last kLine_Verb was generated by kClose_Verb
832:         */
833:         bool isCloseLine() const { return SkToBool(fCloseLine); }
834: 
835:         /** Returns true if subsequent calls to next() return kClose_Verb before returning
836:             kMove_Verb. if true, contour SkPath::Iter is processing may end with kClose_Verb, or
837:             SkPath::Iter may have been initialized with force close set to true.
838: 
839:             @return  true if contour is closed
840: 
841:         example: https://fiddle.skia.org/c/@Path_Iter_isClosedContour
842:         */
843:         bool isClosedContour() const;

845:     private:

849:         const SkScalar*         fConicWeights;

853:         bool                    fForceClose;

857:         SkPathVerb autoClose(SkPoint pts[2]);

865:     /** \class SkPath::RangeIter
866:         Iterates through a raw range of path verbs, points, and conics. All values are returned
867:         unaltered.
868: 
869:         NOTE: This class will be moved into SkPathPriv once RangeIter is removed.
870:     */
871:     class RangeIter {
872:     public:
873:         RangeIter() = default;
874:         RangeIter(const SkPathVerb* verbs, const SkPoint* points, const SkScalar* weights)
875:                 : fVerb(verbs), fPoints(points), fWeights(weights) {
876:             SkDEBUGCODE(fInitialPoints = fPoints;)
877:         }
878:         bool operator!=(const RangeIter& that) const {
879:             return fVerb != that.fVerb;
880:         }
881:         bool operator==(const RangeIter& that) const {
882:             return fVerb == that.fVerb;
883:         }
884:         RangeIter& operator++() {
885:             auto verb = *fVerb++;
886:             fPoints += pts_advance_after_verb(verb);
887:             if (verb == SkPathVerb::kConic) {
888:                 ++fWeights;
889:             }
890:             return *this;
891:         }
892:         RangeIter operator++(int) {
893:             RangeIter copy = *this;
894:             this->operator++();
895:             return copy;
896:         }
897:         SkPathVerb peekVerb() const {
898:             return *fVerb;
899:         }
900:         std::tuple<SkPathVerb, const SkPoint*, const SkScalar*> operator*() const {
901:             SkPathVerb verb = this->peekVerb();
902:             // We provide the starting point for beziers by peeking backwards from the current
903:             // point, which works fine as long as there is always a kMove before any geometry.
904:             // (SkPath::injectMoveToIfNeeded should have guaranteed this to be the case.)
905:             int backset = pts_backset_for_verb(verb);
906:             SkASSERT(fPoints + backset >= fInitialPoints);
907:             return {verb, fPoints + backset, fWeights};
908:         }
909:     private:
910:         constexpr static int pts_advance_after_verb(SkPathVerb verb) {
911:             switch (verb) {
912:                 case SkPathVerb::kMove: return 1;
913:                 case SkPathVerb::kLine: return 1;
914:                 case SkPathVerb::kQuad: return 2;
915:                 case SkPathVerb::kConic: return 2;
916:                 case SkPathVerb::kCubic: return 3;
917:                 case SkPathVerb::kClose: return 0;
918:             }
919:             SkUNREACHABLE;
920:         }
921:         constexpr static int pts_backset_for_verb(SkPathVerb verb) {
922:             switch (verb) {
923:                 case SkPathVerb::kMove: return 0;
924:                 case SkPathVerb::kLine: return -1;
925:                 case SkPathVerb::kQuad: return -1;
926:                 case SkPathVerb::kConic: return -1;
927:                 case SkPathVerb::kCubic: return -1;
928:                 case SkPathVerb::kClose: return -1;
929:             }
930:             SkUNREACHABLE;
931:         }
932:         const SkPathVerb* fVerb = nullptr;
933:         const SkPoint* fPoints = nullptr;
934:         const SkScalar* fWeights = nullptr;
935:         SkDEBUGCODE(const SkPoint* fInitialPoints = nullptr;)
936:     };

944:

946:             Call setPath to initialize SkPath::Iter at a later time.

962:             path.

967: 
968:         /** Returns next SkPath::Verb in verb array, and advances RawIter.
969:             When verb array is exhausted, returns kDone_Verb.
970:             Zero to four SkPoint are stored in pts, depending on the returned SkPath::Verb.
971: 
972:             @param pts  storage for SkPoint data describing returned SkPath::Verb
973:             @return     next SkPath::Verb from verb array
974:         */
975:         Verb next(SkPoint[4]);

169: static inline bool check_edge_against_rect(const SkPoint& p0,
170:                                            const SkPoint& p1,
171:                                            const SkRect& rect,
172:                                            SkPathDirection dir) {
173:     const SkPoint* edgeBegin;
174:     SkVector v;
175:     if (SkPathDirection::kCW == dir) {
176:         v = p1 - p0;
177:         edgeBegin = &p0;
178:     } else {
179:         v = p0 - p1;
180:         edgeBegin = &p1;
181:     }
182:     if (v.fX || v.fY) {
183:         // check the cross product of v with the vec from edgeBegin to each rect corner
184:         SkScalar yL = v.fY * (rect.fLeft - edgeBegin->fX);
185:         SkScalar xT = v.fX * (rect.fTop - edgeBegin->fY);
186:         SkScalar yR = v.fY * (rect.fRight - edgeBegin->fX);
187:         SkScalar xB = v.fX * (rect.fBottom - edgeBegin->fY);
188:         if ((xT < yL) || (xT < yR) || (xB < yL) || (xB < yR)) {
189:             return false;
190:         }
191:     }
192:     return true;
193: }

195: bool SkPath::conservativelyContainsRect(const SkRect& rect) const {
196:     const SkPathConvexity convexity = this->getConvexity();
197:     if (!SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(convexity)) {
198:         return false;
199:     }
200: 
201:     const auto direction = SkPathConvexity_ToDirection(convexity);
202:     if (!direction) {
203:         return false;
204:     }
205: 
206:     SkPoint firstPt;
207:     SkPoint prevPt;
208:     int segmentCount = 0;
209:     SkDEBUGCODE(int moveCnt = 0;)
210: 
211:     for (auto [verb, pts, weight] : SkPathPriv::Iterate(*this)) {
212:         if (verb == SkPathVerb::kClose || (segmentCount > 0 && verb == SkPathVerb::kMove)) {
213:             // Closing the current contour; but since convexity is a precondition, it's the only
214:             // contour that matters.
215:             SkASSERT(moveCnt);
216:             segmentCount++;
217:             break;
218:         } else if (verb == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
219:             // A move at the start of the contour (or multiple leading moves, in which case we
220:             // keep the last one before a non-move verb).
221:             SkASSERT(!segmentCount);
222:             SkDEBUGCODE(++moveCnt);
223:             firstPt = prevPt = pts[0];
224:         } else {
225:             int pointCount = SkPathPriv::PtsInVerb((unsigned) verb);
226:             SkASSERT(pointCount > 0);
227: 
228:             if (!SkPathPriv::AllPointsEq({pts, (size_t)pointCount + 1})) {
229:                 SkASSERT(moveCnt);
230:                 int nextPt = pointCount;
231:                 segmentCount++;
232: 
233:                 if (prevPt == pts[nextPt]) {
234:                     // A pre-condition to getting here is that the path is convex, so if a
235:                     // verb's start and end points are the same, it means it's the only
236:                     // verb in the contour (and the only contour). While it's possible for
237:                     // such a single verb to be a convex curve, we do not have any non-zero
238:                     // length edges to conservatively test against without splitting or
239:                     // evaluating the curve. For simplicity, just reject the rectangle.
240:                     return false;
241:                 } else if (SkPathVerb::kConic == verb) {
242:                     SkConic orig;
243:                     orig.set(pts, *weight);
244:                     SkPoint quadPts[5];
245:                     int count = orig.chopIntoQuadsPOW2(quadPts, 1);
246:                     SkASSERT_RELEASE(2 == count);
247: 
248:                     if (!check_edge_against_rect(quadPts[0], quadPts[2], rect, *direction)) {
249:                         return false;
250:                     }
251:                     if (!check_edge_against_rect(quadPts[2], quadPts[4], rect, *direction)) {
252:                         return false;
253:                     }
254:                 } else {
255:                     if (!check_edge_against_rect(prevPt, pts[nextPt], rect, *direction)) {
256:                         return false;
257:                     }
258:                 }
259:                 prevPt = pts[nextPt];
260:             }
261:         }
262:     }
263: 
264:     if (segmentCount) {
265:         return check_edge_against_rect(prevPt, firstPt, rect, *direction);
266:     }
267:     return false;
268: }

393: SkPathIter SkPath::iter() const {
394:     return { this->points(), this->verbs(), this->conicWeights() };
395: }

398: 
399: SkPath::Iter::Iter() {
400: #ifdef SK_DEBUG
401:     fPts = nullptr;
402:     fConicWeights = nullptr;
403:     fMoveTo.fX = fMoveTo.fY = fLastPt.fX = fLastPt.fY = 0;
404:     fForceClose = fCloseLine = false;
405: #endif
406:     // need to init enough to make next() harmlessly return kDone_Verb
407:     fVerbs = nullptr;
408:     fVerbStop = nullptr;
409:     fNeedClose = false;
410: }
411: 
412: SkPath::Iter::Iter(const SkPath& path, bool forceClose) {
413:     this->setPath(path, forceClose);
414: }
415: 
416: void SkPath::Iter::setPath(const SkPath& path, bool forceClose) {
417:     fPts = path.points().data();
418: 
419:     const SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs = path.verbs();
420:     fVerbs = vbs.begin();
421:     fVerbStop = vbs.end();
422:     // For empty paths we receive an empty span, which should yield a nullptr fVerbsStop.
423:     SkASSERT(!!fVerbs == !!fVerbStop);
424: 
425:     fConicWeights = path.conicWeights().data();
426:     if (fConicWeights) {
427:       fConicWeights -= 1;  // begin one behind
428:     }
429:     fLastPt.fX = fLastPt.fY = 0;
430:     fMoveTo.fX = fMoveTo.fY = 0;
431:     fForceClose = SkToU8(forceClose);
432:     fNeedClose = false;
433: }
434: 
435: bool SkPath::Iter::isClosedContour() const {
436:     if (fVerbs == nullptr || fVerbs == fVerbStop) {
437:         return false;
438:     }
439:     if (fForceClose) {
440:         return true;
441:     }
442: 
443:     const SkPathVerb* verbs = fVerbs;
444:     const SkPathVerb* stop = fVerbStop;
445: 
446:     if (SkPathVerb::kMove == *verbs) {
447:         verbs += 1; // skip the initial moveto
448:     }
449: 
450:     while (verbs < stop) {
451:         // verbs points one beyond the current verb, decrement first.
452:         SkPathVerb v = *verbs++;
453:         if (SkPathVerb::kMove == v) {
454:             break;
455:         }
456:         if (SkPathVerb::kClose == v) {
457:             return true;
458:         }
459:     }
460:     return false;
461: }
462: 
463: SkPathVerb SkPath::Iter::autoClose(SkPoint pts[2]) {
464:     SkASSERT(pts);
465:     if (fLastPt != fMoveTo) {
466:         // A special case: if both points are NaN, SkPoint::operation== returns
467:         // false, but the iterator expects that they are treated as the same.
468:         // (consider SkPoint is a 2-dimension float point).
469:         if (SkIsNaN(fLastPt.fX) || SkIsNaN(fLastPt.fY) ||
470:             SkIsNaN(fMoveTo.fX) || SkIsNaN(fMoveTo.fY)) {
471:             return SkPathVerb::kClose;
472:         }
473: 
474:         pts[0] = fLastPt;
475:         pts[1] = fMoveTo;
476:         fLastPt = fMoveTo;
477:         fCloseLine = true;
478:         return SkPathVerb::kLine;
479:     }
480:     pts[0] = fMoveTo;
481:     return SkPathVerb::kClose;
482: }
483: 
484: SkPath::Verb SkPath::Iter::next(SkPoint ptsParam[4]) {
485:     SkASSERT(ptsParam);
486:     SkASSERT(!!fVerbs == !!fVerbStop);
487: 
488:     if (fVerbs == fVerbStop) {
489:         // Close the curve if requested and if there is some curve to close
490:         if (fNeedClose) {
491:             if (SkPathVerb::kLine == this->autoClose(ptsParam)) {
492:                 return kLine_Verb;
493:             }
494:             fNeedClose = false;
495:             return kClose_Verb;
496:         }
497:         return kDone_Verb;
498:     }
499: 
500:     SkPathVerb verb = *fVerbs++;
501:     const SkPoint* SK_RESTRICT srcPts = fPts;
502:     SkPoint* SK_RESTRICT       pts = ptsParam;
503: 
504:     switch (verb) {
505:         case SkPathVerb::kMove:
506:             if (fNeedClose) {
507:                 fVerbs--; // move back one verb
508:                 verb = this->autoClose(pts);
509:                 if (verb == SkPathVerb::kClose) {
510:                     fNeedClose = false;
511:                 }
512:                 return (Verb)verb;
513:             }
514:             if (fVerbs == fVerbStop) {    // might be a trailing moveto
515:                 return kDone_Verb;
516:             }
517:             fMoveTo = *srcPts;
518:             pts[0] = *srcPts;
519:             srcPts += 1;
520:             fLastPt = fMoveTo;
521:             fNeedClose = fForceClose;
522:             break;
523:         case SkPathVerb::kLine:
524:             pts[0] = fLastPt;
525:             pts[1] = srcPts[0];
526:             fLastPt = srcPts[0];
527:             fCloseLine = false;
528:             srcPts += 1;
529:             break;
530:         case SkPathVerb::kConic:
531:             fConicWeights += 1;
532:             [[fallthrough]];
533:         case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
534:             pts[0] = fLastPt;
535:             memcpy(&pts[1], srcPts, 2 * sizeof(SkPoint));
536:             fLastPt = srcPts[1];
537:             srcPts += 2;
538:             break;
539:         case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
540:             pts[0] = fLastPt;
541:             memcpy(&pts[1], srcPts, 3 * sizeof(SkPoint));
542:             fLastPt = srcPts[2];
543:             srcPts += 3;
544:             break;
545:         case SkPathVerb::kClose:
546:             verb = this->autoClose(pts);
547:             if (verb == SkPathVerb::kLine) {
548:                 fVerbs--; // move back one verb
549:             } else {
550:                 fNeedClose = false;
551:             }
552:             fLastPt = fMoveTo;
553:             break;
554:     }
555:     fPts = srcPts;
556:     return (Verb)verb;
557: }
558: 
559: static inline uint8_t SkPathIterPointsPerVerb(SkPathVerb verb) {
560:     static constexpr auto gCounts = std::to_array<uint8_t>({ 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 0 });
561:     unsigned index = static_cast<unsigned>(verb);
562:     SkASSERT(index < std::size(gCounts));
563:     return gCounts[index];
564: }
565: 
566: std::optional<SkPath::IterRec> SkPath::Iter::next() {
567:     auto legacyVerb = this->next(fStorage.data());
568:     if (legacyVerb == kDone_Verb) {
569:         return {};
570:     }
571: 
572:     SkPathVerb verb = static_cast<SkPathVerb>(legacyVerb);
573:     return {{
574:         verb,
575:         {fStorage.data(), SkPathIterPointsPerVerb(verb)},
576:         verb == SkPathVerb::kConic ? *fConicWeights : 1,
577:     }};
578: }
579: 
580: void SkPath::RawIter::setPath(const SkPath& path) {
581:     SkPathPriv::Iterate iterate(path);
582:     fIter = iterate.begin();
583:     fEnd = iterate.end();
584: }
585: 
586: SkPath::Verb SkPath::RawIter::next(SkPoint pts[4]) {
587:     if (!(fIter != fEnd)) {
588:         return kDone_Verb;
589:     }
590:     auto [verb, iterPts, weights] = *fIter;
591:     int numPts;
592:     switch (verb) {
593:         case SkPathVerb::kMove: numPts = 1; break;
594:         case SkPathVerb::kLine: numPts = 2; break;
595:         case SkPathVerb::kQuad: numPts = 3; break;
596:         case SkPathVerb::kConic:
597:             numPts = 3;
598:             fConicWeight = *weights;
599:             break;
600:         case SkPathVerb::kCubic: numPts = 4; break;
601:         case SkPathVerb::kClose: numPts = 0; break;
602:     }
603:     memcpy(pts, iterPts, sizeof(SkPoint) * numPts);
604:     ++fIter;
605:     return (Verb) verb;
606: }
607: 
608: std::optional<SkPath::IterRec> SkPath::RawIter::next() {
609:     if (fIter == fEnd) {
610:         return {};
611:     }
612: 
613:     auto [verb, iterPts, weights] = *fIter++;
614:     return {{
615:         verb,
616:         {iterPts, SkPathIterPointsPerVerb(verb)},
617:         verb == SkPathVerb::kConic ? *weights : 1
618:     }};
619: }

639: SkPathConvexity SkPath::computeConvexity() const {
640:     if (auto c = this->getConvexityOrUnknown(); c != SkPathConvexity::kUnknown) {
641:         return c;
642:     }
643: 
644:     SkPathConvexity convexity = SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
645: 
646:     if (this->isFinite()) {
647:         convexity = SkPathPriv::ComputeConvexity(this->points(),
648:                                                  this->verbs(),
649:                                                  this->conicWeights());
650:     }
651: 
652:     SkASSERT(convexity != SkPathConvexity::kUnknown);
653:     this->setConvexity(convexity);
654:     return convexity;
655: }

721: SkPathFirstDirection SkPathPriv::ComputeFirstDirection(const SkPath& path) {
722:     auto convexity = path.getConvexityOrUnknown();
723:     if (SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(convexity)) {
724:         // Note, this can return kUnknown. That is valid. If we've determined that the
725:         // path is convex, then we've already tried to compute its first-direction. If
726:         // that failed, then kUnknown is the right answer.
727:         return SkPathConvexity_ToFirstDirection(convexity);
728:     }
729: 
730:     // Note, this can compute a 'first' direction, even for non-convex shapes.
731:     if (auto raw = SkPathPriv::Raw(path, SkResolveConvexity::kNo)) {
732:         return ComputeFirstDirection(*raw);
733:     } else {
734:         return SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown;
735:     }
736: }

738: /*
739:  *  This returns a singleton instance which SkPath uses to signify that its pathdata is in error:
740:  *  either because the inputs were invalid (e.g. bad verbs), or its coordintes were non-finite
741:  *  (either from the client, or after a makeTransform() call).
742:  */
743: SkPathData* SkPath::PeekErrorSingleton() {
744:     static SkPathData* gErrorSingleton = SkPathData::MakeNoCheck({}, {}, {}, {}, {}).release();
745: 
746:     // Make sure MakeNoCheck() didn't alias us to the standard Empty instance. We want our
747:     // pointer to be distinct from that one.
748:     SkASSERT(gErrorSingleton != SkPathData::Empty().get());
749: 
750:     return gErrorSingleton;
751: }
752: 
753: SkPath SkPath::MakeNullCheck(sk_sp<SkPathData> pdata, SkPathFillType ft, bool isVolatile) {
754:     if (!pdata) {
755:         pdata = sk_ref_sp(PeekErrorSingleton());
756:     }
757:     return SkPath(std::move(pdata), ft, isVolatile);
758: }

760: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
761: 
762: struct SkHalfPlane {
763:     SkScalar fA, fB, fC;
764: 
765:     SkScalar eval(SkScalar x, SkScalar y) const {
766:         return fA * x + fB * y + fC;
767:     }
768:     SkScalar operator()(SkScalar x, SkScalar y) const { return this->eval(x, y); }
769: 
770:     bool normalize() {
771:         double a = fA;
772:         double b = fB;
773:         double c = fC;
774:         double dmag = sqrt(a * a + b * b);
775:         // length of initial plane normal is zero
776:         if (dmag == 0) {
777:            fA = fB = 0;
778:            fC = SK_Scalar1;
779:            return true;
780:         }
781:         double dscale = sk_ieee_double_divide(1.0, dmag);
782:         a *= dscale;
783:         b *= dscale;
784:         c *= dscale;
785:         // check if we're not finite, or normal is zero-length
786:         if (!SkIsFinite(a, b, c) ||
787:             (a == 0 && b == 0)) {
788:             fA = fB = 0;
789:             fC = SK_Scalar1;
790:             return false;
791:         }
792:         fA = a;
793:         fB = b;
794:         fC = c;
795:         return true;
796:     }
797: 
798:     enum Result {
799:         kAllNegative,
800:         kAllPositive,
801:         kMixed
802:     };
803:     Result test(const SkRect& bounds) const {
804:         // check whether the diagonal aligned with the normal crosses the plane
805:         SkPoint diagMin, diagMax;
806:         if (fA >= 0) {
807:             diagMin.fX = bounds.fLeft;
808:             diagMax.fX = bounds.fRight;
809:         } else {
810:             diagMin.fX = bounds.fRight;
811:             diagMax.fX = bounds.fLeft;
812:         }
813:         if (fB >= 0) {
814:             diagMin.fY = bounds.fTop;
815:             diagMax.fY = bounds.fBottom;
816:         } else {
817:             diagMin.fY = bounds.fBottom;
818:             diagMax.fY = bounds.fTop;
819:         }
820:         SkScalar test = this->eval(diagMin.fX, diagMin.fY);
821:         SkScalar sign = test*this->eval(diagMax.fX, diagMax.fY);
822:         if (sign > 0) {
823:             // the path is either all on one side of the half-plane or the other
824:             if (test < 0) {
825:                 return kAllNegative;
826:             } else {
827:                 return kAllPositive;
828:             }
829:         }
830:         return kMixed;
831:     }
832: };
833: 
834: // assumes plane is pre-normalized
835: static std::optional<SkPath> clip(const SkPath& path, const SkHalfPlane& plane) {
836:     SkMatrix mx;
837:     SkPoint p0 = { -plane.fA*plane.fC, -plane.fB*plane.fC };
838:     mx.setAll( plane.fB, plane.fA, p0.fX,
839:               -plane.fA, plane.fB, p0.fY,
840:                       0,        0,     1);
841:     auto inv = mx.invert();
842:     if (!inv) {
843:         return {};
844:     }
845: 
846:     auto rotated = path.tryMakeTransform(*inv);
847:     if (!rotated) {
848:         return {};
849:     }
850:     auto raw = SkPathPriv::Raw(*rotated, SkResolveConvexity::kNo);
851:     if (!raw) {
852:         SkASSERT(false);    // if rotated was valid, so should the raw
853:         return {};
854:     }
855: 
856:     SkScalar big = SK_ScalarMax;
857:     SkRect clip = {-big, 0, big, big };
858: 
859:     struct Rec {
860:         SkPathBuilder fResult;
861:         SkPoint       fPrev = {0,0};
862:     } rec;
863: 
864:     SkEdgeClipper::ClipPath(*raw, clip, false,
865:                             [](SkEdgeClipper* clipper, bool newCtr, void* ctx) {
866:         Rec* rec = (Rec*)ctx;
867: 
868:         bool addLineTo = false;
869:         SkPoint      pts[4];
870:         while (auto verb = clipper->next(pts)) {
871:             if (newCtr) {
872:                 rec->fResult.moveTo(pts[0]);
873:                 rec->fPrev = pts[0];
874:                 newCtr = false;
875:             }
876: 
877:             if (addLineTo || pts[0] != rec->fPrev) {
878:                 rec->fResult.lineTo(pts[0]);
879:             }
880: 
881:             switch (*verb) {
882:                 case SkPathVerb::kLine:
883:                     rec->fResult.lineTo(pts[1]);
884:                     rec->fPrev = pts[1];
885:                     break;
886:                 case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
887:                     rec->fResult.quadTo(pts[1], pts[2]);
888:                     rec->fPrev = pts[2];
889:                     break;
890:                 case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
891:                     rec->fResult.cubicTo(pts[1], pts[2], pts[3]);
892:                     rec->fPrev = pts[3];
893:                     break;
894:                 default: break;
895:             }
896:             addLineTo = true;
897:         }
898:     }, &rec);
899: 
900:     rec.fResult.setFillType(path.getFillType());
901:     SkPath result = rec.fResult.detach(&mx);
902:     if (!result.isFinite()) {
903:         return {};
904:     }
905:     return result;
906: }
907: 
908: // true means we have written to clippedPath
909: bool SkPathPriv::PerspectiveClip(const SkPath& path, const SkMatrix& matrix, SkPath* clippedPath) {
910:     if (!matrix.hasPerspective()) {
911:         return false;
912:     }
913: 
914:     SkHalfPlane plane {
915:         matrix[SkMatrix::kMPersp0],
916:         matrix[SkMatrix::kMPersp1],
917:         matrix[SkMatrix::kMPersp2] - kW0PlaneDistance
918:     };
919:     if (plane.normalize()) {
920:         switch (plane.test(path.getBounds())) {
921:             case SkHalfPlane::kAllPositive:
922:                 return false;
923:             case SkHalfPlane::kMixed: {
924:                 if (auto result = clip(path, plane)) {
925:                     *clippedPath = *result;
926:                 } else {
927:                     *clippedPath = SkPath(); // clipped out (or failed)
928:                 }
929:                 return true;
930:             }
931:             default: break; // handled outside of the switch
932:         }
933:     }
934:     // clipped out (or failed)
935:     *clippedPath = SkPath();
936:     return true;
937: }
938: 
939: std::optional<SkPathRectInfo> SkPathPriv::IsSimpleRect(const SkPath& path, bool isSimpleFill) {
940:     if (path.getSegmentMasks() != SkPath::kLine_SegmentMask) {
941:         return {};
942:     }
943:     std::array<SkPoint, 5> rectPts;
944:     int rectPtCnt = 0;
945:     bool needsClose = !isSimpleFill;
946:     for (auto [v, verbPts, w] : SkPathPriv::Iterate(path)) {
947:         switch (v) {
948:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:
949:                 if (0 != rectPtCnt) {
950:                     return {};
951:                 }
952:                 rectPts[0] = verbPts[0];
953:                 ++rectPtCnt;
954:                 break;
955:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:
956:                 if (5 == rectPtCnt) {
957:                     return {};
958:                 }
959:                 rectPts[rectPtCnt] = verbPts[1];
960:                 ++rectPtCnt;
961:                 break;
962:             case SkPathVerb::kClose:
963:                 if (4 == rectPtCnt) {
964:                     rectPts[4] = rectPts[0];
965:                     rectPtCnt = 5;
966:                 }
967:                 needsClose = false;
968:                 break;
969:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
970:             case SkPathVerb::kConic:
971:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
972:                 return {};
973:         }
974:     }
975:     if (needsClose) {
976:         return {};
977:     }
978:     if (rectPtCnt < 5) {
979:         return {};
980:     }
981:     if (rectPts[0] != rectPts[4]) {
982:         return {};
983:     }
984:     // Check for two cases of rectangles: pts 0 and 3 form a vertical edge or a horizontal edge (
985:     // and pts 1 and 2 the opposite vertical or horizontal edge).
986:     bool vec03IsVertical;
987:     if (rectPts[0].fX == rectPts[3].fX && rectPts[1].fX == rectPts[2].fX &&
988:         rectPts[0].fY == rectPts[1].fY && rectPts[3].fY == rectPts[2].fY) {
989:         // Make sure it has non-zero width and height
990:         if (rectPts[0].fX == rectPts[1].fX || rectPts[0].fY == rectPts[3].fY) {
991:             return {};
992:         }
993:         vec03IsVertical = true;
994:     } else if (rectPts[0].fY == rectPts[3].fY && rectPts[1].fY == rectPts[2].fY &&
995:                rectPts[0].fX == rectPts[1].fX && rectPts[3].fX == rectPts[2].fX) {
996:         // Make sure it has non-zero width and height
997:         if (rectPts[0].fY == rectPts[1].fY || rectPts[0].fX == rectPts[3].fX) {
998:             return {};
999:         }
1000:         vec03IsVertical = false;
1001:     } else {
1002:         return {};
1003:     }
1004: 
1005:     SkPathRectInfo info;
1006:

#ifndef SkPathTypes_DEFINED
#define SkPathTypes_DEFINED

#include "include/core/SkTypes.h"

#include <cstdint>

enum class SkPathFillType : uint8_t {
    /** Specifies that "inside" is computed by a non-zero sum of signed edge crossings */
    kWinding,
    /** Specifies that "inside" is computed by an odd number of edge crossings */
    kEvenOdd,
    /** Same as Winding, but draws outside of the path, rather than inside */
    kInverseWinding,
    /** Same as EvenOdd, but draws outside of the path, rather than inside */
    kInverseEvenOdd,

    kDefault = kWinding,
};

static inline bool SkPathFillType_IsEvenOdd(SkPathFillType ft) {
    return (static_cast<int>(ft) & 1) != 0;
}

static inline bool SkPathFillType_IsInverse(SkPathFillType ft) {
    return (static_cast<int>(ft) & 2) != 0;
}

static inline SkPathFillType SkPathFillType_ToggleInverse(SkPathFillType ft) {
    return static_cast<SkPathFillType>(static_cast<int>(ft) ^ 2);
}

static inline SkPathFillType SkPathFillType_ConvertToNonInverse(SkPathFillType ft) {
    return static_cast<SkPathFillType>(static_cast<int>(ft) & 1);
}

enum class SkPathDirection : uint8_t {
    /** clockwise direction for adding closed contours */
    kCW,
    /** counter-clockwise direction for adding closed contours */
    kCCW,

    kDefault = kCW,
};

enum SkPathSegmentMask {
    kLine_SkPathSegmentMask   = 1 << 0,
    kQuad_SkPathSegmentMask   = 1 << 1,
    kConic_SkPathSegmentMask  = 1 << 2,
    kCubic_SkPathSegmentMask  = 1 << 3,
};

enum class SkPathVerb : uint8_t {
    kMove,   //!< SkPath::RawIter returns 1 point
    kLine,   //!< SkPath::RawIter returns 2 points
    kQuad,   //!< SkPath::RawIter returns 3 points
    kConic,  //!< SkPath::RawIter returns 3 points + 1 weight
    kCubic,  //!< SkPath::RawIter returns 4 points
    kClose,  //!< SkPath::RawIter returns 0 points

    kLast_Verb = kClose,
};

#endif

 * found in the LICENSE file.

#ifndef SkPathEnums_DEFINED
#define SkPathEnums_DEFINED

#include "include/core/SkPathTypes.h"

#include <optional>

enum class SkPathConvexity {
    kConvex_CW,
    kConvex_CCW,
    kConvex_Degenerate,  // known to not have a determinable direction, but convex

    kConcave,

    kUnknown,   // todo: can we eliminate this, and use optional or other patterns?
};

enum class SkResolveConvexity {
    kNo = false,
    kYes = true,
};

static inline bool SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(SkPathConvexity cv) {
    return cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW
        || cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW
        || cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate;
}

static inline SkPathConvexity SkPathConvexity_OppositeConvexDirection(SkPathConvexity cv) {
    SkASSERT(SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(cv));
    switch (cv) {
        case SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW:  cv = SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW; break;
        case SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW: cv = SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW;  break;
        default: break;
    }
    return cv;
}

enum class SkPathFirstDirection {
    kCW,         // == SkPathDirection::kCW
    kCCW,        // == SkPathDirection::kCCW
    kUnknown,
};

static inline SkPathConvexity SkPathDirection_ToConvexity(SkPathDirection dir) {
    switch (dir) {
        case SkPathDirection::kCW:  return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW;
        case SkPathDirection::kCCW: return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW;
    }
    SkUNREACHABLE;
}

static inline SkPathConvexity SkPathFirstDirection_ToConvexity(SkPathFirstDirection dir) {
    switch (dir) {
        case SkPathFirstDirection::kCW:      return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW;
        case SkPathFirstDirection::kCCW:     return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW;
        case SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown: return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate;
    }
    SkUNREACHABLE;
}

static inline std::optional<SkPathDirection> SkPathConvexity_ToDirection(SkPathConvexity cv) {
    if (cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW) {
        return SkPathDirection::kCW;
    }
    if (cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW) {
        return SkPathDirection::kCCW;
    }
    return {};
}

static inline SkPathFirstDirection SkPathConvexity_ToFirstDirection(SkPathConvexity cv) {
    if (cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW) {
        return SkPathFirstDirection::kCW;
    }
    if (cv == SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW) {
        return SkPathFirstDirection::kCCW;
    }
    return SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown;
}

static inline SkPathFirstDirection SkPathDirectionToFirst(SkPathDirection dir) {
    return dir == SkPathDirection::kCW ? SkPathFirstDirection::kCW
                                       : SkPathFirstDirection::kCCW;
}

#endif

#ifndef SkArc_DEFINED
#define SkArc_DEFINED

#include "include/core/SkRect.h"
#include "include/core/SkScalar.h"

// Represents an arc along an oval boundary, or a closed wedge of the oval.
struct SkArc {
    enum class Type : bool {
        kArc,   // An arc along the perimeter of the oval
        kWedge  // A closed wedge that includes the oval's center
    };

    SkArc() = default;
    SkArc(const SkArc& arc) = default;
    SkArc& operator=(const SkArc& arc) = default;

    const SkRect& oval() const { return fOval; }
    SkScalar startAngle() const { return fStartAngle; }
    SkScalar sweepAngle() const { return fSweepAngle; }
    bool isWedge() const { return fType == Type::kWedge; }

    friend bool operator==(const SkArc& a, const SkArc& b) {
        return a.fOval == b.fOval && a.fStartAngle == b.fStartAngle &&
               a.fSweepAngle == b.fSweepAngle && a.fType == b.fType;
    }

    friend bool operator!=(const SkArc& a, const SkArc& b) { return !(a == b); }

    // Preferred factory that explicitly states which type of arc
    static SkArc Make(const SkRect& oval,
                      SkScalar startAngleDegrees,
                      SkScalar sweepAngleDegrees,
                      Type type) {
        return SkArc(oval, startAngleDegrees, sweepAngleDegrees, type);
    }

    // Deprecated factory to assist with legacy code based on `useCenter`
    static SkArc Make(const SkRect& oval,
                      SkScalar startAngleDegrees,
                      SkScalar sweepAngleDegrees,
                      bool useCenter) {
        return SkArc(
                oval, startAngleDegrees, sweepAngleDegrees, useCenter ? Type::kWedge : Type::kArc);
    }

    // Bounds of oval containing the arc.
    SkRect   fOval = SkRect::MakeEmpty();

    // Angle in degrees where the arc begins. Zero means horizontally to the right.
    SkScalar fStartAngle = 0;
    // Sweep angle in degrees; positive is clockwise.
    SkScalar fSweepAngle = 0;

    Type     fType = Type::kArc;

private:
    SkArc(const SkRect& oval, SkScalar startAngle, SkScalar sweepAngle, Type type)
            : fOval(oval), fStartAngle(startAngle), fSweepAngle(sweepAngle), fType(type) {}
};

#endif

}
fn mono(r: &mut Reporter, name: &str, input: &[Point], t: f32, expected: &[Point], x: bool) {

    );

#ifndef SkPathIter_DEFINED
#define SkPathIter_DEFINED

#include "include/core/SkPathTypes.h"
#include "include/core/SkPoint.h"
#include "include/core/SkSpan.h"

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <optional>

class SK_API SkPathIter {
public:
    struct Rec {
        SkSpan<const SkPoint> fPoints;
        float                 fConicWeight;
        SkPathVerb            fVerb;

        float conicWeight() const {
            SkASSERT(fVerb == SkPathVerb::kConic);
            return fConicWeight;
        }
    };

    SkPathIter(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs, SkSpan<const float> cns)
        : pIndex(0), vIndex(0), cIndex(0)
        , fPoints(pts), fVerbs(vbs), fConics(cns)
    {
        // For compat older iterators, we trim off a trailing Move.
        // SkPathData is defined to never create this pattern, so perhaps in the future
        // this check can be removed (or replaced by an assert)
        if (!vbs.empty() && vbs.back() == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
            fVerbs = vbs.first(vbs.size() - 1);
        }
    }

    /*  Holds the current verb, and its associated points
     *  move:  pts[0]
     *  line:  pts[0..1]
     *  quad:  pts[0..2]
     *  conic: pts[0..2] fConicWeight
     *  cubic: pts[0..3]
     *  close: pts[0..1] ... as if close were a line from pts[0] to pts[1]
     */
    std::optional<Rec> next();

    std::optional<SkPathVerb> peekNextVerb() const {
        if (vIndex < fVerbs.size()) {
            return fVerbs[vIndex];
        }
        return {};
    }

private:
    size_t                   pIndex, vIndex, cIndex;
    SkSpan<const SkPoint>    fPoints;
    SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> fVerbs;
    SkSpan<const float>      fConics;
    std::array<SkPoint, 2>   fClosePointStorage;
};

class SkPathContourIter {
public:
    struct Rec {
        SkSpan<const SkPoint>    fPoints;
        SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> fVerbs;
        SkSpan<const float>      fConics;
    };

    SkPathContourIter(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
                      SkSpan<const float> cns)
        : fPoints(pts), fVerbs(vbs), fConics(cns)
    {}

    std::optional<Rec> next();

private:
    SkSpan<const SkPoint>    fPoints;
    SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> fVerbs;
    SkSpan<const float>      fConics;
};

#endif
/*
 * Copyright 2025 Google LLC
 *
 * Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style license that can be
 * found in the LICENSE file.
 */

#include "include/core/SkPathIter.h"

/*
 *  Close is funny -- it has no explicit point data, but we return 2 points,
 *  the logical 2 points that would make up the line connecting the end of
 *  the contour, and its beginning.
 *
 *  To do this, we have local storage (fClosePointStorage)
 */
std::optional<SkPathIter::Rec> SkPathIter::next() {
    if (vIndex >= fVerbs.size()) {
        return {};
    }

    size_t n = 0;

    float w = -1;
    SkPathVerb v;
    switch (v = fVerbs[vIndex++]) {
        case SkPathVerb::kMove:
            fClosePointStorage[1] = fPoints[pIndex++]; // remember for close
            return Rec{{&fClosePointStorage[1], 1}, w, v};
        case SkPathVerb::kLine:  n = 1; break;
        case SkPathVerb::kQuad:  n = 2; break;
        case SkPathVerb::kConic: n = 2; w = fConics[cIndex++]; break;
        case SkPathVerb::kCubic: n = 3; break;
        case SkPathVerb::kClose:
            SkASSERT(pIndex > 0);
            fClosePointStorage[0] = fPoints[pIndex-1];   // the last point we saw
            return Rec{fClosePointStorage, w, v};
    }

    SkASSERT(pIndex > 0);
    auto start = pIndex - 1;
    SkASSERT(n >= 1 && n <= 3);
    pIndex += n;
    return Rec{{&fPoints[start], n+1}, w, v};

}

///////////////////////////////////////////////

std::optional<SkPathContourIter::Rec> SkPathContourIter::next() {
    if (fVerbs.empty()) {
        return {};
    }

    SkASSERT(fVerbs[0] == SkPathVerb::kMove);
    size_t npts = 1, nvbs = 1, nws = 0;

    for (size_t i = 1; i < fVerbs.size(); ++i) {
        switch (fVerbs[i]) {
            case SkPathVerb::kMove: goto DONE;
            case SkPathVerb::kLine:  npts += 1; break;
            case SkPathVerb::kQuad:  npts += 2; break;
            case SkPathVerb::kConic: npts += 2; nws += 1; break;
            case SkPathVerb::kCubic: npts += 3; break;
            case SkPathVerb::kClose: nvbs += 1; goto DONE;
        }
        nvbs += 1;
    }
DONE:
    Rec rec = {
        fPoints.subspan(0, npts),
        fVerbs.subspan(0, nvbs),
        fConics.subspan(0, nws),
    };
    fPoints = fPoints.last(fPoints.size() - npts);
    fVerbs  = fVerbs.last( fVerbs.size()  - nvbs);
    fConics = fConics.last(fConics.size() - nws);
    return rec;
}

#ifndef SkPathMakers_DEFINED
#define SkPathMakers_DEFINED

#include "include/core/SkPathTypes.h"
#include "include/core/SkPoint.h"
#include "include/core/SkRRect.h"

#include <array>

template <unsigned N> class SkPath_PointIterator {
public:
    SkPath_PointIterator(SkPathDirection dir, unsigned startIndex)
    : fCurrent(startIndex % N)
    , fAdvance(dir == SkPathDirection::kCW ? 1 : N - 1) { }

    const SkPoint& current() const {
        SkASSERT(fCurrent < N);
        return fPts[fCurrent];
    }

    const SkPoint& next() {
        fCurrent = (fCurrent + fAdvance) % N;
        return this->current();
    }

    protected:
    std::array<SkPoint, N> fPts;

    private:
    unsigned fCurrent;
    unsigned fAdvance;
};

class SkPath_RectPointIterator : public SkPath_PointIterator<4> {
public:
    SkPath_RectPointIterator(const SkRect& rect, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned startIndex)
        : SkPath_PointIterator(dir, startIndex) {

        fPts[0] = SkPoint::Make(rect.fLeft, rect.fTop);
        fPts[1] = SkPoint::Make(rect.fRight, rect.fTop);
        fPts[2] = SkPoint::Make(rect.fRight, rect.fBottom);
        fPts[3] = SkPoint::Make(rect.fLeft, rect.fBottom);
    }
};

class SkPath_OvalPointIterator : public SkPath_PointIterator<4> {
public:
    SkPath_OvalPointIterator(const SkRect& oval, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned startIndex)
        : SkPath_PointIterator(dir, startIndex) {

        const SkScalar cx = oval.centerX();
        const SkScalar cy = oval.centerY();

        fPts[0] = SkPoint::Make(cx, oval.fTop);
        fPts[1] = SkPoint::Make(oval.fRight, cy);
        fPts[2] = SkPoint::Make(cx, oval.fBottom);
        fPts[3] = SkPoint::Make(oval.fLeft, cy);
    }
};

class SkPath_RRectPointIterator : public SkPath_PointIterator<8> {
public:
    SkPath_RRectPointIterator(const SkRRect& rrect, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned startIndex)
        : SkPath_PointIterator(dir, startIndex) {

        const SkRect& bounds = rrect.getBounds();
        const SkScalar L = bounds.fLeft;
        const SkScalar T = bounds.fTop;
        const SkScalar R = bounds.fRight;
        const SkScalar B = bounds.fBottom;

        fPts[0] = SkPoint::Make(L + rrect.radii(SkRRect::kUpperLeft_Corner).fX, T);
        fPts[1] = SkPoint::Make(R - rrect.radii(SkRRect::kUpperRight_Corner).fX, T);
        fPts[2] = SkPoint::Make(R, T + rrect.radii(SkRRect::kUpperRight_Corner).fY);
        fPts[3] = SkPoint::Make(R, B - rrect.radii(SkRRect::kLowerRight_Corner).fY);
        fPts[4] = SkPoint::Make(R - rrect.radii(SkRRect::kLowerRight_Corner).fX, B);
        fPts[5] = SkPoint::Make(L + rrect.radii(SkRRect::kLowerLeft_Corner).fX, B);
        fPts[6] = SkPoint::Make(L, B - rrect.radii(SkRRect::kLowerLeft_Corner).fY);
        fPts[7] = SkPoint::Make(L, T + rrect.radii(SkRRect::kUpperLeft_Corner).fY);
    }
};

#endif

        : RRect(rr, dir, (dir == SkPathDirection::kCW ? 6 : 7)) {}
    explicit RRect(const SkRRect& rr) : RRect(rr, SkPathDirection::kCW, 6) {}
};

#include "src/core/SkPathRawShapes.h"

#include "include/core/SkPathTypes.h"
#include "include/core/SkRRect.h"
#include "include/private/SkAssert.h"
#include "src/core/SkPathMakers.h"

const SkPathFillType kDefFillType = SkPathFillType::kWinding;

const SkPathVerb gRectVerbs[] = {
    SkPathVerb::kMove,
    SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kClose
};

const uint8_t gRectSegMask = kLine_SkPathSegmentMask;

static void set_as_rect(SkPathRaw* raw, SkSpan<SkPoint> storage,
                        const SkRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
    SkASSERT(storage.size() >= 4);

    raw->fPoints = { storage.data(), 4 };
    raw->fVerbs = gRectVerbs;
    raw->fConics = {};
    raw->fBounds = r;
    raw->fFillType = kDefFillType;
    raw->fConvexity = SkPathDirection_ToConvexity(dir);
    raw->fSegmentMask = gRectSegMask;

    SkPath_RectPointIterator iter(r, dir, index);

    storage[0] = iter.current();
    storage[1] = iter.next();
    storage[2] = iter.next();
    storage[3] = iter.next();
}

//////////////////

const SkPathVerb gOvalVerbs[] = {
    SkPathVerb::kMove,
    SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kClose
};

const uint8_t gOvalSegMask = kConic_SkPathSegmentMask;

const float gFourQuarterCircleConics[] = {
    SK_ScalarRoot2Over2,
    SK_ScalarRoot2Over2,
    SK_ScalarRoot2Over2,
    SK_ScalarRoot2Over2,
};

static void set_as_oval(SkPathRaw* raw, SkSpan<SkPoint> storage,
                        const SkRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
    SkASSERT(storage.size() >= 9);

    raw->fPoints = { storage.data(), 9 };
    raw->fVerbs = gOvalVerbs;
    raw->fConics = gFourQuarterCircleConics;
    raw->fBounds = r;
    raw->fFillType = kDefFillType;
    raw->fConvexity = SkPathDirection_ToConvexity(dir);
    raw->fSegmentMask = gOvalSegMask;

    SkPath_OvalPointIterator ovalIter(r, dir, index);
    SkPath_RectPointIterator rectIter(r, dir, index + (dir == SkPathDirection::kCW ? 0 : 1));

    storage[0] = ovalIter.current();
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        storage[i*2 + 1] = rectIter.next();
        storage[i*2 + 2] = ovalIter.next();
    }
}

/////////////////////////////

const SkPathVerb gRRectVerbs_LineStart[] = {
    SkPathVerb::kMove,
    SkPathVerb::kLine, SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kLine, SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kLine, SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kLine, SkPathVerb::kConic,
    SkPathVerb::kClose
};

const SkPathVerb gRRectVerbs_ConicStart[] = {
    SkPathVerb::kMove,
    SkPathVerb::kConic, SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kConic, SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kConic, SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kConic, // we can skip the last line
    SkPathVerb::kClose
};

const uint8_t gRRectSegMask = kLine_SkPathSegmentMask | kConic_SkPathSegmentMask;

static void set_as_rrect(SkPathRaw* raw, SkSpan<SkPoint> storage,
                         const SkRRect& rrect, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
    // we start with a conic on odd indices when moving CW vs. even indices when moving CCW
    const bool startsWithConic = ((index & 1) == (dir == SkPathDirection::kCW));
    // if we start with a conic, we end with a line, which we can skip (relying on close())
    const size_t npoints = 13 - startsWithConic;
    const SkRect& bounds = rrect.getBounds();

    SkASSERT(storage.size() >= npoints);

    raw->fPoints = { storage.data(), npoints };
    if (startsWithConic) {
        raw->fVerbs = gRRectVerbs_ConicStart;
    } else {
        raw->fVerbs = gRRectVerbs_LineStart;
    }
    raw->fConics = gFourQuarterCircleConics;
    raw->fBounds = bounds;
    raw->fFillType = kDefFillType;
    raw->fConvexity = SkPathDirection_ToConvexity(dir);
    raw->fSegmentMask = gRRectSegMask;

    SkPath_RRectPointIterator rrectIter(rrect, dir, index);
    // Corner iterator indices follow the collapsed radii model,
    // adjusted such that the start pt is "behind" the radii start pt.
    const unsigned rectStartIndex = index / 2 + (dir == SkPathDirection::kCW ? 0 : 1);
    SkPath_RectPointIterator rectIter(bounds, dir, rectStartIndex);

    storage[0] = rrectIter.current();
    if (startsWithConic) {
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
            // conic points
            storage[i*3 + 1] = rectIter.next();
            storage[i*3 + 2] = rrectIter.next();
            // line point
            storage[i*3 + 3] = rrectIter.next();
        }
        // last conic points
        storage[10] = rectIter.next();
        storage[11] = rrectIter.next();
        // the final line is accomplished by close()
    } else {
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
            // line point
            storage[i*3 + 1] = rrectIter.next();
            // conic points
            storage[i*3 + 2] = rectIter.next();
            storage[i*3 + 3] = rrectIter.next();
        }
    }
    // close
}

/////////////////////////////

SkPathRawShapes::Rect::Rect(const SkRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
    set_as_rect(this, fStorage, r, dir, index);
}

SkPathRawShapes::Oval::Oval(const SkRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
    set_as_oval(this, fStorage, r, dir, index);
}

SkPathRawShapes::RRect::RRect(const SkRRect& rrect, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
    const SkRect& bounds = rrect.getBounds();

    if (rrect.isRect() || rrect.isEmpty()) {
        // degenerate(rect) => radii points are collapsing
        set_as_rect(this, fStorage, bounds, dir, (index + 1) / 2);
    } else if (rrect.isOval()) {
        // degenerate(oval) => line points are collapsing
        set_as_oval(this, fStorage, bounds, dir, index / 2);
    } else {
        set_as_rrect(this, fStorage, rrect, dir, index);
    }
}

/////////////////////////////

const SkPathVerb gTriangle_Verbs[] = {
    SkPathVerb::kMove,
    SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kLine,
    SkPathVerb::kClose
};

static SkPathConvexity tri_to_convexity(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts) {
    SkVector u = pts[1] - pts[0],
             v = pts[2] - pts[1];
    float cross = u.fX * v.fY - u.fY * v.fX;

    return cross > 0 ? SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CW
                     : (cross < 0) ? SkPathConvexity::kConvex_CCW
                                   : SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate;
}

SkPathRawShapes::Triangle::Triangle(SkSpan<const SkPoint> threePoints, const SkRect& bounds)
    : SkPathRaw{threePoints, gTriangle_Verbs, {}, bounds,
                SkPathFillType::kDefault, tri_to_convexity(threePoints), kLine_SkPathSegmentMask}
{
    SkASSERT(threePoints.size() == 3);
    SkASSERT(SkRect::Bounds(threePoints).value() == bounds);
}

#ifndef SkPathRaw_DEFINED

/**
 *  SkPathRaw is a non-owning, immutable view of the path geometry.
 *
 *  It allows us to have stack-allocated paths, see SkPathRawShapes.h
 *
 *  It is the responsibility of the creator to ensure that the spans in SkPathRaw point to valid
 *  data that outlives the SkPathRaw instance.
 */
struct SkPathRaw {
    SkSpan<const SkPoint>    fPoints;
    SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> fVerbs;
    SkSpan<const float>      fConics;
    SkRect                   fBounds;
    SkPathFillType           fFillType;
    SkPathConvexity          fConvexity;
    uint8_t                  fSegmentMask;  // See SkPath::SegmentMask

    SkSpan<const SkPoint> points() const { return fPoints; }
    SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> verbs() const { return fVerbs; }
    SkSpan<const float> conics() const { return fConics; }
    SkRect bounds() const { return fBounds; }
    SkPathFillType fillType() const { return fFillType; }
    SkPathConvexity convexity() const { return fConvexity; }
    unsigned segmentMasks() const { return fSegmentMask; }

    bool empty() const { return fVerbs.empty(); }
    bool isInverseFillType() const { return SkPathFillType_IsInverse(fFillType); }
    bool isKnownToBeConvex() const { return SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(fConvexity); }

    std::optional<SkRect> isRect() const;

    SkPathIter iter() const { return {fPoints, fVerbs, fConics}; }

    static SkPathRaw Empty(SkPathFillType ft = SkPathFillType::kDefault) {
        return {
            {}, {}, {}, SkRect::MakeEmpty(), ft, SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate, 0,
        };
    }
};

#endif
