#include "include/core/SkPathTypes.h"
#include "include/private/SkAssert.h"
#include "src/core/SkPathPriv.h"
#include "src/core/SkPathRaw.h"

#include <array>

static constexpr auto gVerbToSegmentMask = std::to_array<uint8_t>({
    0,  // move
    kLine_SkPathSegmentMask,
    kQuad_SkPathSegmentMask,
    kConic_SkPathSegmentMask,
    kCubic_SkPathSegmentMask,
    0,  // close
});

uint8_t SkPathPriv::ComputeSegmentMask(SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> verbs) {
    unsigned mask = 0;
    for (auto v : verbs) {
        unsigned i = static_cast<unsigned>(v);
        SkASSERT(i < std::size(gVerbToSegmentMask));
        mask |= gVerbToSegmentMask[i];
    }
    return SkTo<uint8_t>(mask);
}

std::optional<SkRect> SkPathRaw::isRect() const {
    if (auto rc = SkPathPriv::IsRectContour(fPoints, fVerbs, fSegmentMask, false)) {
        return rc->fRect;
    }
    return {};
}

55: 
56:     SkSafeAccumulator& addMul(size_t a, size_t b) {
57:         fTotal = fSafe.add(fTotal, fSafe.mul(a, b));
58:         return *this;
59:     }
60: 
61:     std::optional<size_t> total() const {
62:         if (fSafe.ok()) {
63:             return fTotal;
64:         }
65:         return {};
66:     }
67: private:
68:     SkSafeMath fSafe;
69:     size_t     fTotal;
70: };

72: static constexpr auto gPtsPerVerb = std::to_array<uint8_t>({
73:     1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 0,  // move, line, quad, conic, cubic, close
74: });
75: 
76: static inline bool valid_conic_weight(float w) {
77:     return w >= 0 && SkIsFinite(w);
78: }
79: 
80: static bool valid_path_data(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts,
81:                             SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
82:                             SkSpan<const float> conics) {
83:     if (vbs.empty()) {
84:         return pts.empty() && conics.empty();
85:     }
86: 
87:     // We must begin with a Move (unless we're empty)
88:     if (vbs.front() != SkPathVerb::kMove) {
89:         return false;
90:     }
91:     SkPathVerb prev = SkPathVerb::kMove;
92:     size_t point_count = 1,
93:            conic_count = 0;
94: 
95:     // Check that we have a valid sequence.
96:     for (size_t i = 1; i < vbs.size(); ++i) {
97:         SkPathVerb curr = vbs[i];
98: 
99:         if (static_cast<unsigned>(curr) > static_cast<unsigned>(SkPathVerb::kLast_Verb)) {
100:             return false;
101:         }
102: 
103:         // Previous verb             Valid next verb
104:         // -----------------------------------------
105:         // Move                  --> not Move
106:         // Line/Quad/Conic/Cubic --> *
107:         // Close                 --> Move
108:         //
109:         if (prev == SkPathVerb::kMove && curr == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
110:             return false;
111:         }
112:         if (prev == SkPathVerb::kClose && curr != SkPathVerb::kMove) {
113:             return false;
114:         }
115: 
116:         point_count += gPtsPerVerb[SkToSizeT(curr)];
117:         conic_count += (curr == SkPathVerb::kConic);
118: 
119:         prev = curr;
120:     }
121: 
122:     if (pts.size() != point_count || conics.size() != conic_count){
123:         return false;
124:     }
125: 
126:     for (auto w : conics) {
127:         if (!valid_conic_weight(w)) {
128:             return false;
129:         }
130:     }
131: 
132:     return true;
133: }

201: // NOTE: This only allocates and initializes the span pointers (points, verbs),

203: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Alloc(size_t npts, size_t nvbs, size_t ncns) {
204:     SkSafeAccumulator accum(sizeof(SkPathData));
205: 
206:     accum.addMul(npts, sizeof(SkPoint))
207:          .addMul(ncns, sizeof(float))
208:          .addMul(nvbs, sizeof(SkPathVerb));
209: 
210:     if (auto size = accum.total()) {
211:         // This trick allows us to just make one allocation, for us and our buffer
212:         // rather than allocating us and also allocating the buffer (via malloc or new[])
213:         // We have the corresponding operator delete() specified as well.
214:         void* storage = ::operator new (*size);
215:         sk_sp<SkPathData> path(new (storage) SkPathData(npts, nvbs, ncns));
216: 
217:         return path;
218:     }
219:     return nullptr;
220: }

222: bool SkPathData::finishInit(std::optional<SkRect> bounds, std::optional<uint8_t> segmentMask) {
223:     SkASSERT(valid_path_data(fPoints, fVerbs, fConics));
224: 
225:     if (fPoints.empty()) {
226:         fBounds = SkRect::MakeEmpty();
227:         fSegmentMask = 0;
228:         return true;
229:     }
230: 
231:     if (segmentMask.has_value()) {
232:         fSegmentMask = segmentMask.value();
233:     } else {
234:         fSegmentMask = SkPathPriv::ComputeSegmentMask(fVerbs);
235:     }
236: 
237:     if (bounds.has_value()) {
238:         fBounds = bounds.value().makeSorted();
239:         SkASSERT(SkIsFinite(&fPoints.data()->fX, fPoints.size() * 2));
240:     } else {
241:         if (auto r = SkPathPriv::TrimmedBounds(fPoints, fVerbs)) {
242:             fBounds = r.value();
243:         } else {
244:             report_pathdata_make_failure("non-finite bounds");
245:             return false;
246:         }
247:     }
248: 
249:     SkASSERT(fBounds.isSorted());
250:     return true;
251: }

253: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::MakeTransform(const SkPathRaw& src, const SkMatrix& mx) {
254:     if (src.empty()) {
255:         return SkPathData::Empty();
256:     }
257: 
258:     if (mx.hasPerspective()) {
259:         return SkPathBuilder()
260:             .addRaw(src, SkPathBuilder::Reserve::kExact)
261:             .transform(mx)
262:             .detachData();
263:     }
264: 
265:     // Allocate our result, so we can map the new points directly into it
266:     auto result = Alloc(src.points().size(), src.verbs().size(), src.conics().size());
267:     mx.mapPoints(result->fPoints, src.points());
268:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(result->fConics, src.conics());
269:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(result->fVerbs,  src.verbs());
270: 
271:     std::optional<SkRect> transformedBounds;
272:     if (mx.rectStaysRect()) {
273:         // safe us from having to compute our transformed bounds in finishInit()
274:         transformedBounds = mx.mapRect(src.bounds());
275:         if (!transformedBounds.value().isFinite()) {
276:             report_pathdata_make_failure("transform created non-finite bounds");
277:             return nullptr;
278:         }
279:     }
280: 
281:     if (!result->finishInit(transformedBounds, src.fSegmentMask)) {
282:         return nullptr;
283:     }
284: 
285:     result->setConvexity(SkPathPriv::TransformConvexity(mx, src.fPoints, src.fConvexity));
286: 
287:     return result;
288: }

290: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::makeTransform(const SkMatrix& mx) const {
291:     if (mx.isIdentity()) {
292:         return sk_ref_sp(this);
293:     }
294: 
295:     // not important for transform, just need a value
296:     const SkPathFillType ft = SkPathFillType::kDefault;
297: 
298:     auto result = MakeTransform(this->raw(ft, SkResolveConvexity::kNo), mx);
299: 
300:     if (!result) {
301:         return nullptr;
302:     }
303: 
304:     if (fType == SkPathIsAType::kGeneral) {
305:         return result;
306:     }
307: 
308:     // See if we can maintain our IsA status ...
309:     bool canMaintainIsA =
310:             mx.rectStaysRect() && SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(fPoints) && !result->bounds().isEmpty();
311:     if (!canMaintainIsA) {
312:         return result;
313:     }
314: 
315:     auto [dir, start] = SkPathPriv::TransformDirAndStart(
316:             mx, fType == SkPathIsAType::kRRect, fIsA.fDirection, fIsA.fStartIndex);
317:     result->setupIsA(fType, dir, start);
318:     return result;
319: }

406: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Polygon(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, bool isClosed) {
407:     if (pts.size() == 0 || (pts.size() == 1 && !isClosed)) {
408:         return Empty();
409:     }
410: 
411:     const size_t nverbs = pts.size() + isClosed;    // +1 for the kClose verb
412:     const size_t nconics = 0;
413:     auto path = Alloc(pts.size(), nverbs, nconics);
414: 
415:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(path->fPoints, pts);
416: 
417:     path->fVerbs[0] = SkPathVerb::kMove;
418:     for (size_t i = 1; i < pts.size(); ++i) {
419:         path->fVerbs[i] = SkPathVerb::kLine;
420:     }
421:     if (isClosed) {
422:         path->fVerbs.back() = SkPathVerb::kClose;
423:     }
424: 
425:     return path->finishInit({}, kLine_SkPathSegmentMask) ? path : nullptr;
426: }

37:  Determines if path is a rect by keeping track of changes in direction

40:  The direction is computed such that:

42:   1: horizontal left
43:   2: vertical down

45: 
46: A rectangle cycles up/right/down/left or up/left/down/right.
47: 
48: The test fails if:
49:   The path is closed, and followed by a line.
50:   A second move creates a new endpoint.
51:   A diagonal line is parsed.
52:   There's more than four changes of direction.
53:   There's a discontinuity on the line (e.g., a move in the middle)

55:   The path contains a quadratic or cubic.
56:   The path contains fewer than four points.
57:  *The rectangle doesn't complete a cycle.

59: 
60:   *These last two conditions we relax if we have a 3-edge path that would
61:    form a rectangle if it were closed (as we do when we fill a path)

63: It's OK if the path has:
64:   Several colinear line segments composing a rectangle side.

291:     return {{
292:         bounds(firstCorner, thirdCorner),
293:         autoClose,
294:         directions[0] == ((directions[1] + 1) & 3) ? SkPathDirection::kCW
295:                                                    : SkPathDirection::kCCW,
296:         savePts ? size_t(savePts - ptSpan.data()) : 0,
297:         currVerb,
298:     }};
299: }
300: 
301: bool SkPathPriv::IsNestedFillRects(const SkPathRaw& raw, SkRect rects[2], SkPathDirection dirs[2]) {
302:     SkPathDirection testDirs[2];
303:     SkRect testRects[2];
304: 
305:     SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts = raw.points();
306:     SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs = raw.verbs();
307: 
308:     auto rc = IsRectContour(pts, vbs, raw.fSegmentMask, true);
309:     if (!rc) {
310:         return false;
311:     }
312: 
313:     testDirs[0] = rc->fDirection;
314:     testRects[0] = rc->fRect;
315:     pts = pts.subspan(rc->fPointsConsumed);
316:     vbs = vbs.subspan(rc->fVerbsConsumed);
317: 
318:     rc = IsRectContour(pts, vbs, raw.fSegmentMask, false);
319:     if (rc) {
320:         testDirs[1] = rc->fDirection;
321:         testRects[1] = rc->fRect;
322:         if (testRects[0].contains(testRects[1])) {
323:             if (rects) {
324:                 rects[0] = testRects[0];
325:                 rects[1] = testRects[1];
326:             }
327:             if (dirs) {
328:                 dirs[0] = testDirs[0];
329:                 dirs[1] = testDirs[1];
330:             }
331:             return true;
332:         }
333:         if (testRects[1].contains(testRects[0])) {
334:             if (rects) {
335:                 rects[0] = testRects[1];
336:                 rects[1] = testRects[0];
337:             }
338:             if (dirs) {
339:                 dirs[0] = testDirs[1];
340:                 dirs[1] = testDirs[0];
341:             }
342:             return true;
343:         }
344:     }
345:     return false;
346: }
347: 
348: bool SkPathPriv::DrawArcIsConvex(SkScalar sweepAngle,
349:                                  SkArc::Type arcType,
350:                                  bool isFillNoPathEffect) {
351:     if (isFillNoPathEffect && SkScalarAbs(sweepAngle) >= 360.f) {
352:         // This gets converted to an oval.
353:         return true;
354:     }
355:     if (arcType == SkArc::Type::kWedge) {
356:         // This is a pie wedge. It's convex if the angle is <= 180.
357:         return SkScalarAbs(sweepAngle) <= 180.f;
358:     }
359:     // When the angle exceeds 360 this wraps back on top of itself. Otherwise it is a circle clipped
360:     // to a secant, i.e. convex.
361:     return SkScalarAbs(sweepAngle) <= 360.f;
362: }
363: 
364: SkPath SkPathPriv::CreateDrawArcPath(const SkArc& arc, bool isFillNoPathEffect) {
365:     SkRect oval = arc.fOval;
366:     SkScalar startAngle = arc.fStartAngle, sweepAngle = arc.fSweepAngle;
367:     SkASSERT(!oval.isEmpty());
368:     SkASSERT(sweepAngle);
369:     // We cap the number of total rotations. This keeps the resulting paths simpler. More important,
370:     // it prevents values so large that the loops below never terminate (once ULP > 360).
371:     if (SkScalarAbs(sweepAngle) > 3600.0f) {
372:         sweepAngle = std::copysign(3600.0f, sweepAngle) + std::fmod(sweepAngle, 360.0f);
373:     }
374: 
375:     SkPathBuilder builder(SkPathFillType::kWinding);
376:     builder.setIsVolatile(true);
377: 
378:     if (isFillNoPathEffect && SkScalarAbs(sweepAngle) >= 360.f) {
379:         builder.addOval(oval);
380:         SkASSERT(DrawArcIsConvex(sweepAngle, SkArc::Type::kArc, isFillNoPathEffect));
381:         return builder.detach();
382:     }
383: 
384:     if (arc.isWedge()) {
385:         builder.moveTo(oval.centerX(), oval.centerY());
386:     }
387:     auto firstDir =
388:             sweepAngle > 0 ? SkPathFirstDirection::kCW : SkPathFirstDirection::kCCW;
389:     bool convex = DrawArcIsConvex(sweepAngle, arc.fType, isFillNoPathEffect);
390:     // Arc to mods at 360 and drawArc is not supposed to.
391:     bool forceMoveTo = !arc.isWedge();
392:     while (sweepAngle <= -360.f) {
393:         builder.arcTo(oval, startAngle, -180.f, forceMoveTo);
394:         startAngle -= 180.f;
395:         builder.arcTo(oval, startAngle, -180.f, false);
396:         startAngle -= 180.f;
397:         forceMoveTo = false;
398:         sweepAngle += 360.f;
399:     }
400:     while (sweepAngle >= 360.f) {
401:         builder.arcTo(oval, startAngle, 180.f, forceMoveTo);
402:         startAngle += 180.f;
403:         builder.arcTo(oval, startAngle, 180.f, false);
404:         startAngle += 180.f;
405:         forceMoveTo = false;
406:         sweepAngle -= 360.f;
407:     }
408:     builder.arcTo(oval, startAngle, sweepAngle, forceMoveTo);
409:     if (arc.isWedge()) {
410:         builder.close();
411:     }
412: 
413:     auto path = builder.detach();
414:     const auto convexity = convex ? SkPathFirstDirection_ToConvexity(firstDir)
415:                                   : SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
416:     path.setConvexity(convexity);
417:     return path;
418: }
419: 
420: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
421: 
422: static int sign(SkScalar x) { return x < 0; }
423: #define kValueNeverReturnedBySign   2
424: 
425: enum DirChange {
426:     kUnknown_DirChange,
427:     kLeft_DirChange,
428:     kRight_DirChange,
429:     kStraight_DirChange,
430:     kBackwards_DirChange, // if double back, allow simple lines to be convex
431:     kInvalid_DirChange
432: };
433: 
434: // only valid for a single contour
435: struct Convexicator {
436: 
437:     /** The direction returned is only valid if the path is determined convex */
438:     SkPathFirstDirection getFirstDirection() const { return fFirstDirection; }
439: 
440:     void setMovePt(const SkPoint& pt) {
441:         fFirstPt = fLastPt = pt;
442:         fExpectedDir = kInvalid_DirChange;
443:     }
444: 
445:     bool addPt(const SkPoint& pt) {
446:         if (fLastPt == pt) {
447:             return true;
448:         }
449:         // should only be true for first non-zero vector after setMovePt was called. It is possible
450:         // we doubled backed at the start so need to check if fLastVec is zero or not.
451:         if (fFirstPt == fLastPt && fExpectedDir == kInvalid_DirChange && fLastVec.equals(0,0)) {
452:             fLastVec = pt - fLastPt;
453:             fFirstVec = fLastVec;
454:         } else if (!this->addVec(pt - fLastPt)) {
455:             return false;
456:         }
457:         fLastPt = pt;
458:         return true;
459:     }
460: 
461:     static bool IsConcaveBySign(const SkPoint points[], int count) {
462:         if (count <= 3) {
463:             // point, line, or triangle are always convex
464:             return false;
465:         }
466: 
467:         const SkPoint* last = points + count;
468:         SkPoint currPt = *points++;
469:         SkPoint firstPt = currPt;
470:         int dxes = 0;
471:         int dyes = 0;
472:         int lastSx = kValueNeverReturnedBySign;
473:         int lastSy = kValueNeverReturnedBySign;
474:         for (int outerLoop = 0; outerLoop < 2; ++outerLoop ) {
475:             while (points != last) {
476:                 SkVector vec = *points - currPt;
477:                 if (!vec.isZero()) {
478:                     // give up if vector construction failed
479:                     if (!vec.isFinite()) {
480:                         return true;    // treat as concave
481:                     }
482:                     int sx = sign(vec.fX);
483:                     int sy = sign(vec.fY);
484:                     dxes += (sx != lastSx);
485:                     dyes += (sy != lastSy);
486:                     if (dxes > 3 || dyes > 3) {
487:                         return true;
488:                     }
489:                     lastSx = sx;
490:                     lastSy = sy;
491:                 }
492:                 currPt = *points++;
493:                 if (outerLoop) {
494:                     break;
495:                 }
496:             }
497:             points = &firstPt;
498:         }
499:         return false;  // that is, it may be convex, don't know yet
500:     }
501: 
502:     bool close() {
503:         // If this was an explicit close, there was already a lineTo to fFirstPoint, so this
504:         // addPt() is a no-op. Otherwise, the addPt implicitly closes the contour. In either case,
505:         // we have to check the direction change along the first vector in case it is concave.
506:         return this->addPt(fFirstPt) && this->addVec(fFirstVec);
507:     }
508: 
509:     bool isFinite() const {
510:         return fIsFinite;
511:     }
512: 
513:     int reversals() const {
514:         return fReversals;
515:     }
516: 
517: private:
518:     DirChange directionChange(const SkVector& curVec) {
519:         SkScalar cross = SkPoint::CrossProduct(fLastVec, curVec);
520:         if (!SkIsFinite(cross)) {
521:             return kUnknown_DirChange;
522:         }
523:         if (cross == 0) {
524:             return fLastVec.dot(curVec) < 0 ? kBackwards_DirChange : kStraight_DirChange;
525:         }
526:         return 1 == SkScalarSignAsInt(cross) ? kRight_DirChange : kLeft_DirChange;
527:     }
528: 
529:     bool addVec(const SkVector& curVec) {
530:         DirChange dir = this->directionChange(curVec);
531:         switch (dir) {
532:             case kLeft_DirChange:       // fall through
533:             case kRight_DirChange:
534:                 if (kInvalid_DirChange == fExpectedDir) {
535:                     fExpectedDir = dir;
536:                     fFirstDirection = (kRight_DirChange == dir) ? SkPathFirstDirection::kCW
537:                                                                 : SkPathFirstDirection::kCCW;
538:                 } else if (dir != fExpectedDir) {
539:                     fFirstDirection = SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown;
540:                     return false;
541:                 }
542:                 fLastVec = curVec;
543:                 break;
544:             case kStraight_DirChange:
545:                 break;
546:             case kBackwards_DirChange:
547:                 //  allow path to reverse direction twice
548:                 //    Given path.moveTo(0, 0); path.lineTo(1, 1);
549:                 //    - 1st reversal: direction change formed by line (0,0 1,1), line (1,1 0,0)
550:                 //    - 2nd reversal: direction change formed by line (1,1 0,0), line (0,0 1,1)
551:                 fLastVec = curVec;
552:                 return ++fReversals < 3;
553:             case kUnknown_DirChange:
554:                 return (fIsFinite = false);
555:             case kInvalid_DirChange:
556:                 SK_ABORT("Use of invalid direction change flag");
557:                 break;
558:         }
559:         return true;
560:     }
561: 
562:     SkPoint              fFirstPt {0, 0};  // The first point of the contour, e.g. moveTo(x,y)
563:     SkVector             fFirstVec {0, 0}; // The direction leaving fFirstPt to the next vertex
564: 
565:     SkPoint              fLastPt {0, 0};   // The last point passed to addPt()
566:     SkVector             fLastVec {0, 0};  // The direction that brought the path to fLastPt
567: 
568:     DirChange            fExpectedDir { kInvalid_DirChange };
569:     SkPathFirstDirection fFirstDirection { SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown };
570:     int                  fReversals { 0 };
571:     bool                 fIsFinite { true };
572: };
573: 
574: static void trim_trailing_moves(SkSpan<const SkPoint>& pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb>& vbs) {
575:     size_t vbCount = vbs.size();
576:     while (vbCount > 0 && vbs[vbCount - 1] == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
577:         vbCount -= 1;
578:     }
579:     if (size_t delta = vbs.size() - vbCount) {
580:         SkASSERT(pts.size() >= delta);
581:         pts = {pts.data(), pts.size() - delta};
582:         vbs = {vbs.data(), vbs.size() - delta};
583:     }
584: }
585: 
586: SkPathConvexity SkPathPriv::ComputeConvexity(SkSpan<const SkPoint> points,
587:                                              SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
588:                                              SkSpan<const float> conicWeights) {
589:     // callers need to give us finite values
590:     SkASSERT(SkRect::Bounds(points).has_value());
591: 
592:     trim_trailing_moves(points, vbs);
593: 
594:     if (vbs.empty()) {
595:         return SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate;
596:     }
597: 
598:     // Check to see if path changes direction more than three times as quick concave test
599:     if (Convexicator::IsConcaveBySign(points.data(), points.size())) {
600:         return SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
601:     }
602: 
603:     int contourCount = 0;
604:     bool needsClose = false;
605:     Convexicator state;
606: 
607:     auto iter = SkPathIter(points, vbs, conicWeights);
608:     while (auto rec = iter.next()) {
609:         auto verb = rec->fVerb;
610:         auto pts = rec->fPoints;
611: 
612:         // Looking for the last moveTo before non-move verbs start
613:         if (contourCount == 0) {
614:             if (verb == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
615:                 state.setMovePt(pts[0]);
616:             } else {
617:                 // Starting the actual contour, fall through to c=1 to add the points
618:                 contourCount++;
619:                 needsClose = true;
620:             }
621:         }
622:         // Accumulating points into the Convexicator until we hit a close or another move
623:         if (contourCount == 1) {
624:             if (verb == SkPathVerb::kClose || verb == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
625:                 if (!state.close()) {
626:                     return SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
627:                 }
628:                 needsClose = false;
629:                 contourCount++;
630:             } else {
631:                 // lines add 1 point, cubics add 3, conics and quads add 2
632:                 int count = SkPathPriv::PtsInVerb((unsigned) verb);
633:                 SkASSERT(count > 0);
634:                 for (int i = 1; i <= count; ++i) {
635:                     if (!state.addPt(pts[i])) {
636:                         return SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
637:                     }
638:                 }
639:             }
640:         } else {
641:             // The first contour has closed and anything other than spurious trailing moves means
642:             // there's multiple contours and the path can't be convex
643:             if (verb != SkPathVerb::kMove) {
644:                 return SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
645:             }
646:         }
647:     }
648: 
649:     // If the path isn't explicitly closed do so implicitly
650:     if (needsClose && !state.close()) {
651:         return SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
652:     }
653: 
654:     const auto firstDir = state.getFirstDirection();
655:     if (firstDir == SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown && state.reversals() >= 3) {
656:         return SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
657:     }
658:     return SkPathFirstDirection_ToConvexity(firstDir);
659: }
660: 
661: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
662: 
663: // returns cross product of (p1 - p0) and (p2 - p0)
664: static SkScalar cross_prod(const SkPoint& p0, const SkPoint& p1, const SkPoint& p2) {
665:     SkScalar cross = SkPoint::CrossProduct(p1 - p0, p2 - p0);
666:     // We may get 0 when the above subtracts underflow. We expect this to be
667:     // very rare and lazily promote to double.
668:     if (0 == cross) {
669:         double p0x = SkScalarToDouble(p0.fX);
670:         double p0y = SkScalarToDouble(p0.fY);
671: 
672:         double p1x = SkScalarToDouble(p1.fX);
673:         double p1y = SkScalarToDouble(p1.fY);
674: 
675:         double p2x = SkScalarToDouble(p2.fX);
676:         double p2y = SkScalarToDouble(p2.fY);
677: 
678:         cross = SkDoubleToScalar((p1x - p0x) * (p2y - p0y) -
679:                                  (p1y - p0y) * (p2x - p0x));
680: 
681:     }
682:     return cross;
683: }
684: 
685: // Returns the first pt with the maximum Y coordinate
686: static int find_max_y(const SkPoint pts[], int count) {
687:     SkASSERT(count > 0);
688:     SkScalar max = pts[0].fY;
689:     int firstIndex = 0;
690:     for (int i = 1; i < count; ++i) {
691:         SkScalar y = pts[i].fY;
692:         if (y > max) {
693:             max = y;
694:             firstIndex = i;
695:         }
696:     }
697:     return firstIndex;
698: }
699: 
700: static int find_diff_pt(const SkPoint pts[], int index, int n, int inc) {
701:     int i = index;
702:     for (;;) {
703:         i = (i + inc) % n;
704:         if (i == index) {   // we wrapped around, so abort
705:             break;
706:         }
707:         if (pts[index] != pts[i]) { // found a different point, success!
708:             break;
709:         }
710:     }
711:     return i;
712: }
713: 
714: /**
715:  *  Starting at index, and moving forward (incrementing), find the xmin and
716:  *  xmax of the contiguous points that have the same Y.
717:  */
718: static int find_min_max_x_at_y(const SkPoint pts[], int index, int n,
719:                                int* maxIndexPtr) {
720:     const SkScalar y = pts[index].fY;
721:     SkScalar min = pts[index].fX;
722:     SkScalar max = min;
723:     int minIndex = index;
724:     int maxIndex = index;
725:     for (int i = index + 1; i < n; ++i) {
726:         if (pts[i].fY != y) {
727:             break;
728:         }
729:         SkScalar x = pts[i].fX;
730:         if (x < min) {
731:             min = x;
732:             minIndex = i;
733:         } else if (x > max) {
734:             max = x;
735:             maxIndex = i;
736:         }
737:     }
738:     *maxIndexPtr = maxIndex;
739:     return minIndex;
740: }
741: 
742: static SkPathFirstDirection crossToDir(SkScalar cross) {
743:     return cross > 0 ? SkPathFirstDirection::kCW : SkPathFirstDirection::kCCW;
744: }
745: 
746: class ContourIter {
747: public:
748:     ContourIter(SkSpan<const SkPoint>, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb>, SkSpan<const float> conicWeights);
749: 
750:     bool done() const { return fDone; }
751:     // if !done() then these may be called
752:     int count() const { return fCurrPtCount; }
753:     const SkPoint* pts() const { return fCurrPt; }
754:     void next();
755: 
756: private:
757:     int fCurrPtCount;
758:     const SkPoint* fCurrPt;
759:     const SkPathVerb* fCurrVerb;
760:     const SkPathVerb* fStopVerbs;
761:     const SkScalar* fCurrConicWeight;
762:     bool fDone;
763:     SkDEBUGCODE(int fContourCounter;)
764: };
765: 
766: ContourIter::ContourIter(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
767:                          SkSpan<const float> conicWeights) {
768:     fStopVerbs = vbs.data() + vbs.size();
769:     fDone = false;
770:     fCurrPt = pts.data();
771:     fCurrVerb = vbs.data();
772:     fCurrConicWeight = conicWeights.data();
773:     fCurrPtCount = 0;
774:     SkDEBUGCODE(fContourCounter = 0;)
775:     this->next();
776: }
777: 
778: void ContourIter::next() {
779:     if (fCurrVerb >= fStopVerbs) {
780:         fDone = true;
781:     }
782:     if (fDone) {
783:         return;
784:     }
785: 
786:     // skip pts of prev contour
787:     fCurrPt += fCurrPtCount;
788: 
789:     SkASSERT(SkPathVerb::kMove == fCurrVerb[0]);
790:     int ptCount = 1;    // moveTo
791:     const SkPathVerb* verbs = fCurrVerb;
792: 
793:     for (verbs++; verbs < fStopVerbs; verbs++) {
794:         switch (*verbs) {
795:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:
796:                 goto CONTOUR_END;
797:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:
798:                 ptCount += 1;
799:                 break;
800:             case SkPathVerb::kConic:
801:                 fCurrConicWeight += 1;
802:                 [[fallthrough]];
803:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
804:                 ptCount += 2;
805:                 break;
806:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
807:                 ptCount += 3;
808:                 break;
809:             case SkPathVerb::kClose:
810:                 break;
811:         }
812:     }
813: CONTOUR_END:
814:     fCurrPtCount = ptCount;
815:     fCurrVerb = verbs;
816:     SkDEBUGCODE(++fContourCounter;)
817: }
818: 
819: /*
820:  *  We loop through all contours, and keep the computed cross-product of the
821:  *  contour that contained the global y-max. If we just look at the first
822:  *  contour, we may find one that is wound the opposite way (correctly) since
823:  *  it is the interior of a hole (e.g. 'o'). Thus we must find the contour
824:  *  that is outer most (or at least has the global y-max) before we can consider
825:  *  its cross product.
826:  */
827: SkPathFirstDirection SkPathPriv::ComputeFirstDirection(const SkPathRaw& raw) {
828:     ContourIter iter(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics());
829: 
830:     // initialize with our logical y-min
831:     SkScalar ymax = raw.bounds().fTop;
832:     SkScalar ymaxCross = 0;
833: 
834:     for (; !iter.done(); iter.next()) {
835:         int n = iter.count();
836:         if (n < 3) {
837:             continue;
838:         }
839: 
840:         const SkPoint* pts = iter.pts();
841:         SkScalar cross = 0;
842:         int index = find_max_y(pts, n);
843:         if (pts[index].fY < ymax) {
844:             continue;
845:         }
846: 
847:         // If there is more than 1 distinct point at the y-max, we take the
848:         // x-min and x-max of them and just subtract to compute the dir.
849:         if (pts[(index + 1) % n].fY == pts[index].fY) {
850:             int maxIndex;
851:             int minIndex = find_min_max_x_at_y(pts, index, n, &maxIndex);
852:             if (minIndex == maxIndex) {
853:                 goto TRY_CROSSPROD;
854:             }
855:             SkASSERT(pts[minIndex].fY == pts[index].fY);
856:             SkASSERT(pts[maxIndex].fY == pts[index].fY);
857:             SkASSERT(pts[minIndex].fX <= pts[maxIndex].fX);
858:             // we just subtract the indices, and let that auto-convert to
859:             // SkScalar, since we just want - or + to signal the direction.
860:             cross = minIndex - maxIndex;
861:         } else {
862:             TRY_CROSSPROD:
863:             // Find a next and prev index to use for the cross-product test,
864:             // but we try to find pts that form non-zero vectors from pts[index]
865:             //
866:             // Its possible that we can't find two non-degenerate vectors, so
867:             // we have to guard our search (e.g. all the pts could be in the
868:             // same place).
869: 
870:             // we pass n - 1 instead of -1 so we don't foul up % operator by
871:             // passing it a negative LH argument.
872:             int prev = find_diff_pt(pts, index, n, n - 1);
873:             if (prev == index) {
874:                 // completely degenerate, skip to next contour
875:                 continue;
876:             }
877:             int next = find_diff_pt(pts, index, n, 1);
878:             SkASSERT(next != index);
879:             cross = cross_prod(pts[prev], pts[index], pts[next]);
880:             // if we get a zero and the points are horizontal, then we look at the spread in
881:             // x-direction. We really should continue to walk away from the degeneracy until
882:             // there is a divergence.
883:             if (0 == cross && pts[prev].fY == pts[index].fY && pts[next].fY == pts[index].fY) {
884:                 // construct the subtract so we get the correct Direction below
885:                 cross = pts[index].fX - pts[next].fX;
886:             }
887:         }
888: 
889:         if (cross) {
890:             // record our best guess so far
891:             ymax = pts[index].fY;
892:             ymaxCross = cross;
893:         }
894:     }
895: 
896:     return ymaxCross ? crossToDir(ymaxCross) : SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown;
897: }
898: 
899: //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
900: 
901: static float poly_eval(float A, float B, float C, float t) {
902:     return (A * t + B) * t + C;
903: }
904: 
905: static float poly_eval(float A, float B, float C, float D, float t) {
906:     return ((A * t + B) * t + C) * t + D;
907: }
908: 
909: static bool between(SkScalar a, SkScalar b, SkScalar c) {
910:     SkASSERT(((a <= b && b <= c) || (a >= b && b >= c)) == ((a - b) * (c - b) <= 0)
911:             || (SkScalarNearlyZero(a) && SkScalarNearlyZero(b) && SkScalarNearlyZero(c)));
912:     return (a - b) * (c - b) <= 0;
913: }
914: 
915: static SkScalar eval_cubic_pts(SkScalar c0, SkScalar c1, SkScalar c2, SkScalar c3,
916:                                SkScalar t) {
917:     SkScalar A = c3 + 3*(c1 - c2) - c0;
918:     SkScalar B = 3*(c2 - c1 - c1 + c0);
919:     SkScalar C = 3*(c1 - c0);
920:     SkScalar D = c0;
921:     return poly_eval(A, B, C, D, t);
922: }
923: 
924: template <size_t N> static void find_minmax(const SkPoint pts[],
925:                                             SkScalar* minPtr, SkScalar* maxPtr) {
926:     SkScalar min, max;
927:     min = max = pts[0].fX;
928:     for (size_t i = 1; i < N; ++i) {
929:         min = std::min(min, pts[i].fX);
930:         max = std::max(max, pts[i].fX);
931:     }
932:     *minPtr = min;
933:     *maxPtr = max;
934: }
935: 
936: static bool checkOnCurve(SkScalar x, SkScalar y, const SkPoint& start, const SkPoint& end) {
937:     if (start.fY == end.fY) {
938:         return between(start.fX, x, end.fX) && x != end.fX;
939:     } else {
940:         return x == start.fX && y == start.fY;
941:     }
942: }
943: 
944: static int winding_mono_cubic(const SkPoint pts[], SkScalar x, SkScalar y, int* onCurveCount) {
945:     SkScalar y0 = pts[0].fY;
946:     SkScalar y3 = pts[3].fY;
947: 
948:     int dir = 1;
949:     if (y0 > y3) {
950:         using std::swap;
951:         swap(y0, y3);
952:         dir = -1;
953:     }
954:     if (y < y0 || y > y3) {
955:         return 0;
956:     }
957:     if (checkOnCurve(x, y, pts[0], pts[3])) {
958:         *onCurveCount += 1;
959:         return 0;
960:     }
961:     if (y == y3) {
962:         return 0;
963:     }
964: 
965:     // quickreject or quickaccept
966:     SkScalar min, max;
967:     find_minmax<4>(pts, &min, &max);
968:     if (x < min) {
969:         return 0;
970:     }
971:     if (x > max) {
972:         return dir;
973:     }
974: 
975:     // compute the actual x(t) value
976:     SkScalar t;
977:     if (!SkCubicClipper::ChopMonoAtY(pts, y, &t)) {
978:         return 0;
979:     }
980:     SkScalar xt = eval_cubic_pts(pts[0].fX, pts[1].fX, pts[2].fX, pts[3].fX, t);
981:     if (SkScalarNearlyEqual(xt, x)) {
982:         if (x != pts[3].fX || y != pts[3].fY) {  // don't test end points; they're start points
983:             *onCurveCount += 1;
984:             return 0;
985:         }
986:     }
987:     return xt < x ? dir : 0;
988: }
989: 
990: static int winding_cubic(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, int* onCurveCount) {
991:     std::array<SkPoint, 10> dst;
992:     int n = SkChopCubicAtYExtrema(pts.data(), dst.data());
993:     int w = 0;
994:     for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i) {
995:         w += winding_mono_cubic(&dst[i * 3], x, y, onCurveCount);
996:     }
997:     return w;
998: }
999: 
1000: static double conic_eval_numerator(const SkScalar src[], SkScalar w, SkScalar t) {
1001:     SkASSERT(src);
1002:     SkASSERT(t >= 0 && t <= 1);
1003:     SkScalar src2w = src[2] * w;
1004:     SkScalar C = src[0];
1005:     SkScalar A = src[4] - 2 * src2w + C;
1006:     SkScalar B = 2 * (src2w - C);
1007:     return poly_eval(A, B, C, t);
1008: }
1009: 
1010: 
1011: static double conic_eval_denominator(SkScalar w, SkScalar t) {
1012:     SkScalar B = 2 * (w - 1);
1013:     SkScalar C = 1;
1014:     SkScalar A = -B;
1015:     return poly_eval(A, B, C, t);
1016: }
1017: 
1018: static int winding_mono_conic(const SkConic& conic, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, int* onCurveCount) {
1019:     const SkPoint* pts = conic.fPts;
1020:     SkScalar y0 = pts[0].fY;
1021:     SkScalar y2 = pts[2].fY;
1022: 
1023:     int dir = 1;
1024:     if (y0 > y2) {
1025:         using std::swap;
1026:         swap(y0, y2);
1027:         dir = -1;
1028:     }
1029:     if (y < y0 || y > y2) {
1030:         return 0;
1031:     }
1032:     if (checkOnCurve(x, y, pts[0], pts[2])) {
1033:         *onCurveCount += 1;
1034:         return 0;
1035:     }
1036:     if (y == y2) {
1037:         return 0;
1038:     }
1039: 
1040:     SkScalar roots[2];
1041:     SkScalar A = pts[2].fY;
1042:     SkScalar B = pts[1].fY * conic.fW - y * conic.fW + y;
1043:     SkScalar C = pts[0].fY;
1044:     A += C - 2 * B;  // A = a + c - 2*(b*w - yCept*w + yCept)
1045:     B -= C;  // B = b*w - w * yCept + yCept - a
1046:     C -= y;
1047:     int n = SkFindUnitQuadRoots(A, 2 * B, C, roots);
1048:     SkASSERT(n <= 1);
1049:     SkScalar xt;
1050:     if (0 == n) {
1051:         // zero roots are returned only when y0 == y
1052:         // Need [0] if dir == 1
1053:         // and  [2] if dir == -1
1054:         xt = pts[1 - dir].fX;
1055:     } else {
1056:         SkScalar t = roots[0];
1057:         xt = conic_eval_numerator(&pts[0].fX, conic.fW, t) / conic_eval_denominator(conic.fW, t);
1058:     }
1059:     if (SkScalarNearlyEqual(xt, x)) {
1060:         if (x != pts[2].fX || y != pts[2].fY) {  // don't test end points; they're start points
1061:             *onCurveCount += 1;
1062:             return 0;
1063:         }
1064:     }
1065:     return xt < x ? dir : 0;
1066: }
1067: 
1068: static bool is_mono_quad(SkScalar y0, SkScalar y1, SkScalar y2) {
1069:     //    return SkScalarSignAsInt(y0 - y1) + SkScalarSignAsInt(y1 - y2) != 0;
1070:     if (y0 == y1) {
1071:         return true;
1072:     }
1073:     if (y0 < y1) {
1074:         return y1 <= y2;
1075:     } else {
1076:         return y1 >= y2;
1077:     }
1078: }
1079: 
1080: static int winding_conic(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, SkScalar weight,
1081:                          int* onCurveCount) {
1082:     SkConic conic(pts.data(), weight);
1083:     SkConic chopped[2];
1084:     // If the data points are very large, the conic may not be monotonic but may also
1085:     // fail to chop. Then, the chopper does not split the original conic in two.
1086:     bool isMono = is_mono_quad(pts[0].fY, pts[1].fY, pts[2].fY) || !conic.chopAtYExtrema(chopped);
1087:     int w = winding_mono_conic(isMono ? conic : chopped[0], x, y, onCurveCount);
1088:     if (!isMono) {
1089:         w += winding_mono_conic(chopped[1], x, y, onCurveCount);
1090:     }
1091:     return w;
1092: }
1093: 
1094: static int winding_mono_quad(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, int* onCurveCount) {
1095:     SkScalar y0 = pts[0].fY;
1096:     SkScalar y2 = pts[2].fY;
1097: 
1098:     int dir = 1;
1099:     if (y0 > y2) {
1100:         using std::swap;
1101:         swap(y0, y2);
1102:         dir = -1;
1103:     }
1104:     if (y < y0 || y > y2) {
1105:         return 0;
1106:     }
1107:     if (checkOnCurve(x, y, pts[0], pts[2])) {
1108:         *onCurveCount += 1;
1109:         return 0;
1110:     }
1111:     if (y == y2) {
1112:         return 0;
1113:     }
1114:     // bounds check on X (not required. is it faster?)
1115: #if 0
1116:     if (pts[0].fX > x && pts[1].fX > x && pts[2].fX > x) {
1117:         return 0;
1118:     }
1119: #endif
1120: 
1121:     SkScalar roots[2];
1122:     int n = SkFindUnitQuadRoots(pts[0].fY - 2 * pts[1].fY + pts[2].fY,
1123:                                 2 * (pts[1].fY - pts[0].fY),
1124:                                 pts[0].fY - y,
1125:                                 roots);
1126:     SkASSERT(n <= 1);
1127:     SkScalar xt;
1128:     if (0 == n) {
1129:         // zero roots are returned only when y0 == y
1130:         // Need [0] if dir == 1
1131:         // and  [2] if dir == -1
1132:         xt = pts[1 - dir].fX;
1133:     } else {
1134:         SkScalar t = roots[0];
1135:         SkScalar C = pts[0].fX;
1136:         SkScalar A = pts[2].fX - 2 * pts[1].fX + C;
1137:         SkScalar B = 2 * (pts[1].fX - C);
1138:         xt = poly_eval(A, B, C, t);
1139:     }
1140:     if (SkScalarNearlyEqual(xt, x)) {
1141:         if (x != pts[2].fX || y != pts[2].fY) {  // don't test end points; they're start points
1142:             *onCurveCount += 1;
1143:             return 0;
1144:         }
1145:     }
1146:     return xt < x ? dir : 0;
1147: }
1148: 
1149: static int winding_quad(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, int* onCurveCount) {
1150:     SkPoint               spanStorage[5];
1151:     SkSpan<const SkPoint> span = pts;
1152:     int                   n = 0;
1153: 
1154:     if (!is_mono_quad(pts[0].fY, pts[1].fY, pts[2].fY)) {
1155:         n = SkChopQuadAtYExtrema(pts.data(), spanStorage);
1156:         span = spanStorage;
1157:     }
1158:     int w = winding_mono_quad(span, x, y, onCurveCount);
1159:     if (n > 0) {
1160:         w += winding_mono_quad(span.subspan(2), x, y, onCurveCount);
1161:     }
1162:     return w;
1163: }
1164: 
1165: static int winding_line(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, int* onCurveCount) {
1166:     SkScalar x0 = pts[0].fX;
1167:     SkScalar y0 = pts[0].fY;
1168:     SkScalar x1 = pts[1].fX;
1169:     SkScalar y1 = pts[1].fY;
1170: 
1171:     SkScalar dy = y1 - y0;
1172: 
1173:     int dir = 1;
1174:     if (y0 > y1) {
1175:         using std::swap;
1176:         swap(y0, y1);
1177:         dir = -1;
1178:     }
1179:     if (y < y0 || y > y1) {
1180:         return 0;
1181:     }
1182:     if (checkOnCurve(x, y, pts[0], pts[1])) {
1183:         *onCurveCount += 1;
1184:         return 0;
1185:     }
1186:     if (y == y1) {
1187:         return 0;
1188:     }
1189:     SkScalar cross = (x1 - x0) * (y - pts[0].fY) - dy * (x - x0);
1190: 
1191:     if (!cross) {
1192:         // zero cross means the point is on the line, and since the case where
1193:         // y of the query point is at the end point is handled above, we can be
1194:         // sure that we're on the line (excluding the end point) here
1195:         if (x != x1 || y != pts[1].fY) {
1196:             *onCurveCount += 1;
1197:         }
1198:         dir = 0;
1199:     } else if (SkScalarSignAsInt(cross) == dir) {
1200:         dir = 0;
1201:     }
1202:     return dir;
1203: }
1204: 
1205: static void tangent_cubic(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y,
1206:                           SkTDArray<SkVector>* tangents) {
1207:     if (!between(pts[0].fY, y, pts[1].fY) && !between(pts[1].fY, y, pts[2].fY)
1208:              && !between(pts[2].fY, y, pts[3].fY)) {
1209:         return;
1210:     }
1211:     if (!between(pts[0].fX, x, pts[1].fX) && !between(pts[1].fX, x, pts[2].fX)
1212:              && !between(pts[2].fX, x, pts[3].fX)) {
1213:         return;
1214:     }
1215:     std::array<SkPoint, 10> dst;
1216:     int n = SkChopCubicAtYExtrema(pts.data(), dst.data());
1217:     for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i) {
1218:         SkPoint* c = &dst[i * 3];
1219:         SkScalar t;
1220:         if (!SkCubicClipper::ChopMonoAtY(c, y, &t)) {
1221:             continue;
1222:         }
1223:         SkScalar xt = eval_cubic_pts(c[0].fX, c[1].fX, c[2].fX, c[3].fX, t);
1224:         if (!SkScalarNearlyEqual(x, xt)) {
1225:             continue;
1226:         }
1227:         SkVector tangent;
1228:         SkEvalCubicAt(c, t, nullptr, &tangent, nullptr);
1229:         tangents->push_back(tangent);
1230:     }
1231: }
1232: 
1233: static void tangent_conic(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y, SkScalar w,
1234:                           SkTDArray<SkVector>* tangents) {
1235:     if (!between(pts[0].fY, y, pts[1].fY) && !between(pts[1].fY, y, pts[2].fY)) {
1236:         return;
1237:     }
1238:     if (!between(pts[0].fX, x, pts[1].fX) && !between(pts[1].fX, x, pts[2].fX)) {
1239:         return;
1240:     }
1241:     std::array<SkScalar, 2> roots;
1242:     SkScalar A = pts[2].fY;
1243:     SkScalar B = pts[1].fY * w - y * w + y;
1244:     SkScalar C = pts[0].fY;
1245:     A += C - 2 * B;  // A = a + c - 2*(b*w - yCept*w + yCept)
1246:     B -= C;  // B = b*w - w * yCept + yCept - a
1247:     C -= y;
1248:     int n = SkFindUnitQuadRoots(A, 2 * B, C, roots.data());
1249:     for (int index = 0; index < n; ++index) {
1250:         SkScalar t = roots[index];
1251:         SkScalar xt = conic_eval_numerator(&pts[0].fX, w, t) / conic_eval_denominator(w, t);
1252:         if (!SkScalarNearlyEqual(x, xt)) {
1253:             continue;
1254:         }
1255:         SkConic conic(pts.data(), w);
1256:         tangents->push_back(conic.evalTangentAt(t));
1257:     }
1258: }
1259: 
1260: static void tangent_quad(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y,
1261:                          SkTDArray<SkVector>* tangents) {
1262:     if (!between(pts[0].fY, y, pts[1].fY) && !between(pts[1].fY, y, pts[2].fY)) {
1263:         return;
1264:     }
1265:     if (!between(pts[0].fX, x, pts[1].fX) && !between(pts[1].fX, x, pts[2].fX)) {
1266:         return;
1267:     }
1268:     std::array<SkScalar, 2> roots;
1269:     int n = SkFindUnitQuadRoots(pts[0].fY - 2 * pts[1].fY + pts[2].fY,
1270:                                 2 * (pts[1].fY - pts[0].fY),
1271:                                 pts[0].fY - y,
1272:                                 roots.data());
1273:     for (int index = 0; index < n; ++index) {
1274:         SkScalar t = roots[index];
1275:         SkScalar C = pts[0].fX;
1276:         SkScalar A = pts[2].fX - 2 * pts[1].fX + C;
1277:         SkScalar B = 2 * (pts[1].fX - C);
1278:         SkScalar xt = poly_eval(A, B, C, t);
1279:         if (!SkScalarNearlyEqual(x, xt)) {
1280:             continue;
1281:         }
1282:         tangents->push_back(SkEvalQuadTangentAt(pts.data(), t));
1283:     }
1284: }
1285: 
1286: static void tangent_line(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y,
1287:                          SkTDArray<SkVector>* tangents) {
1288:     SkScalar y0 = pts[0].fY;
1289:     SkScalar y1 = pts[1].fY;
1290:     if (!between(y0, y, y1)) {
1291:         return;
1292:     }
1293:     SkScalar x0 = pts[0].fX;
1294:     SkScalar x1 = pts[1].fX;
1295:     if (!between(x0, x, x1)) {
1296:         return;
1297:     }
1298:     SkScalar dx = x1 - x0;
1299:     SkScalar dy = y1 - y0;
1300:     if (!SkScalarNearlyEqual((x - x0) * dy, dx * (y - y0))) {
1301:         return;
1302:     }
1303:     SkVector v;
1304:     v.set(dx, dy);
1305:     tangents->push_back(v);
1306: }
1307: 
1308: static bool contains_inclusive(const SkRect& r, SkPoint p) {
1309:     return r.fLeft <= p.fX && p.fX <= r.fRight && r.fTop <= p.fY && p.fY <= r.fBottom;
1310: }
1311: 
1312: bool SkPathPriv::Contains(const SkPathRaw& raw, SkPoint p) {
1313:     const SkPathFillType ft = raw.fillType();
1314:     const bool isInverse = SkPathFillType_IsInverse(ft);
1315:     if (raw.empty()) {
1316:         return isInverse;
1317:     }
1318: 
1319:     if (!contains_inclusive(raw.bounds(), p)) {
1320:         return isInverse;
1321:     }
1322: 
1323:     int w = 0;
1324:     int onCurveCount = 0;
1325: 
1326:     for (auto iter = SkPathEdgeIter(raw); auto rec = iter.next(); ) {
1327:         switch (rec.fEdge) {
1328:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kLine:
1329:                 w += winding_line({rec.fPts, 2}, p.fX, p.fY, &onCurveCount);
1330:                 break;
1331:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kQuad:
1332:                 w += winding_quad({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, &onCurveCount);
1333:                 break;
1334:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kConic:
1335:                 w += winding_conic({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, iter.conicWeight(), &onCurveCount);
1336:                 break;
1337:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kCubic:
1338:                 w += winding_cubic({rec.fPts, 4}, p.fX, p.fY, &onCurveCount);
1339:                 break;
1340:        }
1341:     }
1342:     bool evenOddFill = SkPathFillType::kEvenOdd        == ft
1343:                     || SkPathFillType::kInverseEvenOdd == ft;
1344:     if (evenOddFill) {
1345:         w &= 1;
1346:     }
1347:     if (w) {
1348:         return !isInverse;
1349:     }
1350:     if (onCurveCount <= 1) {
1351:         return SkToBool(onCurveCount) ^ isInverse;
1352:     }
1353:     if ((onCurveCount & 1) || evenOddFill) {
1354:         return SkToBool(onCurveCount & 1) ^ isInverse;
1355:     }
1356:     // If the point touches an even number of curves, and the fill is winding, check for
1357:     // coincidence. Count coincidence as places where the on curve points have identical tangents.
1358:     SkTDArray<SkVector> tangents;
1359:     for (auto iter = SkPathEdgeIter(raw); auto rec = iter.next(); ) {
1360:         int oldCount = tangents.size();
1361:         switch (rec.fEdge) {
1362:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kLine:
1363:                 tangent_line({rec.fPts, 2}, p.fX, p.fY, &tangents);
1364:                 break;
1365:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kQuad:
1366:                 tangent_quad({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, &tangents);
1367:                 break;
1368:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kConic:
1369:                 tangent_conic({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, iter.conicWeight(), &tangents);
1370:                 break;
1371:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kCubic:
1372:                 tangent_cubic({rec.fPts, 4}, p.fX, p.fY, &tangents);
1373:                 break;
1374:        }
1375:        if (tangents.size() > oldCount) {
1376:             int last = tangents.size() - 1;
1377:             const SkVector& tangent = tangents[last];
1378:             if (SkScalarNearlyZero(SkPointPriv::LengthSqd(tangent))) {
1379:                 tangents.remove(last);
1380:             } else {
1381:                 for (int index = 0; index < last; ++index) {
1382:                     const SkVector& test = tangents[index];
1383:                     if (SkScalarNearlyZero(test.cross(tangent))
1384:                             && SkScalarSignAsInt(tangent.fX * test.fX) <= 0
1385:                             && SkScalarSignAsInt(tangent.fY * test.fY) <= 0) {
1386:                         tangents.remove(last);
1387:                         tangents.removeShuffle(index);
1388:                         break;
1389:                     }
1390:                 }
1391:             }
1392:         }
1393:     }
1394:     return SkToBool(tangents.size()) ^ isInverse;
1395: }

1398: 
1399: bool SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts) {
1400:     // Conservative (quick) test to see if all segments are axis-aligned.

1430:                 matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMSkewX)  * matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMSkewY);

pub struct SkConic {
    pub pts: [Point; 3],
    pub w: Scalar,
}

pub type Conic = SkConic;

impl Default for SkConic {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            pts: [Point::default(); 3],
            w: 1.0,
        }
    }
}

impl SkConic {
    pub fn new(p0: Point, p1: Point, p2: Point, w: Scalar) -> Self {
        let mut conic = Self {
            pts: [p0, p1, p2],
            w: 1.0,
        };
        conic.set_w(w);
        conic
    }

    pub fn from_pts(pts: &[Point], w: Scalar) -> Self {
        let mut conic = Self {
            pts: [pts[0], pts[1], pts[2]],
            w: 1.0,
        };
        conic.set_w(w);
        conic
    }

    pub fn set(&mut self, pts: &[Point], w: Scalar) {
        self.pts = [pts[0], pts[1], pts[2]];
        self.set_w(w);
    }

    pub fn set_pts_w(&mut self, p0: Point, p1: Point, p2: Point, w: Scalar) {
        self.pts = [p0, p1, p2];
        self.set_w(w);
    }

    /// Guard against bad weights by forcing them to 1.
    pub fn set_w(&mut self, w: Scalar) {
        self.w = if w > 0.0 && is_finite(w) { w } else { 1.0 };
    }

    pub fn eval_at(&self, t: Scalar) -> Point {
        ConicCoeff::new(self).eval(t)
    }

    pub fn eval_at_with(&self, t: Scalar, pt: Option<&mut Point>, tangent: Option<&mut Vector>) {
        debug_assert!((0.0..=1.0).contains(&t));

        if let Some(pt) = pt {
            *pt = self.eval_at(t);
        }
        if let Some(tangent) = tangent {
            *tangent = self.eval_tangent_at(t);
        }
    }

    pub fn eval_tangent_at(&self, t: Scalar) -> Vector {
        // The derivative equation returns a zero tangent vector when t is 0 or 1,
        // and the control point is equal to the end point.
        // In this case, use the conic endpoints to compute the tangent.
        if (t == 0.0 && self.pts[0] == self.pts[1]) || (t == 1.0 && self.pts[1] == self.pts[2]) {
            return self.pts[2] - self.pts[0];
        }

574: static void trim_trailing_moves(SkSpan<const SkPoint>& pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb>& vbs) {

586: SkPathConvexity SkPathPriv::ComputeConvexity(SkSpan<const SkPoint> points,
587:                                              SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
588:                                              SkSpan<const float> conicWeights) {

598:     // Check to see if path changes direction more than three times as quick concave test
599:     if (Convexicator::IsConcaveBySign(points.data(), points.size())) {

603:     int contourCount = 0;

607:     auto iter = SkPathIter(points, vbs, conicWeights);

618:                 contourCount++;

621:         }
622:         // Accumulating points into the Convexicator until we hit a close or another move
623:         if (contourCount == 1) {
624:             if (verb == SkPathVerb::kClose || verb == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
625:                 if (!state.close()) {
626:                     return SkPathConvexity::kConcave;
627:                 }
628:                 needsClose = false;
629:                 contourCount++;
630:             } else {
631:                 // lines add 1 point, cubics add 3, conics and quads add 2
632:                 int count = SkPathPriv::PtsInVerb((unsigned) verb);
633:                 SkASSERT(count > 0);
634:                 for (int i = 1; i <= count; ++i) {

664: static SkScalar cross_prod(const SkPoint& p0, const SkPoint& p1, const SkPoint& p2) {
665:     SkScalar cross = SkPoint::CrossProduct(p1 - p0, p2 - p0);
666:     // We may get 0 when the above subtracts underflow. We expect this to be
667:     // very rare and lazily promote to double.

677: 
678:         cross = SkDoubleToScalar((p1x - p0x) * (p2y - p0y) -
679:                                  (p1y - p0y) * (p2x - p0x));

681:     }
682:     return cross;
683: }

720:     const SkScalar y = pts[index].fY;
721:     SkScalar min = pts[index].fX;
722:     SkScalar max = min;
723:     int minIndex = index;
724:     int maxIndex = index;
725:     for (int i = index + 1; i < n; ++i) {
726:         if (pts[i].fY != y) {
727:             break;
728:         }
729:         SkScalar x = pts[i].fX;
730:         if (x < min) {
731:             min = x;
732:             minIndex = i;
733:         } else if (x > max) {
734:             max = x;
735:             maxIndex = i;
736:         }
737:     }
738:     *maxIndexPtr = maxIndex;
739:     return minIndex;
740: }

747: public:

749: 
750:     bool done() const { return fDone; }
751:     // if !done() then these may be called
752:     int count() const { return fCurrPtCount; }
753:     const SkPoint* pts() const { return fCurrPt; }

756: private:
757:     int fCurrPtCount;
758:     const SkPoint* fCurrPt;
759:     const SkPathVerb* fCurrVerb;
760:     const SkPathVerb* fStopVerbs;
761:     const SkScalar* fCurrConicWeight;

763:     SkDEBUGCODE(int fContourCounter;)
764: };
765: 
766: ContourIter::ContourIter(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
767:                          SkSpan<const float> conicWeights) {
768:     fStopVerbs = vbs.data() + vbs.size();
769:     fDone = false;
770:     fCurrPt = pts.data();
771:     fCurrVerb = vbs.data();
772:     fCurrConicWeight = conicWeights.data();
773:     fCurrPtCount = 0;
774:     SkDEBUGCODE(fContourCounter = 0;)
775:     this->next();
776: }
777: 
778: void ContourIter::next() {
779:     if (fCurrVerb >= fStopVerbs) {
780:         fDone = true;
781:     }
782:     if (fDone) {
783:         return;
784:     }
785: 
786:     // skip pts of prev contour
787:     fCurrPt += fCurrPtCount;
788: 
789:     SkASSERT(SkPathVerb::kMove == fCurrVerb[0]);
790:     int ptCount = 1;    // moveTo
791:     const SkPathVerb* verbs = fCurrVerb;
792: 
793:     for (verbs++; verbs < fStopVerbs; verbs++) {
794:         switch (*verbs) {
795:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:
796:                 goto CONTOUR_END;
797:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:
798:                 ptCount += 1;
799:                 break;
800:             case SkPathVerb::kConic:
801:                 fCurrConicWeight += 1;
802:                 [[fallthrough]];
803:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
804:                 ptCount += 2;
805:                 break;
806:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
807:                 ptCount += 3;
808:                 break;
809:             case SkPathVerb::kClose:
810:                 break;
811:         }
812:     }
813: CONTOUR_END:
814:     fCurrPtCount = ptCount;
815:     fCurrVerb = verbs;
816:     SkDEBUGCODE(++fContourCounter;)
817: }
818: 
819: /*
820:  *  We loop through all contours, and keep the computed cross-product of the
821:  *  contour that contained the global y-max. If we just look at the first
822:  *  contour, we may find one that is wound the opposite way (correctly) since
823:  *  it is the interior of a hole (e.g. 'o'). Thus we must find the contour
824:  *  that is outer most (or at least has the global y-max) before we can consider
825:  *  its cross product.
826:  */
827: SkPathFirstDirection SkPathPriv::ComputeFirstDirection(const SkPathRaw& raw) {
828:     ContourIter iter(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics());
829: 
830:     // initialize with our logical y-min
831:     SkScalar ymax = raw.bounds().fTop;
832:     SkScalar ymaxCross = 0;
833: 
834:     for (; !iter.done(); iter.next()) {
835:         int n = iter.count();
836:         if (n < 3) {
837:             continue;
838:         }
839: 
840:         const SkPoint* pts = iter.pts();
841:         SkScalar cross = 0;
842:         int index = find_max_y(pts, n);
843:         if (pts[index].fY < ymax) {
844:             continue;
845:         }
846: 
847:         // If there is more than 1 distinct point at the y-max, we take the
848:         // x-min and x-max of them and just subtract to compute the dir.
849:         if (pts[(index + 1) % n].fY == pts[index].fY) {
850:             int maxIndex;
851:             int minIndex = find_min_max_x_at_y(pts, index, n, &maxIndex);
852:             if (minIndex == maxIndex) {
853:                 goto TRY_CROSSPROD;
854:             }
855:             SkASSERT(pts[minIndex].fY == pts[index].fY);
856:             SkASSERT(pts[maxIndex].fY == pts[index].fY);
857:             SkASSERT(pts[minIndex].fX <= pts[maxIndex].fX);
858:             // we just subtract the indices, and let that auto-convert to
859:             // SkScalar, since we just want - or + to signal the direction.
860:             cross = minIndex - maxIndex;
861:         } else {
862:             TRY_CROSSPROD:
863:             // Find a next and prev index to use for the cross-product test,
864:             // but we try to find pts that form non-zero vectors from pts[index]
865:             //
866:             // Its possible that we can't find two non-degenerate vectors, so
867:             // we have to guard our search (e.g. all the pts could be in the
868:             // same place).
869: 
870:             // we pass n - 1 instead of -1 so we don't foul up % operator by
871:             // passing it a negative LH argument.
872:             int prev = find_diff_pt(pts, index, n, n - 1);
873:             if (prev == index) {
874:                 // completely degenerate, skip to next contour
875:                 continue;
876:             }
877:             int next = find_diff_pt(pts, index, n, 1);
878:             SkASSERT(next != index);
879:             cross = cross_prod(pts[prev], pts[index], pts[next]);
880:             // if we get a zero and the points are horizontal, then we look at the spread in
881:             // x-direction. We really should continue to walk away from the degeneracy until
882:             // there is a divergence.
883:             if (0 == cross && pts[prev].fY == pts[index].fY && pts[next].fY == pts[index].fY) {
884:                 // construct the subtract so we get the correct Direction below
885:                 cross = pts[index].fX - pts[next].fX;
886:             }
887:         }
888: 
889:         if (cross) {
890:             // record our best guess so far
891:             ymax = pts[index].fY;
892:             ymaxCross = cross;
893:         }
894:     }
895: 
896:     return ymaxCross ? crossToDir(ymaxCross) : SkPathFirstDirection::kUnknown;
897: }

901: static float poly_eval(float A, float B, float C, float t) {
902:     return (A * t + B) * t + C;
903: }
904: 
905: static float poly_eval(float A, float B, float C, float D, float t) {
906:     return ((A * t + B) * t + C) * t + D;

909: static bool between(SkScalar a, SkScalar b, SkScalar c) {
910:     SkASSERT(((a <= b && b <= c) || (a >= b && b >= c)) == ((a - b) * (c - b) <= 0)
911:             || (SkScalarNearlyZero(a) && SkScalarNearlyZero(b) && SkScalarNearlyZero(c)));
912:     return (a - b) * (c - b) <= 0;

915: static SkScalar eval_cubic_pts(SkScalar c0, SkScalar c1, SkScalar c2, SkScalar c3,
916:                                SkScalar t) {
917:     SkScalar A = c3 + 3*(c1 - c2) - c0;
918:     SkScalar B = 3*(c2 - c1 - c1 + c0);
919:     SkScalar C = 3*(c1 - c0);
920:     SkScalar D = c0;
921:     return poly_eval(A, B, C, D, t);
922: }

1246:     B -= C;  // B = b*w - w * yCept + yCept - a
1247:     C -= y;
1248:     int n = SkFindUnitQuadRoots(A, 2 * B, C, roots.data());
1249:     for (int index = 0; index < n; ++index) {
1250:         SkScalar t = roots[index];
1251:         SkScalar xt = conic_eval_numerator(&pts[0].fX, w, t) / conic_eval_denominator(w, t);
1252:         if (!SkScalarNearlyEqual(x, xt)) {
1253:             continue;
1254:         }
1255:         SkConic conic(pts.data(), w);
1256:         tangents->push_back(conic.evalTangentAt(t));
1257:     }
1258: }
1259: 
1260: static void tangent_quad(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y,
1261:                          SkTDArray<SkVector>* tangents) {
1262:     if (!between(pts[0].fY, y, pts[1].fY) && !between(pts[1].fY, y, pts[2].fY)) {
1263:         return;
1264:     }
1265:     if (!between(pts[0].fX, x, pts[1].fX) && !between(pts[1].fX, x, pts[2].fX)) {
1266:         return;
1267:     }
1268:     std::array<SkScalar, 2> roots;
1269:     int n = SkFindUnitQuadRoots(pts[0].fY - 2 * pts[1].fY + pts[2].fY,
1270:                                 2 * (pts[1].fY - pts[0].fY),
1271:                                 pts[0].fY - y,
1272:                                 roots.data());
1273:     for (int index = 0; index < n; ++index) {
1274:         SkScalar t = roots[index];
1275:         SkScalar C = pts[0].fX;
1276:         SkScalar A = pts[2].fX - 2 * pts[1].fX + C;
1277:         SkScalar B = 2 * (pts[1].fX - C);
1278:         SkScalar xt = poly_eval(A, B, C, t);
1279:         if (!SkScalarNearlyEqual(x, xt)) {
1280:             continue;
1281:         }
1282:         tangents->push_back(SkEvalQuadTangentAt(pts.data(), t));
1283:     }
1284: }
1285: 
1286: static void tangent_line(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, SkScalar x, SkScalar y,
1287:                          SkTDArray<SkVector>* tangents) {
1288:     SkScalar y0 = pts[0].fY;
1289:     SkScalar y1 = pts[1].fY;
1290:     if (!between(y0, y, y1)) {
1291:         return;
1292:     }
1293:     SkScalar x0 = pts[0].fX;
1294:     SkScalar x1 = pts[1].fX;
1295:     if (!between(x0, x, x1)) {
1296:         return;
1297:     }
1298:     SkScalar dx = x1 - x0;
1299:     SkScalar dy = y1 - y0;
1300:     if (!SkScalarNearlyEqual((x - x0) * dy, dx * (y - y0))) {
1301:         return;
1302:     }
1303:     SkVector v;
1304:     v.set(dx, dy);
1305:     tangents->push_back(v);
1306: }

1308: static bool contains_inclusive(const SkRect& r, SkPoint p) {
1309:     return r.fLeft <= p.fX && p.fX <= r.fRight && r.fTop <= p.fY && p.fY <= r.fBottom;
1310: }

1312: bool SkPathPriv::Contains(const SkPathRaw& raw, SkPoint p) {
1313:     const SkPathFillType ft = raw.fillType();
1314:     const bool isInverse = SkPathFillType_IsInverse(ft);
1315:     if (raw.empty()) {
1316:         return isInverse;
1317:     }
1318: 
1319:     if (!contains_inclusive(raw.bounds(), p)) {
1320:         return isInverse;
1321:     }
1322: 
1323:     int w = 0;
1324:     int onCurveCount = 0;
1325: 
1326:     for (auto iter = SkPathEdgeIter(raw); auto rec = iter.next(); ) {
1327:         switch (rec.fEdge) {
1328:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kLine:
1329:                 w += winding_line({rec.fPts, 2}, p.fX, p.fY, &onCurveCount);
1330:                 break;
1331:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kQuad:
1332:                 w += winding_quad({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, &onCurveCount);
1333:                 break;
1334:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kConic:
1335:                 w += winding_conic({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, iter.conicWeight(), &onCurveCount);
1336:                 break;
1337:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kCubic:
1338:                 w += winding_cubic({rec.fPts, 4}, p.fX, p.fY, &onCurveCount);
1339:                 break;
1340:        }
1341:     }
1342:     bool evenOddFill = SkPathFillType::kEvenOdd        == ft
1343:                     || SkPathFillType::kInverseEvenOdd == ft;
1344:     if (evenOddFill) {
1345:         w &= 1;
1346:     }
1347:     if (w) {
1348:         return !isInverse;
1349:     }
1350:     if (onCurveCount <= 1) {
1351:         return SkToBool(onCurveCount) ^ isInverse;
1352:     }
1353:     if ((onCurveCount & 1) || evenOddFill) {
1354:         return SkToBool(onCurveCount & 1) ^ isInverse;
1355:     }
1356:     // If the point touches an even number of curves, and the fill is winding, check for
1357:     // coincidence. Count coincidence as places where the on curve points have identical tangents.
1358:     SkTDArray<SkVector> tangents;
1359:     for (auto iter = SkPathEdgeIter(raw); auto rec = iter.next(); ) {
1360:         int oldCount = tangents.size();
1361:         switch (rec.fEdge) {
1362:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kLine:
1363:                 tangent_line({rec.fPts, 2}, p.fX, p.fY, &tangents);
1364:                 break;
1365:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kQuad:
1366:                 tangent_quad({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, &tangents);
1367:                 break;
1368:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kConic:
1369:                 tangent_conic({rec.fPts, 3}, p.fX, p.fY, iter.conicWeight(), &tangents);
1370:                 break;
1371:             case SkPathEdgeIter::Edge::kCubic:
1372:                 tangent_cubic({rec.fPts, 4}, p.fX, p.fY, &tangents);
1373:                 break;
1374:        }
1375:        if (tangents.size() > oldCount) {
1376:             int last = tangents.size() - 1;
1377:             const SkVector& tangent = tangents[last];
1378:             if (SkScalarNearlyZero(SkPointPriv::LengthSqd(tangent))) {
1379:                 tangents.remove(last);
1380:             } else {
1381:                 for (int index = 0; index < last; ++index) {
1382:                     const SkVector& test = tangents[index];
1383:                     if (SkScalarNearlyZero(test.cross(tangent))
1384:                             && SkScalarSignAsInt(tangent.fX * test.fX) <= 0
1385:                             && SkScalarSignAsInt(tangent.fY * test.fY) <= 0) {
1386:                         tangents.remove(last);
1387:                         tangents.removeShuffle(index);
1388:                         break;
1389:                     }
1390:                 }
1391:             }
1392:         }
1393:     }
1394:     return SkToBool(tangents.size()) ^ isInverse;
1395: }

1399: bool SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts) {
1400:     // Conservative (quick) test to see if all segments are axis-aligned.
1401:     // Multiple contours might give a false-negative, but for speed, we ignore that
1402:     // and just look at the raw points.
1403: 
1404:     for (size_t i = 1; i < pts.size(); ++i) {
1405:         if (pts[i-1].fX != pts[i].fX && pts[i-1].fY != pts[i].fY) {
1406:             return false;

1412: SkPathConvexity SkPathPriv::TransformConvexity(const SkMatrix& matrix, SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts,
1413:                                                SkPathConvexity convexity) {
1414:     if (matrix.isIdentity() || pts.empty()) {
1415:         return convexity;
1416:     }
1417: 
1418:     // Due to finite/fragile float numerics, we can't assume that a convex path remains
1419:     // convex after a transformation, so mark it as unknown here.
1420:     // However, some transformations are thought to be safe:
1421:     //    axis-aligned values under scale/translate.
1422:     //
1423:     if (SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(convexity)) {
1424:         if (!matrix.isScaleTranslate() || !SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(pts)) {
1425:             // Not safe to still assume we're convex...
1426:             convexity = SkPathConvexity::kUnknown;
1427:         } else {
1428:             SkScalar det2x2 =
1429:                 matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMScaleX) * matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMScaleY) -
1430:                 matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMSkewX)  * matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMSkewY);
1431:             if (det2x2 < 0) {
1432:                 convexity = SkPathConvexity_OppositeConvexDirection(convexity);
1433:             } else if (det2x2 > 0) {
1434:                 // we keep our direction
1435:             } else /* det2x == 0 */ {
1436:                 convexity = SkPathConvexity::kConvex_Degenerate;
1437:             }
1438:         }
1439:     }
1440:     return convexity;
1441: }

1444: 
1445: static int compute_quad_extremas(const SkPoint src[3], SkPoint extremas[3]) {
1446:     std::array<SkScalar, 2> ts;
1447:     int n  = SkFindQuadExtrema(src[0].fX, src[1].fX, src[2].fX, ts.data());
1448:         n += SkFindQuadExtrema(src[0].fY, src[1].fY, src[2].fY, &ts[n]);
1449:     SkASSERT(n >= 0 && n <= 2);
1450:     for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
1451:         extremas[i] = SkEvalQuadAt(src, ts[i]);
1452:     }
1453:     extremas[n] = src[2];
1454:     return n + 1;
1455: }
1456: 
1457: static int compute_conic_extremas(const SkPoint src[3], SkScalar w, SkPoint extremas[3]) {
1458:     SkConic conic(src[0], src[1], src[2], w);
1459:     std::array<SkScalar, 2> ts;
1460:     int n  = conic.findXExtrema(ts.data());
1461:         n += conic.findYExtrema(&ts[n]);
1462:     SkASSERT(n >= 0 && n <= 2);
1463:     for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
1464:         extremas[i] = conic.evalAt(ts[i]);
1465:     }
1466:     extremas[n] = src[2];
1467:     return n + 1;
1468: }
1469: 
1470: static int compute_cubic_extremas(const SkPoint src[4], SkPoint extremas[5]) {
1471:     std::array<SkScalar, 4> ts;
1472:     int n  = SkFindCubicExtrema(src[0].fX, src[1].fX, src[2].fX, src[3].fX, ts.data());
1473:         n += SkFindCubicExtrema(src[0].fY, src[1].fY, src[2].fY, src[3].fY, &ts[n]);
1474:     SkASSERT(n >= 0 && n <= 4);
1475:     for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
1476:         SkEvalCubicAt(src, ts[i], &extremas[i], nullptr, nullptr);
1477:     }
1478:     extremas[n] = src[3];
1479:     return n + 1;
1480: }

1482: SkRect SkPathPriv::ComputeTightBounds(SkSpan<const SkPoint> points,
1483:                                       SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> verbs,
1484:                                       SkSpan<const float> conicWeights) {
1485:     if (verbs.empty()) {
1486:         return SkRect::MakeEmpty();
1487:     }
1488: 
1489:     // initial with the first MoveTo, so we don't have to check inside the switch
1490:     float L = points[0].fX,
1491:           T = points[0].fY,
1492:           R = points[0].fX,
1493:           B = points[0].fY;
1494: 
1495:     for (auto [verb, pts, w] : SkPathPriv::Iterate(verbs, points.data(), conicWeights.data())) {
1496:         SkPoint extremas[5]; // big enough to hold worst-case curve type (cubic) extremas + 1
1497:         int count = 0;
1498:         switch (verb) {
1499:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:
1500:                 extremas[0] = pts[0];
1501:                 count = 1;
1502:                 break;
1503:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:
1504:                 extremas[0] = pts[1];
1505:                 count = 1;
1506:                 break;
1507:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
1508:                 count = compute_quad_extremas(pts, extremas);
1509:                 break;
1510:             case SkPathVerb::kConic:
1511:                 count = compute_conic_extremas(pts, *w, extremas);
1512:                 break;
1513:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
1514:                 count = compute_cubic_extremas(pts, extremas);
1515:                 break;
1516:             case SkPathVerb::kClose:
1517:                 break;
1518:         }
1519:         for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
1520:             SkPoint p = extremas[i];
1521:             L = std::fminf(p.fX, L);
1522:             T = std::fminf(p.fY, T);
1523:             R = std::fmaxf(p.fX, R);
1524:             B = std::fmaxf(p.fY, B);
1525:         }
1526:     }
1527:     return {L, T, R, B};
1528: }

1530: int SkPathPriv::FindLastMoveToIndex(SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> verbs, const size_t ptCount) {
1531:     if (verbs.empty()) {
1532:         SkASSERT(ptCount == 0);
1533:         return -1;
1534:     }
1535:     SkASSERT(verbs[0] == SkPathVerb::kMove);
1536:     SkASSERT(ptCount > 0);
1537: 
1538:     int ptIndex = SkToInt(ptCount) - 1;
1539:     for (auto it = verbs.rbegin(), end = verbs.rend(); it != end; ++it) {
1540:         const SkPathVerb verb = *it;
1541:         if (verb == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
1542:             break;
1543:         }
1544:         ptIndex -= PtsInVerb(verb);
1545:     }
1546:     SkASSERT(ptIndex >= 0);
1547:     return ptIndex;

1550: std::pair<SkPathDirection, unsigned>
1551: SkPathPriv::TransformDirAndStart(const SkMatrix& matrix, bool isRRect, SkPathDirection dir,
1552:                                  unsigned start) {
1553:     if (matrix.isIdentity()) {
1554:         return {dir, start};
1555:     }
1556:     unsigned inStart = start;
1557:     bool isCCW = (dir == SkPathDirection::kCCW);
1558: 
1559:     int rm = 0;
1560:     if (isRRect) {
1561:         // Degenerate rrect indices to oval indices and remember the remainder.
1562:         // Ovals have one index per side whereas rrects have two.
1563:         rm = inStart & 0b1;
1564:         inStart /= 2;
1565:     }
1566:     // Is the antidiagonal non-zero (otherwise the diagonal is zero)
1567:     int antiDiag;
1568:     // Is the non-zero value in the top row (either kMScaleX or kMSkewX) negative
1569:     int topNeg;
1570:     // Are the two non-zero diagonal or antidiagonal values the same sign.
1571:     int sameSign;
1572:     if (matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMScaleX) != 0) {
1573:         antiDiag = 0b00;
1574:         if (matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMScaleX) > 0) {
1575:             topNeg = 0b00;
1576:             sameSign = matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMScaleY) > 0 ? 0b01 : 0b00;
1577:         } else {
1578:             topNeg = 0b10;
1579:             sameSign = matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMScaleY) > 0 ? 0b00 : 0b01;
1580:         }
1581:     } else {
1582:         antiDiag = 0b01;
1583:         if (matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMSkewX) > 0) {
1584:             topNeg = 0b00;
1585:             sameSign = matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMSkewY) > 0 ? 0b01 : 0b00;
1586:         } else {
1587:             topNeg = 0b10;
1588:             sameSign = matrix.get(SkMatrix::kMSkewY) > 0 ? 0b00 : 0b01;
1589:         }
1590:     }
1591:     if (sameSign != antiDiag) {
1592:         // This is a rotation (and maybe scale). The direction is unchanged.
1593:         // Trust me on the start computation (or draw yourself some pictures)
1594:         start = (inStart + 4 - (topNeg | antiDiag)) % 4;
1595:         SkASSERT(start < 4);
1596:         if (isRRect) {
1597:             start = 2 * start + rm;
1598:         }
1599:     } else {
1600:         // This is a mirror (and maybe scale). The direction is reversed.
1601:         isCCW = !isCCW;
1602:         // Trust me on the start computation (or draw yourself some pictures)
1603:         start = (6 + (topNeg | antiDiag) - inStart) % 4;
1604:         SkASSERT(start < 4);
1605:         if (isRRect) {
1606:             start = 2 * start + (rm ? 0 : 1);
1607:         }
1608:     }
1609: 
1610:     return {
1611:         isCCW ? SkPathDirection::kCCW : SkPathDirection::kCW,
1612:         start
1613:     };
1614: }

36: /*
37:  Determines if path is a rect by keeping track of changes in direction
38:  and looking for a loop either clockwise or counterclockwise.
39: 
40:  The direction is computed such that:
41:   0: vertical up
42:   1: horizontal left
43:   2: vertical down
44:   3: horizontal right
45: 
46: A rectangle cycles up/right/down/left or up/left/down/right.
47: 
48: The test fails if:
49:   The path is closed, and followed by a line.
50:   A second move creates a new endpoint.
51:   A diagonal line is parsed.
52:   There's more than four changes of direction.
53:   There's a discontinuity on the line (e.g., a move in the middle)
54:   The line reverses direction.
55:   The path contains a quadratic or cubic.
56:   The path contains fewer than four points.
57:  *The rectangle doesn't complete a cycle.
58:  *The final point isn't equal to the first point.
59: 
60:   *These last two conditions we relax if we have a 3-edge path that would
61:    form a rectangle if it were closed (as we do when we fill a path)
62: 
63: It's OK if the path has:
64:   Several colinear line segments composing a rectangle side.
65:   Single points on the rectangle side.
66: 
67: The direction takes advantage of the corners found since opposite sides
68: must travel in opposite directions.
