142:     /** Specifies whether SkPath is volatile; whether it will be altered or discarded
143:         by the caller after it is drawn. SkPath by default have volatile set false, allowing
144:         Skia to attach a cache of data which speeds repeated drawing.
145: 
146:         Mark temporary paths, discarded or modified after use, as volatile
147:         to inform Skia that the path need not be cached.
148: 
149:         Mark animating SkPath volatile to improve performance.
150:         Mark unchanging SkPath non-volatile to improve repeated rendering.
151: 
152:         raster surface SkPath draws are affected by volatile for some shadows.
153:         GPU surface SkPath draws are affected by volatile for some shadows and concave geometries.
154:

156:         @return            reference to SkPathBuilder

249:     /** Adds conic from last point towards pt1, to pt2, weighted by w.
250:         If SkPathBuilder is empty, or last SkPath::Verb is kClose_Verb, last point is set to (0, 0)
251:         before adding conic.

253:         Appends kMove_Verb to verb array and (0, 0) to SkPoint array, if needed.
254: 
255:         If w is finite, positive, and not one, appends kConic_Verb to verb array;
256:         and pt1, pt2 to SkPoint array; and w to conic weights.
257: 
258:         If w is one, appends kQuad_Verb to verb array, and
259:         pt1, pt2 to SkPoint array.
260: 
261:         If w is zero, this is the same as lineTo(pt2)
262: 
263:         If w is not finite, appends kLine_Verb twice to verb array, and
264:         pt1, pt2 to SkPoint array.

266:         @param pt1  control SkPoint of conic

273:     /** Adds conic from last point towards (x1, y1), to (x2, y2), weighted by w.

279:         If w is finite and not one, appends kConic_Verb to verb array;

469:         control and quad end to SkPoint array.

492:         and w is recorded as conic weight; otherwise, if w is one, appends

514:         if needed.

516:         If w is finite and not one, next appends kConic_Verb to verb array,
517:         and w is recorded as conic weight; otherwise, if w is one, appends
518:         kQuad_Verb to verb array; or if w is not finite, appends kLine_Verb
519:         twice to verb array.

521:         In all cases appends SkPoint control and end to SkPoint array.
522:         control is last point plus vector (dx1, dy1).
523:         end is last point plus vector (dx2, dy2).
524: 
525:         Function name stands for "relative conic to".

527:         @param dx1  offset from last point to conic control on x-axis
528:         @param dy1  offset from last point to conic control on y-axis
529:         @param dx2  offset from last point to conic end on x-axis
530:         @param dy2  offset from last point to conic end on y-axis

535:         return this->rConicTo({dx1, dy1}, {dx2, dy2}, w);

583:     // Arcs
584: 
585:     enum ArcSize {
586:         kSmall_ArcSize, //!< smaller of arc pair
587:         kLarge_ArcSize, //!< larger of arc pair
588:     };
589: 
590:     /** Appends arc to SkPathBuilder, relative to last SkPath SkPoint. Arc is implemented by one or
591:         more conic, weighted to describe part of oval with radii (rx, ry) rotated by
592:         xAxisRotate degrees. Arc curves from last SkPathBuilder SkPoint to relative end SkPoint:
593:         (dx, dy), choosing one of four possible routes: clockwise or
594:         counterclockwise, and smaller or larger. If SkPathBuilder is empty, the start arc SkPoint
595:         is (0, 0).
596: 
597:         Arc sweep is always less than 360 degrees. arcTo() appends line to end SkPoint
598:         if either radii are zero, or if last SkPath SkPoint equals end SkPoint.
599:         arcTo() scales radii (rx, ry) to fit last SkPath SkPoint and end SkPoint if both are
600:         greater than zero but too small to describe an arc.
601: 
602:         arcTo() appends up to four conic curves.
603:         arcTo() implements the functionality of svg arc, although SVG "sweep-flag" value is
604:         opposite the integer value of sweep; SVG "sweep-flag" uses 1 for clockwise, while
605:         kCW_Direction cast to int is zero.
606: 
607:         @param r            radii on axes before x-axis rotation
608:         @param xAxisRotate  x-axis rotation in degrees; positive values are clockwise
609:         @param largeArc     chooses smaller or larger arc
610:         @param sweep        chooses clockwise or counterclockwise arc
611:         @param dxdy         offset end of arc from last SkPath point
612:         @return             reference to SkPath
613:     */
614:     SkPathBuilder& rArcTo(SkPoint r, SkScalar xAxisRotate, ArcSize largeArc,
615:                           SkPathDirection sweep, SkVector dxdy);
616: 
617:     /** Appends arc to the builder. Arc added is part of ellipse
618:         bounded by oval, from startAngle through sweepAngle. Both startAngle and
619:         sweepAngle are measured in degrees, where zero degrees is aligned with the
620:         positive x-axis, and positive sweeps extends arc clockwise.
621:

635:     /** Appends arc to SkPath, after appending line if needed. Arc is implemented by conic

638:         is part of circle sized to radius, positioned so it touches both tangent lines.

640:         If last SkPath SkPoint does not start arc, arcTo() appends connecting line to SkPath.
641:         The length of vector from p1 to p2 does not affect arc.
642: 
643:         Arc sweep is always less than 180 degrees. If radius is zero, or if
644:         tangents are nearly parallel, arcTo() appends line from last SkPath SkPoint to p1.
645: 
646:         arcTo() appends at most one line and one conic.

659:         clockwise or counterclockwise,

72: static constexpr auto gPtsPerVerb = std::to_array<uint8_t>({
73:     1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 0,  // move, line, quad, conic, cubic, close
74: });
75: 
76: static inline bool valid_conic_weight(float w) {
77:     return w >= 0 && SkIsFinite(w);
78: }
79: 
80: static bool valid_path_data(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts,
81:                             SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs,
82:                             SkSpan<const float> conics) {
83:     if (vbs.empty()) {
84:         return pts.empty() && conics.empty();
85:     }
86: 
87:     // We must begin with a Move (unless we're empty)
88:     if (vbs.front() != SkPathVerb::kMove) {
89:         return false;
90:     }
91:     SkPathVerb prev = SkPathVerb::kMove;
92:     size_t point_count = 1,
93:            conic_count = 0;
94: 
95:     // Check that we have a valid sequence.
96:     for (size_t i = 1; i < vbs.size(); ++i) {
97:         SkPathVerb curr = vbs[i];
98: 
99:         if (static_cast<unsigned>(curr) > static_cast<unsigned>(SkPathVerb::kLast_Verb)) {
100:             return false;
101:         }
102: 
103:         // Previous verb             Valid next verb
104:         // -----------------------------------------
105:         // Move                  --> not Move
106:         // Line/Quad/Conic/Cubic --> *
107:         // Close                 --> Move
108:         //
109:         if (prev == SkPathVerb::kMove && curr == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
110:             return false;
111:         }
112:         if (prev == SkPathVerb::kClose && curr != SkPathVerb::kMove) {
113:             return false;
114:         }
115: 
116:         point_count += gPtsPerVerb[SkToSizeT(curr)];
117:         conic_count += (curr == SkPathVerb::kConic);
118: 
119:         prev = curr;
120:     }
121: 
122:     if (pts.size() != point_count || conics.size() != conic_count){
123:         return false;
124:     }
125: 
126:     for (auto w : conics) {
127:         if (!valid_conic_weight(w)) {
128:             return false;
129:         }
130:     }
131: 
132:     return true;
133: }

201: // NOTE: This only allocates and initializes the span pointers (points, verbs),

203: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Alloc(size_t npts, size_t nvbs, size_t ncns) {
204:     SkSafeAccumulator accum(sizeof(SkPathData));
205: 
206:     accum.addMul(npts, sizeof(SkPoint))
207:          .addMul(ncns, sizeof(float))
208:          .addMul(nvbs, sizeof(SkPathVerb));
209: 
210:     if (auto size = accum.total()) {
211:         // This trick allows us to just make one allocation, for us and our buffer
212:         // rather than allocating us and also allocating the buffer (via malloc or new[])
213:         // We have the corresponding operator delete() specified as well.
214:         void* storage = ::operator new (*size);
215:         sk_sp<SkPathData> path(new (storage) SkPathData(npts, nvbs, ncns));
216: 
217:         return path;
218:     }
219:     return nullptr;
220: }

222: bool SkPathData::finishInit(std::optional<SkRect> bounds, std::optional<uint8_t> segmentMask) {
223:     SkASSERT(valid_path_data(fPoints, fVerbs, fConics));
224: 
225:     if (fPoints.empty()) {
226:         fBounds = SkRect::MakeEmpty();
227:         fSegmentMask = 0;
228:         return true;
229:     }
230: 
231:     if (segmentMask.has_value()) {
232:         fSegmentMask = segmentMask.value();
233:     } else {
234:         fSegmentMask = SkPathPriv::ComputeSegmentMask(fVerbs);
235:     }
236: 
237:     if (bounds.has_value()) {
238:         fBounds = bounds.value().makeSorted();
239:         SkASSERT(SkIsFinite(&fPoints.data()->fX, fPoints.size() * 2));
240:     } else {
241:         if (auto r = SkPathPriv::TrimmedBounds(fPoints, fVerbs)) {
242:             fBounds = r.value();
243:         } else {
244:             report_pathdata_make_failure("non-finite bounds");
245:             return false;
246:         }
247:     }
248: 
249:     SkASSERT(fBounds.isSorted());
250:     return true;
251: }

253: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::MakeTransform(const SkPathRaw& src, const SkMatrix& mx) {
254:     if (src.empty()) {
255:         return SkPathData::Empty();
256:     }
257: 
258:     if (mx.hasPerspective()) {
259:         return SkPathBuilder()
260:             .addRaw(src, SkPathBuilder::Reserve::kExact)
261:             .transform(mx)
262:             .detachData();
263:     }
264: 
265:     // Allocate our result, so we can map the new points directly into it
266:     auto result = Alloc(src.points().size(), src.verbs().size(), src.conics().size());
267:     mx.mapPoints(result->fPoints, src.points());
268:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(result->fConics, src.conics());
269:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(result->fVerbs,  src.verbs());
270: 
271:     std::optional<SkRect> transformedBounds;
272:     if (mx.rectStaysRect()) {
273:         // safe us from having to compute our transformed bounds in finishInit()
274:         transformedBounds = mx.mapRect(src.bounds());
275:         if (!transformedBounds.value().isFinite()) {
276:             report_pathdata_make_failure("transform created non-finite bounds");
277:             return nullptr;
278:         }
279:     }
280: 
281:     if (!result->finishInit(transformedBounds, src.fSegmentMask)) {
282:         return nullptr;
283:     }
284: 
285:     result->setConvexity(SkPathPriv::TransformConvexity(mx, src.fPoints, src.fConvexity));
286: 
287:     return result;
288: }
289: 
290: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::makeTransform(const SkMatrix& mx) const {
291:     if (mx.isIdentity()) {
292:         return sk_ref_sp(this);
293:     }
294: 
295:     // not important for transform, just need a value
296:     const SkPathFillType ft = SkPathFillType::kDefault;
297: 
298:     auto result = MakeTransform(this->raw(ft, SkResolveConvexity::kNo), mx);
299: 
300:     if (!result) {
301:         return nullptr;
302:     }
303: 
304:     if (fType == SkPathIsAType::kGeneral) {
305:         return result;
306:     }
307: 
308:     // See if we can maintain our IsA status ...
309:     bool canMaintainIsA =
310:             mx.rectStaysRect() && SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(fPoints) && !result->bounds().isEmpty();
311:     if (!canMaintainIsA) {
312:         return result;
313:     }
314: 
315:     auto [dir, start] = SkPathPriv::TransformDirAndStart(
316:             mx, fType == SkPathIsAType::kRRect, fIsA.fDirection, fIsA.fStartIndex);
317:     result->setupIsA(fType, dir, start);
318:     return result;
319: }

361: void SkPathData::setupIsA(SkPathIsAType type, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
362:     this->setConvexity(SkPathDirection_ToConvexity(dir));
363: 
364:     SkASSERT(type == SkPathIsAType::kOval || type == SkPathIsAType::kRRect);
365:     fType = type;
366: 
367:     SkASSERT((type == SkPathIsAType::kOval && index < 4) ||
368:              (type == SkPathIsAType::kRRect && index < 8));
369: 
370:     fIsA.fDirection  = dir;
371:     fIsA.fStartIndex = SkTo<uint8_t>(index);
372: }

375:     if (!r.isFinite()) {
376:         return nullptr;
377:     }
378:     SkPathRawShapes::Rect raw(r, dir, index);
379:     return MakeNoCheck(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics(), raw.fBounds, raw.fSegmentMask);
380: }

382: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Oval(const SkRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
383:     if (!r.isFinite()) {
384:         return nullptr;
385:     }
386:     SkPathRawShapes::Oval raw(r, dir, index);
387:     auto path = MakeNoCheck(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics(), raw.fBounds, raw.fSegmentMask);
388:

390:     return path;

393: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::RRect(const SkRRect& r, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {
394:     if (!r.isValid()) {
395:         return nullptr;
396:     }
397:     SkPathRawShapes::RRect raw(r, dir, index);
398:     // we use Make, not MakeNoCheck, to confirm all points an conics are finite
399:     if (auto path = Make(raw.points(), raw.verbs(), raw.conics())) {
400:         path->setupIsA(SkPathIsAType::kRRect, dir, index);
401:         return path;
402:     }
403:     return nullptr;
404: }

406: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathData::Polygon(SkSpan<const SkPoint> pts, bool isClosed) {
407:     if (pts.size() == 0 || (pts.size() == 1 && !isClosed)) {
408:         return Empty();
409:     }
410: 
411:     const size_t nverbs = pts.size() + isClosed;    // +1 for the kClose verb
412:     const size_t nconics = 0;
413:     auto path = Alloc(pts.size(), nverbs, nconics);
414: 
415:     SkSpanPriv::Copy(path->fPoints, pts);
416: 
417:     path->fVerbs[0] = SkPathVerb::kMove;
418:     for (size_t i = 1; i < pts.size(); ++i) {
419:         path->fVerbs[i] = SkPathVerb::kLine;
420:     }
421:     if (isClosed) {
422:         path->fVerbs.back() = SkPathVerb::kClose;
423:     }
424: 
425:     return path->finishInit({}, kLine_SkPathSegmentMask) ? path : nullptr;
426: }

152:  *  Some old behavior in SkPath -- should we keep it?
153:  *
154:  *  After each edit (i.e. adding a verb)
155:         this->setConvexityType(SkPathConvexity::kUnknown);
156:         this->setFirstDirection(SkPathPriv::kUnknown_FirstDirection);
157:  */
158: 
159: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::moveTo(SkPoint pt) {
160:     if (!fVerbs.empty() && fVerbs.back() == SkPathVerb::kMove) {
161:         fPts.back() = pt;
162: 
163:         SkASSERT(fType != SkPathIsAType::kOval && fType != SkPathIsAType::kRRect);
164:         SkASSERT(fConvexity == SkPathConvexity::kUnknown);
165:         SkASSERT(fLastMoveIndex == SkToInt(fPts.size()) - 1);
166:     } else {
167:         fLastMoveIndex = SkToInt(fPts.size());
168: 
169:         fPts.push_back(pt);
170:         fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kMove);
171: 
172:         if (fType == SkPathIsAType::kOval || fType == SkPathIsAType::kRRect) {
173:             fType = SkPathIsAType::kGeneral;
174:         }
175:         fConvexity = SkPathConvexity::kUnknown;
176:     }
177: 
178:     return *this;
179: }
180: 
181: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::lineTo(SkPoint pt) {
182:     this->ensureMove();
183: 
184:     fPts.push_back(pt);
185:     fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kLine);
186: 
187:     fSegmentMask |= kLine_SkPathSegmentMask;
188:     return *this;
189: }
190: 
191: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::quadTo(SkPoint pt1, SkPoint pt2) {
192:     this->ensureMove();
193: 
194:     SkPoint* p = fPts.push_back_n(2);
195:     p[0] = pt1;
196:     p[1] = pt2;
197:     fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kQuad);
198: 
199:     fSegmentMask |= kQuad_SkPathSegmentMask;
200:     return *this;
201: }
202: 
203: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::conicTo(SkPoint pt1, SkPoint pt2, SkScalar w) {
204:     this->ensureMove();
205: 
206:     if (w <= 0) {
207:         return this->lineTo(pt2);
208:     }
209:     SkPoint* p = fPts.push_back_n(2);
210:     p[0] = pt1;
211:     p[1] = pt2;
212:     if (w == 1) {
213:         fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kQuad);
214:         fSegmentMask |= kQuad_SkPathSegmentMask;
215:     } else if (SkIsFinite(w)) {
216:         fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kConic);
217:         fConicWeights.push_back(w);
218:         fSegmentMask |= kConic_SkPathSegmentMask;
219:     } else {
220:         fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kLine);
221:         fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kLine);
222:         fSegmentMask |= kLine_SkPathSegmentMask;
223:     }
224: 
225:     return *this;
226: }
227: 
228: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::cubicTo(SkPoint pt1, SkPoint pt2, SkPoint pt3) {
229:     this->ensureMove();
230: 
231:     SkPoint* p = fPts.push_back_n(3);
232:     p[0] = pt1;
233:     p[1] = pt2;
234:     p[2] = pt3;
235:     fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kCubic);
236: 
237:     fSegmentMask |= kCubic_SkPathSegmentMask;
238:     return *this;
239: }
240: 
241: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::close() {
242:     // If this is a 2nd 'close', we just ignore it
243:     if (!fVerbs.empty() && fVerbs.back() != SkPathVerb::kClose) {
244:         this->ensureMove();
245:         fVerbs.push_back(SkPathVerb::kClose);
246:     }
247:     return *this;
248: }
249: 
250: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
251: 
252: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::rMoveTo(SkVector pt) {
253:     SkPoint lastPt = {0,0}; // in case we're empty
254:     if (!fPts.empty()) {
255:         SkASSERT(fLastMoveIndex >= 0);
256:         if (fVerbs.back() == SkPathVerb::kClose) {
257:             lastPt = fPts[fLastMoveIndex];
258:         } else {
259:             lastPt = fPts.back();
260:         }
261:     }
262:     return this->moveTo(lastPt + pt);
263: }
264: 
265: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::rLineTo(SkVector p1) {
266:     this->ensureMove();
267:     return this->lineTo(fPts.back() + p1);
268: }
269: 
270: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::rQuadTo(SkVector p1, SkVector p2) {
271:     this->ensureMove();
272:     SkPoint base = fPts.back();
273:     return this->quadTo(base + p1, base + p2);
274: }
275: 
276: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::rConicTo(SkVector p1, SkVector p2, SkScalar w) {
277:     this->ensureMove();
278:     SkPoint base = fPts.back();
279:     return this->conicTo(base + p1, base + p2, w);
280: }
281: 
282: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::rCubicTo(SkVector p1, SkVector p2, SkVector p3) {
283:     this->ensureMove();
284:     SkPoint base = fPts.back();
285:     return this->cubicTo(base + p1, base + p2, base + p3);
286: }
287: 
288: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
289: 
290: SkPath SkPathBuilder::snapshot(const SkMatrix* mx) const {
291:     if (!mx) {
292:         mx = &SkMatrix::I();
293:     }
294: 
295:     sk_sp<SkPathData> pdata;
296:     if (auto raw = SkPathPriv::Raw(*this, SkResolveConvexity::kNo)) {
297:         pdata = SkPathData::MakeTransform(*raw, *mx);
298:     }
299:     if (pdata && fType != SkPathIsAType::kGeneral) {
300:         SkASSERT(SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(fPts));
301:         if (mx->rectStaysRect() && !pdata->bounds().isEmpty()) {
302:             auto [dir, start] = SkPathPriv::TransformDirAndStart(
303:                     *mx, fType == SkPathIsAType::kRRect, fIsA.fDirection, fIsA.fStartIndex);
304:             pdata->setupIsA(fType, dir, start);
305:         }
306:     }
307:     return SkPath::MakeNullCheck(std::move(pdata), fFillType, fIsVolatile);
308: }
309: 
310: SkPath SkPathBuilder::detach(const SkMatrix* mx) {
311:     auto path = this->snapshot(mx);
312:     this->reset();
313:     return path;
314: }
315: 
316: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
317: 
318: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathBuilder::snapshotData() const {
319:     if (fVerbs.size() <= 1) {
320:         return SkPathData::Empty();
321:     }
322: 
323:     switch (fType) {
324:         case SkPathIsAType::kGeneral:
325:             break;
326:         case SkPathIsAType::kOval:
327:             if (auto r = SkRect::Bounds(fPts)) {
328:                 return SkPathData::Oval(*r, fIsA.fDirection, fIsA.fStartIndex);
329:             }
330:             return nullptr;
331:         case SkPathIsAType::kRRect:
332:             if (auto r = SkRect::Bounds(fPts)) {
333:                 return SkPathData::RRect(SkPathPriv::DeduceRRectFromContour(*r, fPts, fVerbs),
334:                                          fIsA.fDirection, fIsA.fStartIndex);
335:             }
336:             return nullptr;
337:     }
338:     SkASSERT(fType == SkPathIsAType::kGeneral);
339: 
340:     return SkPathData::Make(fPts, fVerbs, fConicWeights);
341: }
342: 
343: sk_sp<SkPathData> SkPathBuilder::detachData() {
344:     auto data = this->snapshotData();
345:     this->reset();
346:     return data;
347: }
348: 
349: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
350: 
351: static bool arc_is_lone_point(const SkRect& oval, SkScalar startAngle, SkScalar sweepAngle,
352:                               SkPoint* pt) {
353:     if (0 == sweepAngle && (0 == startAngle || SkIntToScalar(360) == startAngle)) {
354:         // Chrome uses this path to move into and out of ovals. If not
355:         // treated as a special case the moves can distort the oval's
356:         // bounding box (and break the circle special case).
357:         pt->set(oval.fRight, oval.centerY());
358:         return true;
359:     } else if (0 == oval.width() && 0 == oval.height()) {
360:         // Chrome will sometimes create 0 radius round rects. Having degenerate
361:         // quad segments in the path prevents the path from being recognized as
362:         // a rect.
363:         // TODO: optimizing the case where only one of width or height is zero
364:         // should also be considered. This case, however, doesn't seem to be
365:         // as common as the single point case.
366:         pt->set(oval.fRight, oval.fTop);
367:         return true;
368:     }
369:     return false;
370: }
371: 
372: // Return the unit vectors pointing at the start/stop points for the given start/sweep angles
373: //
374: static void angles_to_unit_vectors(SkScalar startAngle, SkScalar sweepAngle,
375:                                    SkVector* startV, SkVector* stopV, SkPathDirection* dir) {
376:     SkScalar startRad = SkDegreesToRadians(startAngle),
377:              stopRad  = SkDegreesToRadians(startAngle + sweepAngle);
378: 
379:     startV->fY = SkScalarSinSnapToZero(startRad);
380:     startV->fX = SkScalarCosSnapToZero(startRad);
381:     stopV->fY = SkScalarSinSnapToZero(stopRad);
382:     stopV->fX = SkScalarCosSnapToZero(stopRad);
383: 
384:     /*  If the sweep angle is nearly (but less than) 360, then due to precision
385:      loss in radians-conversion and/or sin/cos, we may end up with coincident
386:      vectors, which will fool SkBuildQuadArc into doing nothing (bad) instead
387:      of drawing a nearly complete circle (good).
388:      e.g. canvas.drawArc(0, 359.99, ...)
389:      -vs- canvas.drawArc(0, 359.9, ...)
390:      We try to detect this edge case, and tweak the stop vector
391:      */
392:     if (*startV == *stopV) {
393:         SkScalar sw = SkScalarAbs(sweepAngle);
394:         if (sw < SkIntToScalar(360) && sw > SkIntToScalar(359)) {
395:             // make a guess at a tiny angle (in radians) to tweak by
396:             SkScalar deltaRad = SkScalarCopySign(SK_Scalar1/512, sweepAngle);
397:             // not sure how much will be enough, so we use a loop
398:             do {
399:                 stopRad -= deltaRad;
400:                 stopV->fY = SkScalarSinSnapToZero(stopRad);
401:                 stopV->fX = SkScalarCosSnapToZero(stopRad);
402:             } while (*startV == *stopV);
403:         }
404:     }
405:     *dir = sweepAngle > 0 ? SkPathDirection::kCW : SkPathDirection::kCCW;
406: }
407: 
408: /**
409:  *  If this returns 0, then the caller should just line-to the singlePt, else it should
410:  *  ignore singlePt and append the specified number of conics.
411:  */
412: static int build_arc_conics(const SkRect& oval, const SkVector& start, const SkVector& stop,
413:                             SkPathDirection dir, SkConic conics[SkConic::kMaxConicsForArc],
414:                             SkPoint* singlePt) {
415:     SkMatrix    matrix;
416: 
417:     matrix.setScale(oval.width() / 2.f, oval.height() / 2.f);
418:     matrix.postTranslate(oval.centerX(), oval.centerY());
419: 
420:     int count = SkConic::BuildUnitArc(start, stop, dir, &matrix, conics);
421:     if (0 == count) {
422:         *singlePt = matrix.mapPoint(stop);
423:     }
424:     return count;
425: }
426: 
427: static bool nearly_equal(const SkPoint& a, const SkPoint& b) {
428:     return SkScalarNearlyEqual(a.fX, b.fX)
429:         && SkScalarNearlyEqual(a.fY, b.fY);
430: }
431: 
432: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::arcTo(const SkRect& oval, SkScalar startAngle, SkScalar sweepAngle,
433:                                     bool forceMoveTo) {
434:     if (oval.width() < 0 || oval.height() < 0) {
435:         return *this;
436:     }
437: 
438:     startAngle = SkScalarMod(startAngle, 360.0f);
439: 
440:     if (fVerbs.empty()) {
441:         forceMoveTo = true;
442:     }
443: 
444:     SkPoint lonePt;
445:     if (arc_is_lone_point(oval, startAngle, sweepAngle, &lonePt)) {
446:         return forceMoveTo ? this->moveTo(lonePt) : this->lineTo(lonePt);
447:     }
448: 
449:     SkVector startV, stopV;
450:     SkPathDirection dir;
451:     angles_to_unit_vectors(startAngle, sweepAngle, &startV, &stopV, &dir);
452: 
453:     SkPoint singlePt;
454: 
455:     // Adds a move-to to 'pt' if forceMoveTo is true. Otherwise a lineTo unless we're sufficiently
456:     // close to 'pt' currently. This prevents spurious lineTos when adding a series of contiguous
457:     // arcs from the same oval.
458:     auto addPt = [forceMoveTo, this](const SkPoint& pt) {
459:         if (forceMoveTo) {
460:             this->moveTo(pt);
461:         } else if (!nearly_equal(fPts.back(), pt)) {
462:             this->lineTo(pt);
463:         }
464:     };
465: 
466:     // At this point, we know that the arc is not a lone point, but startV == stopV
467:     // indicates that the sweepAngle is too small such that angles_to_unit_vectors
468:     // cannot handle it.
469:     if (startV == stopV) {
470:         SkScalar endAngle = SkDegreesToRadians(startAngle + sweepAngle);
471:         SkScalar radiusX = oval.width() / 2;
472:         SkScalar radiusY = oval.height() / 2;
473:         // We do not use SkScalar[Sin|Cos]SnapToZero here. When sin(startAngle) is 0 and sweepAngle
474:         // is very small and radius is huge, the expected behavior here is to draw a line. But
475:         // calling SkScalarSinSnapToZero will make sin(endAngle) be 0 which will then draw a dot.
476:         singlePt.set(oval.centerX() + radiusX * SkScalarCos(endAngle),
477:                      oval.centerY() + radiusY * SkScalarSin(endAngle));
478:         addPt(singlePt);
479:         return *this;
480:     }
481: 
482:     std::array<SkConic, SkConic::kMaxConicsForArc> conics;
483:     int count = build_arc_conics(oval, startV, stopV, dir, conics.data(), &singlePt);
484:     if (count) {
485:         this->incReserve(count * 2 + 1);
486:         const SkPoint& pt = conics[0].fPts[0];
487:         addPt(pt);
488:         for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
489:             this->conicTo(conics[i].fPts[1], conics[i].fPts[2], conics[i].fW);
490:         }
491:     } else {
492:         addPt(singlePt);
493:     }
494:     return *this;
495: }
496: 
497: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::rArcTo(SkPoint r, SkScalar xAxisRotate, ArcSize largeArc,
498:                                      SkPathDirection sweep, SkVector dxdy) {
499:     const SkPoint currentPoint = this->getLastPt().value_or(SkPoint{0, 0});
500:     return this->arcTo(r, xAxisRotate, largeArc, sweep, currentPoint + dxdy);
501: }
502: 
503: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::addArc(const SkRect& oval, SkScalar startAngle, SkScalar sweepAngle) {
504:     if (oval.isEmpty() || 0 == sweepAngle) {
505:         return *this;
506:     }
507: 
508:     const SkScalar kFullCircleAngle = SkIntToScalar(360);
509: 
510:     if (sweepAngle >= kFullCircleAngle || sweepAngle <= -kFullCircleAngle) {
511:         // We can treat the arc as an oval if it begins at one of our legal starting positions.
512:         // See SkPath::addOval() docs.
513:         SkScalar startOver90 = startAngle / 90.f;
514:         SkScalar startOver90I = SkScalarRoundToScalar(startOver90);
515:         SkScalar error = startOver90 - startOver90I;
516:         if (SkScalarNearlyEqual(error, 0)) {
517:             // Index 1 is at startAngle == 0.
518:             SkScalar startIndex = std::fmod(startOver90I + 1.f, 4.f);
519:             startIndex = startIndex < 0 ? startIndex + 4.f : startIndex;
520:             return this->addOval(oval, sweepAngle > 0 ? SkPathDirection::kCW : SkPathDirection::kCCW,
521:                                  (unsigned) startIndex);
522:         }
523:     }
524:     return this->arcTo(oval, startAngle, sweepAngle, true);
525: }
526: 
527: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::arcTo(SkPoint p1, SkPoint p2, SkScalar radius) {
528:     this->ensureMove();
529: 
530:     if (radius == 0) {
531:         return this->lineTo(p1);
532:     }
533: 
534:     // need to know our prev pt so we can construct tangent vectors
535:     SkPoint start = fPts.back();
536: 
537:     // need double precision for these calcs.
538:     skvx::double2 befored = normalize(skvx::double2{p1.fX - start.fX, p1.fY - start.fY});
539:     skvx::double2 afterd = normalize(skvx::double2{p2.fX - p1.fX, p2.fY - p1.fY});
540:     double cosh = dot(befored, afterd);
541:     double sinh = cross(befored, afterd);
542: 
543:     // If the previous point equals the first point, befored will be denormalized.
544:     // If the two points equal, afterd will be denormalized.
545:     // If the second point equals the first point, sinh will be zero.
546:     // In all these cases, we cannot construct an arc, so we construct a line to the first point.
547:     if (!isfinite(befored) || !isfinite(afterd) || SkScalarNearlyZero(SkDoubleToScalar(sinh))) {
548:         return this->lineTo(p1);
549:     }
550: 
551:     // safe to convert back to floats now
552:     SkScalar dist = SkScalarAbs(SkDoubleToScalar(radius * (1 - cosh) / sinh));
553:     SkScalar xx = p1.fX - dist * befored[0];
554:     SkScalar yy = p1.fY - dist * befored[1];
555: 
556:     SkVector after = SkVector::Make(afterd[0], afterd[1]);
557:     after.setLength(dist);
558:     this->lineTo(xx, yy);
559:     SkScalar weight = SkScalarSqrt(SkDoubleToScalar(SK_ScalarHalf + cosh * 0.5));
560:     return this->conicTo(p1, p1 + after, weight);
561: }
562: 
563: // This converts the SVG arc to conics.
564: // Partly adapted from Niko's code in kdelibs/kdecore/svgicons.
565: // Then transcribed from webkit/chrome's SVGPathNormalizer::decomposeArcToCubic()
566: // See also SVG implementation notes:
567: // http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/implnote.html#ArcConversionEndpointToCenter
568: // Note that arcSweep bool value is flipped from the original implementation.
569: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::arcTo(SkPoint rad, SkScalar angle, SkPathBuilder::ArcSize arcLarge,
570:                                     SkPathDirection arcSweep, SkPoint endPt) {
571:     this->ensureMove();
572: 
573:     const SkPoint srcPts[2] = { fPts.back(), endPt };
574: 
575:     // If rx = 0 or ry = 0 then this arc is treated as a straight line segment (a "lineto")
576:     // joining the endpoints.
577:     // http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/implnote.html#ArcOutOfRangeParameters
578:     if (!rad.fX || !rad.fY) {
579:         return this->lineTo(endPt);
580:     }
581:     // If the current point and target point for the arc are identical, it should be treated as a
582:     // zero length path. This ensures continuity in animations.
583:     if (srcPts[0] == srcPts[1]) {
584:         return this->lineTo(endPt);
585:     }
586:     SkScalar rx = SkScalarAbs(rad.fX);
587:     SkScalar ry = SkScalarAbs(rad.fY);
588:     SkVector midPointDistance = srcPts[0] - srcPts[1];
589:     midPointDistance *= 0.5f;
590: 
591:     SkMatrix pointTransform;
592:     pointTransform.setRotate(-angle);
593: 
594:     SkPoint transformedMidPoint = pointTransform.mapPoint(midPointDistance);
595:     SkScalar squareRx = rx * rx;
596:     SkScalar squareRy = ry * ry;
597:     SkScalar squareX = transformedMidPoint.fX * transformedMidPoint.fX;
598:     SkScalar squareY = transformedMidPoint.fY * transformedMidPoint.fY;
599: 
600:     // Check if the radii are big enough to draw the arc, scale radii if not.
601:     // http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/implnote.html#ArcCorrectionOutOfRangeRadii
602:     SkScalar radiiScale = squareX / squareRx + squareY / squareRy;
603:     if (radiiScale > 1) {
604:         radiiScale = SkScalarSqrt(radiiScale);
605:         rx *= radiiScale;
606:         ry *= radiiScale;
607:     }
608: 
609:     pointTransform.setScale(1 / rx, 1 / ry);
610:     pointTransform.preRotate(-angle);
611: 
612:     SkPoint unitPts[2];
613:     pointTransform.mapPoints(unitPts, srcPts);
614:     SkVector delta = unitPts[1] - unitPts[0];
615: 
616:     SkScalar d = delta.fX * delta.fX + delta.fY * delta.fY;
617:     SkScalar scaleFactorSquared = std::max(1 / d - 0.25f, 0.f);
618: 
619:     SkScalar scaleFactor = SkScalarSqrt(scaleFactorSquared);
620:     if ((arcSweep == SkPathDirection::kCCW) != SkToBool(arcLarge)) {  // flipped from the original implementation
621:         scaleFactor = -scaleFactor;
622:     }
623:     delta.scale(scaleFactor);
624:     SkPoint centerPoint = unitPts[0] + unitPts[1];
625:     centerPoint *= 0.5f;
626:     centerPoint.offset(-delta.fY, delta.fX);
627:     unitPts[0] -= centerPoint;
628:     unitPts[1] -= centerPoint;
629:     SkScalar theta1 = SkScalarATan2(unitPts[0].fY, unitPts[0].fX);
630:     SkScalar theta2 = SkScalarATan2(unitPts[1].fY, unitPts[1].fX);
631:     SkScalar thetaArc = theta2 - theta1;
632:     if (thetaArc < 0 && (arcSweep == SkPathDirection::kCW)) {  // arcSweep flipped from the original implementation
633:         thetaArc += SK_ScalarPI * 2;
634:     } else if (thetaArc > 0 && (arcSweep != SkPathDirection::kCW)) {  // arcSweep flipped from the original implementation
635:         thetaArc -= SK_ScalarPI * 2;
636:     }
637: 
638:     // Very tiny angles cause our subsequent math to go wonky (skbug.com/40040578)
639:     // so we do a quick check here. The precise tolerance amount is just made up.
640:     // PI/million happens to fix the bug in 9272, but a larger value is probably
641:     // ok too.
642:     if (SkScalarAbs(thetaArc) < (SK_ScalarPI / (1000 * 1000))) {
643:         return this->lineTo(endPt);
644:     }
645: 
646:     pointTransform.setRotate(angle);
647:     pointTransform.preScale(rx, ry);
648: 
649:     // the arc may be slightly bigger than 1/4 circle, so allow up to 1/3rd
650:     int segments = SkScalarCeilToInt(SkScalarAbs(thetaArc / (2 * SK_ScalarPI / 3)));
651:     SkScalar thetaWidth = thetaArc / segments;
652:     SkScalar t = SkScalarTan(0.5f * thetaWidth);
653:     if (!SkIsFinite(t)) {
654:         return *this;
655:     }
656:     SkScalar startTheta = theta1;
657:     SkScalar w = SkScalarSqrt(SK_ScalarHalf + SkScalarCos(thetaWidth) * SK_ScalarHalf);
658:     auto scalar_is_integer = [](SkScalar scalar) -> bool {
659:         return scalar == SkScalarFloorToScalar(scalar);
660:     };
661:     bool expectIntegers = SkScalarNearlyZero(SK_ScalarPI/2 - SkScalarAbs(thetaWidth)) &&
662:         scalar_is_integer(rx) && scalar_is_integer(ry) &&
663:         scalar_is_integer(endPt.fX) && scalar_is_integer(endPt.fY);
664: 
665:     for (int i = 0; i < segments; ++i) {
666:         SkScalar endTheta    = startTheta + thetaWidth,
667:                  sinEndTheta = SkScalarSinSnapToZero(endTheta),
668:                  cosEndTheta = SkScalarCosSnapToZero(endTheta);
669: 
670:         unitPts[1].set(cosEndTheta, sinEndTheta);
671:         unitPts[1] += centerPoint;
672:         unitPts[0] = unitPts[1];
673:         unitPts[0].offset(t * sinEndTheta, -t * cosEndTheta);
674:         SkPoint mapped[2];
675:         pointTransform.mapPoints(mapped, unitPts);
676:         /*
677:         Computing the arc width introduces rounding errors that cause arcs to start
678:         outside their marks. A round rect may lose convexity as a result. If the input
679:         values are on integers, place the conic on integers as well.
680:          */
681:         if (expectIntegers) {
682:             for (SkPoint& point : mapped) {
683:                 point.fX = SkScalarRoundToScalar(point.fX);
684:                 point.fY = SkScalarRoundToScalar(point.fY);
685:             }
686:         }
687:         this->conicTo(mapped[0], mapped[1], w);
688:         startTheta = endTheta;
689:     }
690: 
691:     // The final point should match the input point (by definition); replace it to
692:     // ensure that rounding errors in the above math don't cause any problems.
693:     fPts.back() = endPt;
694:     return *this;

699: SkPathIter SkPathBuilder::iter() const {

703: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::addRaw(const SkPathRaw& raw, Reserve reserve) {
704:     if (reserve == Reserve::kGrow) {
705:         this->incReserve(raw.points().size(), raw.verbs().size(), raw.conics().size());
706:     } else {
707:         fPts         .reserve_exact(Sk32_sat_add(fPts.size()         , raw.points().size()));
708:         fVerbs       .reserve_exact(Sk32_sat_add(fVerbs.size()       , raw.verbs().size()));
709:         fConicWeights.reserve_exact(Sk32_sat_add(fConicWeights.size(), raw.conics().size()));
710:     }
711: 
712:     for (auto iter = raw.iter(); auto rec = iter.next();) {
713:         const auto pts = rec->fPoints;
714:         switch (rec->fVerb) {
715:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:  this->moveTo( pts[0]); break;
716:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:  this->lineTo( pts[1]); break;
717:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:  this->quadTo( pts[1], pts[2]); break;
718:             case SkPathVerb::kConic: this->conicTo(pts[1], pts[2], rec->fConicWeight); break;
719:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic: this->cubicTo(pts[1], pts[2], pts[3]); break;
720:             case SkPathVerb::kClose: this->close(); break;
721:         }
722:     }
723: 
724:     auto has_trailing_move = [](SkSpan<const SkPathVerb> vbs) {
725:         return vbs.size() > 0 && vbs.back() == SkPathVerb::kMove;
726:     };
727: 
728:     // if the iterator 'trimmed' off a trialing move, we restore it here
729:     if (has_trailing_move(raw.verbs()) && !has_trailing_move(this->verbs())) {
730:         this->moveTo(raw.points().back());
731:     }
732: 
733:     return *this;
734: }
735: 
736: // It's tempting to just look at fSegmentMask, but we could have a degenerate path (move,close)
737: // before this, which is two verbs but still fSegmentMask == 0.
738: static bool is_empty_or_moves(const SkSpan<const SkPathVerb>& verbs) {
739:     return verbs.empty() || (verbs.size() == 1 && verbs.back() == SkPathVerb::kMove);
740: }

742: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::addRect(const SkRect& rect, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {

744: 
745:     this->addRaw(SkPathRawShapes::Rect(rect, dir, index), Reserve::kGrow);
746: 
747:     if (wasEmpty) {
748:         // now we're a rect
749:         fConvexity = SkPathDirection_ToConvexity(dir);

754: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::addOval(const SkRect& oval, SkPathDirection dir, unsigned index) {

787:     if (wasEmpty) {

881:         const size_t count = src.points().size();

884:             memcpy(newWeights, conics.data(), conics.size_bytes());

889:     SkMatrixPriv::MapPtsProc mapPtsProc = SkMatrixPriv::GetMapPtsProc(matrix);

909:                 this->lineTo(mappedPts[0]);

911:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
912:                 mapPtsProc(matrix, mappedPts, &pts[1], 2);

933: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::privateReversePathTo(const SkPath& path) {
934:     auto verbSpan = path.verbs();
935:     if (verbSpan.empty()) {
936:         return *this;
937:     }
938: 
939:     auto verbs = verbSpan.end();
940:     auto verbsBegin = verbSpan.begin();
941:     auto pts = path.points().end() - 1;
942:     auto conicWeights = path.conicWeights().end();
943: 
944:     while (verbs > verbsBegin) {
945:         SkPathVerb v = *--verbs;
946:         pts -= SkPathPriv::PtsInVerb(v);
947:         switch (v) {
948:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:
949:                 // if the path has multiple contours, stop after reversing the last
950:                 return *this;
951:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:
952:                 this->lineTo(pts[0]);
953:                 break;
954:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
955:                 this->quadTo(pts[1], pts[0]);
956:                 break;
957:             case SkPathVerb::kConic:
958:                 this->conicTo(pts[1], pts[0], *--conicWeights);
959:                 break;
960:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
961:                 this->cubicTo(pts[2], pts[1], pts[0]);
962:                 break;
963:             case SkPathVerb::kClose:
964:                 break;
965:         }
966:     }
967:     return *this;

970: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::privateReverseAddPath(const SkPath& src) {
971:     auto verbSpan = src.verbs();
972:     if (verbSpan.empty()) {
973:         return *this;
974:     }
975: 
976:     auto verbs = verbSpan.end();
977:     auto verbsBegin = verbSpan.begin();
978:     auto pts = src.points().end();
979:     auto conicWeights = src.conicWeights().end();
980: 
981:     bool needMove = true;
982:     bool needClose = false;
983:     while (verbs > verbsBegin) {
984:         SkPathVerb v = *--verbs;
985:         int n = SkPathPriv::PtsInVerb(v);
986: 
987:         if (needMove) {
988:             --pts;
989:             this->moveTo(pts->fX, pts->fY);
990:             needMove = false;
991:         }
992:         pts -= n;
993:         switch ((SkPathVerb)v) {
994:             case SkPathVerb::kMove:
995:                 if (needClose) {
996:                     this->close();
997:                     needClose = false;
998:                 }
999:                 needMove = true;
1000:                 pts += 1;   // so we see the point in "if (needMove)" above
1001:                 break;
1002:             case SkPathVerb::kLine:
1003:                 this->lineTo(pts[0]);
1004:                 break;
1005:             case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
1006:                 this->quadTo(pts[1], pts[0]);
1007:                 break;
1008:             case SkPathVerb::kConic:
1009:                 this->conicTo(pts[1], pts[0], *--conicWeights);
1010:                 break;
1011:             case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
1012:                 this->cubicTo(pts[2], pts[1], pts[0]);
1013:                 break;
1014:             case SkPathVerb::kClose:
1015:                 needClose = true;
1016:                 break;
1017:         }
1018:     }

1048: SkPathBuilder& SkPathBuilder::transform(const SkMatrix& matrix) {
1049:     if (matrix.isIdentity() || this->isEmpty()) {
1050:         return *this;
1051:     }
1052: 
1053:     if (matrix.hasPerspective()) {
1054:         SkPath src = this->detach();
1055: 
1056:         // remember this from before the detach()
1057:         this->setFillType(src.getFillType());
1058: 
1059:         SkPath clipped;
1060:         if (SkPathPriv::PerspectiveClip(src, matrix, &clipped)) {
1061:             src = std::move(clipped);
1062:         }
1063: 
1064:         for (auto [verb, pts, wt] : SkPathPriv::Iterate(src)) {
1065:             switch (verb) {
1066:                 case SkPathVerb::kMove:
1067:                     this->moveTo(pts[0]);
1068:                     break;
1069:                 case SkPathVerb::kLine:
1070:                     this->lineTo(pts[1]);
1071:                     break;
1072:                 case SkPathVerb::kQuad:
1073:                     // promote the quad to a conic
1074:                     this->conicTo(pts[1], pts[2], SkConic::TransformW(pts, SK_Scalar1, matrix));
1075:                     break;
1076:                 case SkPathVerb::kConic:
1077:                     this->conicTo(pts[1], pts[2], SkConic::TransformW(pts, wt[0], matrix));
1078:                     break;
1079:                 case SkPathVerb::kCubic:
1080:                     subdivide_cubic_to(this, pts);
1081:                     break;
1082:                 case SkPathVerb::kClose:
1083:                     this->close();
1084:                     break;
1085:             }
1086:         }
1087:     } else {
1088: 
1089:         // Can we maintain our special case shape?
1090:         if (!matrix.rectStaysRect() || !SkPathPriv::IsAxisAligned(fPts)) {
1091:             fType = SkPathIsAType::kGeneral;
1092:             // lose convexity (just to be numerically safe)
1093:             if (SkPathConvexity_IsConvex(fConvexity)) {
1094:                 fConvexity = SkPathConvexity::kUnknown;
1095:             }
1096:         }
1097: 
1098:         // If we're still a special case, check if we need to reverse our winding
1099:         if (fType == SkPathIsAType::kOval || fType == SkPathIsAType::kRRect) {
1100:             auto [dir, start] =

1102:                                              fIsA.fDirection, fIsA.fStartIndex);
1103:             fIsA.fDirection  = dir;
1104:             fIsA.fStartIndex = start;

1106: 
1107:     }
1108:     matrix.mapPoints(fPts);

pub trait RefCnt {
    fn ref_cnt_base(&self) -> &RefCntBase;

    fn ref_(&self) {
        self.ref_cnt_base().ref_();
    }

    fn unref(&self)
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        if self.ref_cnt_base().unref() {
            unsafe { self.internal_dispose() };
        }
    }

    fn unique(&self) -> bool {
        self.ref_cnt_base().unique()
    }

    fn get_ref_cnt(&self) -> i32 {
        self.ref_cnt_base().ref_cnt()
    }

    unsafe fn internal_dispose(&self)
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        unsafe {
            drop(Box::from_raw(self as *const Self as *mut Self));
        }
    }
}

/// Marker for the non-virtual reference-counted contract. It has the same
/// observable ref/unref behavior as `RefCnt`.
pub trait NVRefCnt: RefCnt {}
